The fan says no Argentina, no Brazil — only Bangladesh — and wishes the team good luck.

The fan says holding Indonesia at home without Tariq and Topu is a big achievement, but it was only a friendly and the real target is qualifying for the Asian Cup, which Zico alone cannot deliver every day.

The fan says Badsha saved Bishwanath and Rimon, praising Cabrera's decision to play him at right centre-back and his physical clearances against Irfan Jaya, and insists the in-form Rafi must play because one draw does not fix everything.
The fan says BFF cannot do it and is staging a new drama over Elita, while Indonesia give citizenship to foreign players performing well in their league, and asks when BFF will manage the same.
The fan shares an old post by Arefin Zeesan for those who claim Bangladesh has no good players, telling them to read it and Jisan's writings before saying so again.
The fan says saves like these are what have kept Bangladesh football alive and praises the goalkeeper.

The fan laments that Argentina and Brazil are brothers at the end of the day while Bengalis keep fighting, and says Bangladeshis have forgotten to support their own football, build academies and go to matches, though one day they could play the World Cup.
The fan asks whether others miss the absent players from the last match.
The post reports Yusuf Zulkarnain Haque's salary at Ipswich Town FC as £140 a week and £7,280 a year according to SalarySport, the lowest of the club's 75 listed players.
The fan jokes that Bashundhara have earned the nickname 'Biryani Kings' and hopes Fortis do not end up with 'Khichuri Fortis'.
The post is a vague one-liner, 'A normal at the office', with no clear football topic.
The fan says Zico's saves were outstanding.
The fan asks why Mahmudul Hasan left the striker position and began his football career as a left-back.
The post reports a fire at Mohammedan Sporting Club after an electrical transformer exploded nearby on Thursday night around 11:30, with two fire service units putting it out before major damage.

The fan says celebrities wear other countries' jerseys while the media stay silent and BFF never publicises matches, calls it all a syndicate, demands Salahuddin be removed to save football, and contrasts India where Sachin and Sourav promote football and new leagues appear.

Obituary for grassroots coach Akbar Ali of Satkhira, who discovered Sabina Khatun and ran the Jyoti Krida Shikkha Protisthan academy for underprivileged girls, and died of a stroke the day before receiving the Cool-BSPA grassroots coach award.

The fan questions celebrating a draw with Indonesia, noting Bangladesh drew twice with 106th-ranked India and beat 156th-ranked Maldives, and argues Indonesia are a basic team whose ranking is roughly Bangladesh's actual standard.
The post is a single word, 'Nostalgic', with no clear football topic.

The post profiles Willis Plaza, Sunil Narine's close friend, who played for Bashundhara Kings on a three-month loan in 2019 after scoring 29 goals in 35 games for Churchill Brothers and winning the I-League Golden Boot, and now plays for Aizawl FC.
The post is a one-word affectionate caption, 'Dada', with a heart-eyes emoji and no clear football topic.
The post reports the Cool-BSPA awards: Topu Barman won footballer of the year and the popular choice award, and Oscar Bruzon won coach of the year.
The fan marks one year since Tariq Kazi's national-team debut, saying it felt like Eid, and hopes Elita's debut day will feel the same even though it may never happen.

The fan mocks a local journalists' award, saying the best of the best got the winner's tag though the nominations were never published anywhere and the winner was decided before nominations were even announced.
The post reports Muktijoddha Sangsad will play a tri-nation series organised by Malaysian club Penang FC.
A rumour post says recently resigned Mohammedan head coach Sean Lane is set to join newly promoted Fortis FC.

The fan says India will surely qualify while Bangladesh's chances are doubtful without Topu, Tariq and a number nine, praises Zico's performance in the Indonesia draw, and says only on-pitch performance matters, not the names on the shirts.

The fan sarcastically notes Jack Downer beside Neymar at Aspire Academy, asking whether the academy that raised Nawab is really so low-standard and unprofessional while only the BPL and men like Salahuddin, Shohag and Murshedy are high-standard.
The fan is upset that a football tournament named after Bangabandhu has no Bangladeshi footballer on its big promotional poster.
The fan posts 'pray for Chittagong' with sad and praying emojis after the fire tragedy.
The fan suggests showing FIFA officials Bangladesh's football craze when the World Cup trophy arrives — the Brazil house and the world's biggest German flag — so they understand the passion.
The post is a fragment saying that one by one people expressed condolences over the incident, with no further detail.
The post reports Jamal Bhuiyan and his teammates praying from Malaysia for Bangladesh after the Chittagong fire tragedy.

The fan says play Bishwanath or Rimon at right-back but Badsha and Rafi must be the centre-backs, doubts Bangladesh will qualify for the Asian Cup, and warns against repeating Kings' AFC Cup pattern of winning once then collapsing.
The fan wishes the Bangladesh women's national football team all the best.
The post is only two purple heart emojis with no discernible football topic.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan asks whether injured players in the Asian Cup qualifier squad will be replaced by someone else.
The post welcomes former national footballer Md. Shaifur Rahman Moni into football coaching and wishes him success.
The post welcomes former national footballer Md. Shaifur Rahman Moni into football coaching and wishes him success.
The fan says referees would have no trouble with their honorarium if they were voters in the BFF elections.
Photo-only post, no text.

entities.name: Alamgir Kabir Rana
entities.role: national team and Bashundhara Kings midfielder

posts.summary: The birthday post for Alamgir Kabir Rana says the midfielder, who began at Badda under Maruful Haque and has not been seen since 2016, deserves another national-team chance and now runs an academy in his home district.
The post notes Bangladesh's matches in the AFC Asian Cup qualifiers begin the next day.
The fan shares something they made themselves, with only the caption 'Made by me'.
The post announces the AFC Asian Cup 2023 qualifier Bangladesh vs Bahrain the next day at 3:15 PM, live on T Sports, inviting everyone to watch.
The post is a truncated fragment about the youth and sports state minister answering journalists' questions at the National Sports Council.
The fan asks whether the players in question are not injured, in a short post about squad injuries.
The fan proudly shares 'Our Shohag United Academy' with a heart emoji.
The post is a truncated fragment noting seven FIFA officials will travel on the plane with the World Cup trophy.
Photo-only post, no text.
The post is just 'BFF' with a laughing emoji, mocking the federation.

The fan says right-back Bishu, centre-backs Rafi and Badsha and left-back Yasin would be a great combination, but instead baby Rimon will play right and Bishu in the centre, and mocks the channel's caption since Oscar is close to them.

The fan says he asked Saif's new official page how much commission a trial costs, got a reply that commission-eaters are gone, was then blocked, and saw Shahidul and Roni — accused of demanding money from Hudson — at the trials, calling Saif's management change unprofessional and its future bleak.
The fan notes the Bangladesh football community is abuzz over the Bishwanath-Rafi-Badsha selection issue.
Sheikh Russel Sports Academy beat Ilu Smriti Sangsad 5-2 with all players following the age rules, noting Ilu's players were all under 15.
The post is only hashtags promoting goalkeeper training and Bangladesh football.
The fan jokes that the World Cup is now with Salahuddin sahib.
The fan sarcastically calls Kazi Salahuddin the saviour king of football, saying the World Cup trophy is in Bangladesh to see him and will be completed by the boss's touch.
The fan jokes that the World Cup came to Dhaka itself not to see Salahuddin but to fulfil the promise he made ten years ago.
The fan jokes that the World Cup trophy is now in Dhaka to see the BFF president.
The post is only a facepalm emoji with no discernible football topic.
The fan asks in English what Biplu's job is in the team.

The fan says the players cannot even receive the ball, Rimon was beaten two or three times and was sloppy, Rimon and Bishwanath conceded fouls from bad positions, and asks how much Zico alone can handle.
The fan says that when Rimon or Bishwanath make mistakes, the commentators treat it as normal.
The fan mocks 'Kazi Mirzafaruddin' and the officials grinning for photos, asking whether they know Bangladesh are already 2-0 down at half-time.

At half-time 2-0 down, the fan says there was no passing or control except Jamal's free-kick, recalls Jamie Day's warning that this team cannot go far, and says the expatriates Mahdi Yusuf Khan, Nawab, Elita, Yusuf Zulkarnain and Rahbar have the ball control and skill Bangladesh lack.

The fan calls Salahuddin a devilish money-greedy man dragging football down, demands the BFF office be surrounded and a letter sent to the Prime Minister, with hashtags to remove Salahuddin, Murshedy and Shohag and save football.
The fan asks what Ibrahim and Biplu's job is in the national team and demands the BFF team management answer.
The fan jokes that the coach looks like Pep Guardiola but coaches like Pochettino and uses a memorised Ancelotti-style formation.
The fan jokes that the Qatar World Cup is done because the World Cup itself will come to Bangladesh, attributing the line to Kazi Salahuddin.
The fan says Bangladesh played well overall but is unhappy with Bishwanath, Rimon, Biplu and Ibrahim, and cannot understand why the fast players were given so little time.
The fan sarcastically notes Salahuddin got his chance to see his dream World Cup football and asks others to sum it up in one line.

The fan shows Cabrera's Bangladesh have played without a pure number nine, losing 2-0 to Maldives and Bahrain and drawing 0-0 with Mongolia and Indonesia, with about 90% of goals conceded in the first 45 minutes, mostly between the 30th and 45th.
The fan says it hurts that journalists still drag Argentina and Brazil into coverage when the country and the game are Bangladesh's own.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan tells 'Banglar Bajpakhi' Zico to love Bangladesh football and its players, saying they will progress like him, and wishes him well.
The fan says Zico's saves are likely what kept the goal difference down against Bahrain.
The fan praises a very good tackle in the match.
The fan says Bangladeshi players lack self-belief, get nervous before the ball arrives, and play long passes instead of passing football, asking whether they never learned back passes.
In a joking dialogue, Badsha tells Rimon to go home, Rimon replies that his 'uncles' Oscar and Cabrera told the coach to play him, and the fan says it hurts for Rafi, who is left out.

The fan notes Sunil Chhetri scored twice against Cambodia at 37 and is still indispensable to India, like Ali Ashfaq for Maldives, while Elita Kingsley at 32 was dropped as too old despite being the finisher Bangladesh lack.
The fan says India beat Cambodia on Sunil Chhetri's brace and laments that Elita could have been Bangladesh's regular goalscorer like Sunil.
The post is a one-liner reading 'like father, like son' with a laughing emoji and no clear football topic.

Recalling the 2013 World Cup trophy tour, when Emily told a FIFA official that Bangladesh had no wish to play the World Cup, the fan argues Bangladesh should target the 2030 World Cup with 48 teams instead of giving up before trying.
The fan says beating Bahrain was too much to hope for, but the shame is Bangladesh have not scored in four matches, and asks why Elita cannot be given one chance in this goal drought.
The fan says Bangladesh will badly miss their champion Rahbar Khan.
The fan contrasts Elita's exclusion with Marc Anthony Klok, who took Indonesian citizenship from the Netherlands and scored in Indonesia's win over Kuwait, asking why only Elita is a problem to play.

The post lists the first matchday results for the SAFF-region teams in the Asian Cup qualifiers — India 2-0 Cambodia, Thailand 3-0 Maldives, Jordan 2-0 Nepal, Bangladesh 0-2 Bahrain, Uzbekistan 3-0 Sri Lanka — and asks fans for their views.
The fan calls Anisur Rahman Zico 'our wall' alongside goalkeeper glove and goal emojis.

The fan calls for a protest movement, saying nothing will change without it and that with the Asian Cup qualifiers being publicised so widely, a movement now would be the biggest ever, with help from Barrister Sumon.
The fan asks what Rimon does on the pitch, saying he cannot supply a ball properly and ruins attacks with needless fouls, and wants Rafi and Badsha at centre-back with Bishwanath at right-back.

The birthday tribute to Monem Munna recalls German coach Otto Pfister saying he was mistakenly born in Bangladesh, and that the 'King Back' died aged 39 on January 26, 2005 after kidney disease and a transplant.
The fan wishes Monem Munna a happy birthday, calling him Bangladesh's greatest-ever defender.
After the June 8 Asian Cup qualifier, Bangladesh slipped one place to 189th in the updated FIFA rankings.
The fan laments that when players like these do not get a chance, there is nothing to expect from the team.

The fan's analysis of the 2-0 Bahrain loss says the scoreline flatters Bangladesh given the 99-place ranking gap, praises Zico's saves and Fahad, and calls for Rafi beside Badsha at centre-back and better ball-receiving, noting Cabrera's four matches have produced no goals.
The fan points out that 140th-ranked Ethiopia beat 36th-ranked Egypt 2-0, arguing that with willpower Bangladesh could also have beaten Bahrain.
The post is a truncated fragment about dignitaries and prominent people invited to a dinner, with no clear football topic.
The fan simply wishes Bangladesh all the best ahead of the match.

The fan proposes an attack of Robson on the left wing, Elita as centre forward and Solomon King as attacking midfielder and playmaker, saying that trio plus a local winger could score against any Asian side.
The post announces the AFC Asian Cup 2023 qualifier Bangladesh vs Turkmenistan the next day at 3:15 PM, live on T Sports, inviting everyone to watch.

Quoting Prothom Alo, the post notes Anisur Rahman Zico shows the same resolve under the posts at 5 feet 6-7 inches as Mohammad Mohsin did in the 1980s-90s, and Zico says height alone does not make a good goalkeeper.
Photo-only post, no text.

The fan corrects journalists' errors — Cabrera has played 4 matches, not more, and the 2002 Turkmenistan match was an U23 game — and tells them to ask Jitu or Arefin Zeesan before spreading wrong news.
The fan dubs an unnamed young player the Messi of the Pioneer League.
The post shares a clip or image of goalkeeper training in Bangladesh.
The fan wishes the Bangladesh team well and says they only want one win, praying from the heart that the victory will be theirs.
Photo-only post, no text.

The official match thread for Bangladesh vs Turkmenistan in the 2023 AFC Asian Cup qualification third round at Bukit Jalil, kicking off at 3:15 PM live on T Sports, with the group wall closed until full time.
The fan posts the half-time score after a brilliant first half: Bangladesh 1-1 Turkmenistan.
The fan accuses Turkmenistan of shameful time-wasting in the last 20 minutes against Bangladesh.

The fan reports Turkmenistan 2-1 Bangladesh, praising the first-half play and Cabrera's three good matches in charge, but says the attack kept missing chances and Elita is needed as a proper finisher.
The fan posts the Asian Cup qualifier full-time score Bangladesh 1-2 Turkmenistan, praising the positive play, passing and ball-snatching but blaming Rimon's clearance error for the second goal.
The fan repeats 'disappointment' and says the Turkmenistan defeat again proved how weak Bangladesh are at scoring, making the frustration worse after such good play.

The fan praises Jamal, Sajjad, Sohel, Ibrahim, Badsha, Fahad, Zico and Bishwanath in the 2-1 Turkmenistan defeat but blames Rimon's missed clearance for the second goal, laments the lack of a number nine, and says Elita, Topu, Tariq, Solomon King and Nawab could have changed the outcome.
The fan says hard luck and well played to Bangladesh despite missing plenty of chances, blaming an over-defensive second half, and notes that 70% of Malaysians supported Bangladesh.
The fan says there is no regret about losing because Jamal's team played brilliantly, though the match showed Bangladesh still need a proper number nine.
The post marks 50 years of Abahani, noting the club played its first match on this day in 1972.

The fan mocks the hype over a fighting loss to a team 50 places higher, recalling Jamie Day's bus-parking draws with Afghanistan and India, and blames the Bashundhara-Abahani syndicate's so-called positive football.
The fan calls bringing Sohel Rana on for Atiqur Rahman Fahad a suicidal decision whose consequences were felt by full time.

The post quotes a reporter's question about whether an experienced striker would have scored Bangladesh's second goal instead of newcomer Sajjad Hossain, and coach Javier Cabrera angrily dismissing it as a negative question.
The fan congratulates Bahrain on qualifying for the 2023 AFC Asian Cup from Group E, noting Malaysia missed out directly after a goalkeeper's mistake despite playing brilliantly.

The post argues the syndicate, not the coach, is Bangladesh football's main problem — Salahuddin has run the federation for over a decade with only a few draws and wins to show, and Jamie Day was removed for wanting expatriate players while the board protects itself.
The fan says this Bangladesh team could go far if the mentality changes and suggests appointing a psychiatrist for the players.
The fan jokes that the jacket in the photo looks familiar, having seen it on someone before.

The fan's post-match analysis criticises taking Fahad off, bringing Sohel Rana on, and substituting Ibrahim instead of Sajjad, arguing Jamal is better as an attacking midfielder and that Badsha's late miss recalled Elita.

The fan contrasts India's Sahal Abdul Samad, born in the UAE and trained at a modest academy there, with Aspire Academy graduate Obaidur Nawab, who is deemed unfit, and blames a Bashundhara syndicate for ruining Nawab's form.

The post reports on the Inner City World Cup 2022, where the London Tigers-led Bangladesh team beat China 2-1, then lost 5-4 on penalties to Pakistan after a 0-0 draw, with Spain winning the tournament.

The post lists the second matchday results for the SAFF-region teams in the Asian Cup qualifiers — India 2-1 Afghanistan, Uzbekistan 4-0 Maldives, Kuwait 4-1 Nepal, Bangladesh 1-2 Turkmenistan, Thailand 2-0 Sri Lanka — and asks fans for their views.

The long post laments that domestic football is losing fans amid corruption, unprofessional clubs and a lack of grounds, and argues the syndicate — not the coach — is the main problem, with Salahuddin in charge for over a decade while Jamie Day was sacked for wanting expatriate players.
The post shares an interview with Fortis FC president Shahin Hasan after the club won the Bangladesh Championship League.
The post shares the Bangladesh football team's first-half ball possession figures.
Photo-only post, no text.
The post shares an interesting story about Fortis FC coach Sk Zahidur Rahman Milon, who guided the club to the Bangladesh Championship League title.
Fortis FC footballer Hasanuzzaman Kayes, who scored a hat-trick in the Bangladesh Championship League, says he wants to stay in the Premier League.
The fan says Rakib's pace can beat any defence in Asia and his crosses are improving, but he now needs to work heavily on his finishing.
The post contrasts Sunil Chhetri, turning 38 in August, with Zahid Hasan Emily, once mentioned alongside him but now a forgotten name in Bangladesh football at just 34.
The fan says Sajjad Hossain played well but is a second striker or attacking midfielder, not a number nine, and that Bangladesh has only one true number nine — Elita Kingsley.

The fan argues Bangladesh's decade-old scoring problem persists and proposes a 4-4-2 XI with Zico, Yasin, Tariq, Topu, Rakib, Jamal, Fahad, Solomon King, Elita and Sufil, plus Hamza, Robson, Yusuf and Samit Som as the long-term fix.
After the June 11 Asian Cup qualifier, Bangladesh slipped three places to 192nd in the updated FIFA rankings, eight places from 200th.

The fan lays out the exact June 14 results Bangladesh need — Bahrain beating Turkmenistan, Bangladesh beating Malaysia 2-0, Jordan beating Kuwait and Nepal beating Indonesia — to reach the Asian Cup after 43 years.
Photo-only post, no text.
Prothom Alo Bondhushava Qatar's general secretary Abzz Rahman was selected as a volunteer for the Special Olympics World Games Berlin and received a German visa, drawing congratulations.

posts.summary: Obituary for Mahbub Ur Rahman (Tula), elder brother of Swadhin Bangla football team organiser Saidur Rahman Patel, who died of a heart attack on June 12 at National Hospital.
Photo-only post, no text.
The post breaks down Sufil's sprinting speed — 51 metres in 6.04 seconds at 30.35 km/h for his 2020 Nepal goal — and compares it with Matin Mia's 55 metres in 7 seconds against Sri Lanka in 2018.
Post announces the AFC Asian Cup 2023 qualifiers match tomorrow at 7 PM, Bangladesh versus Malaysia, to be broadcast live by T Sports.
Post says before the Malaysia match, this is their achievement, with best wishes, and asks expatriate brothers working in Malaysia to go to the field and support Bangladesh if possible.

Poetic post says writing about Jamal does not happen for him, just as reading Rudra's poems brings no thought, and compares Jamal to an unknown lover who need not be seen when in front yet is searched for endlessly when absent.

Post says Malaysia's team has two naturalised footballers, Gambian-born Mohamadou Sumareh and Brazilian Guilherme, and is about to give citizenship to Lee Tuck, while coach Cabrera gets angry hearing whether Elita Kingsley is needed in the team.
Post just tags Biplob Bhattacharjee Biplob.

Post tells the national team players they are doing very well and should change their mentality and not be afraid, since they are human and Messi is also human, and 16 crore people's eyes are on them.

Post says Jamal, Zico, Tariq, Yasin Arafat, Topu, Fahad and Rakib are Asia-level players, and argues that if the Banguras had been taken in 2015, Bangladesh would have reached the SAFF final and the Asia Cup main round, and that taking Solomon King and Elita now would bring instant results.

Post says Sheikh Mohammad Aslam played 60 matches for the national team, where Bangladesh Pratidin published 19 matches, and his official goal count is 13 or 14, though 24 goals are mentioned elsewhere.
Post says current Bangladesh national football team manager Iqbal Hossain is hopeful.
Post says 37 years at top one, and on this side our Elita Kingsley, with dashing emojis.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post says enough Brazil and Argentina, today is Bangladesh's match against Malaysia, and until we support our country's football from the heart, it cannot improve.

Post says after 14 years of effort and Salahuddin-Salam's tireless hard work, we need just eight more runs for a double century in football, and invites everyone to give these two proud legends a reception at Paltan Maidan.
Post says me analysing Bangladesh's world class passing game, with sarcasm.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post just says Bangladesh versus Turkmenistan, second half.
Post just says best of luck, with Bangladesh flags, footballs and a smiling heart emoji.

Post says Bangladesh football has enough calibre to rule South Asia, as shown against Turkmenistan, and if good expatriate players are added, Bangladesh will rule South Asia, if Salahuddin bhai has goodwill.
Post says expatriate Bangladeshi football supporters are present to support Bangladesh against hosts Malaysia, who play tonight at 7 PM.
Post says Mongolia's first potential superstar Ganbayar Ganbold scored two goals to beat Yemen, and if Mongolia can do it, Bangladesh can also beat Malaysia today, InshaAllah.
Match thread for the 2023 AFC Asian Cup qualification third round, Malaysia versus Bangladesh, kicking off at 7 PM at Bukit Jalil National Stadium in Kuala Lumpur, live on T Sports.

Post says Malaysia's build-up football looked like a 50-60 ranked team, and argues Bangladesh has even more advantage with Hamza, Samit, Farhan Ali Wahid, Rikuto Hashimoto and Max Rahman, plus Elita, Robson and Solomon King as naturalisation options, urging Salahuddin and his panel to step aside.

Post says Fahad's contribution to Bangladesh's defence was clear in the second half, while wonder boy Rimon was dancing on the field and the syndicate will never let Biplu out of the playing XI or sub him off.
Post just says 100 percent, with a clapping emoji.
Post says keep your head cool, little brother, catch them at the police station, asking whether this is the sound of the syndicate's happy family breaking apart.

Long post by Arefin Zeesan says the promising time in football will not return, as Abahani's 2019 AFC Cup points drop out of the 2025 ranking and Bangladesh will fall to 13th, while corruption and the syndicate waste the form of Matin, Sufil, Elita and Fahad.

Post says what is gone is gone and the options in hand must be used, noting Hamza Choudhury and Samit Som will play for Bangladesh only if they do not get a chance in their birthplace's team, and if Robson wants to play for Bangladesh everyone will be happy.

Long post argues the social media storm does not move Salahuddin and co. at all, TV channels and newspapers barely cover football, and quotes Barrister Sumon saying football is the property of Salahuddin and co.'s in-laws.
Post asks whether BFF failed or we failed, saying they are still tolerating Kazi Salahuddin and Salam Murshedy and could not do anything to remove them.
Post says zero percent performance, one million percent attitude, with a thumbs-up emoji.
Post says this is the world's only football team whose only tactic to get the ball to the opponent's D-box is hit with the hand, with a smiling emoji.
Post says brother, he cannot take this disappointment anymore, and he cannot stop following the country's football news either, with a sad emoji.
Post tells Uncle Oscar to please keep his nephew with him and not send him to the national team anymore, with a sleeping emoji.
Post says those who want to stay up at night crying without even being in love should love Bangladesh football, since staying up at night crying comes free with it.
Post asks if anyone can explain how Rimon Hossain's age is only 16.

Post says talking about Bangladesh football development is no longer useful, so he will enrol his children in youth academies abroad and form teams to take to the country, though if Salahuddin uncle does not leave the chair they may have to return abroad.
Post says Ramos's soul entered Jamal Bhuyan, with a fire emoji.
Post wishes happy birthday to junior Using U, saying use your talent and become established, with many best wishes, signed Jamal Bhuyan.
Post says these cries of ours will not reach the ears of those sitting on the throne, and guesses expatriates could never hold their heads high wherever they went, only bowed, with so much pain.

Post says referees demanded 5,000 taka per match in the Premier League, but the federation raised it only from 2,400 to 3,500, and referees want at least 4,500 taka plus travel and daily allowances or they will not officiate.

Post says this picture is like the sorry state of the country's football, whose makers are Salahuddin-Salam and co., with development locked inside a glass while the mafia gang plays football as they please.
Post wants to know about Muktijoddha Sangsad's Malaysia tournament and when their foreign mission is going.
Post says this time at least he will get game time.
Post says this is how Bengal's girls will move forward, with smiling, football and heart emojis.

Post asks everyone to copy the hashtags and wash BFF with them, including wewant_eleta, wewant_Nobab, wewant_mahdi, wewant_rahbar_khan, wewant_Yousuf_julkarnain, kickout_salauddin, kickout_murshedy and syndicate_out.
Post says a shameless person like him, he has not seen another in his life, with a sunglasses emoji.

Post lists SAFF countries' rankings after the Asian Cup 2023 qualifiers, showing Bangladesh at 192 while India is 88 steps ahead and even Bhutan 7 steps ahead, and notes Bangladesh has not reached a SAFF final in 17 years.

Post laments that after 43 years the team's name should have been Bangladesh, and says helpless supporters think about the country's football, dream, suffer and resolve not to watch, yet are pulled back like a magnet when Bangladesh plays.
Post says Mr. Salahuddin will also contest elections in 2024, citing Jamuna Television as the source.
Post says Samit Som is a great midfielder, skilled in every midfield position, and now he is coming in from the wing and assisting too.
Post says Zico bhai's picture says a lot, with a broken heart emoji.
Post says Robinho has expressed his desire to play for the Bangladesh national football team, asking whether BFF will respond.
Post asks whether there is any process to play foreigners before five years.
Post says since Robson has said he will play for Bangladesh, a big protest soon could get the work done, and expatriate footballers could then also play for the national team.

Post calls for a protest, demanding the expulsion of Salahuddin and Salam Murshedy and expatriate footballers in the team, including Elita, Nawab, Rahbar, Yusuf, Mahdi and Bishal Das, for a syndicate-free Bangladesh football.
Post says Bangladeshi-origin Canadian footballer Shamit Shome is trying to stop Belgium's former defender Laurent Ciman, who was in the 2014 World Cup squad and played 20 matches for Belgium.

Post says Robson Robinho has expressed interest in playing for Bangladesh, and argues BFF will not bother, so they should contact Bashundhara Kings president Imrul Hasan, who alone can arrange his citizenship.

Post says the National Football Championship final phase started at Madaripur Achmat Ali Khan Stadium, but Sylhet district team's players are struggling to survive in severe floods, with many cut off from communication.

Post explains the FIFA rules for Robson Robinho playing for Bangladesh, saying the five-year rule is no longer on paper and a passport plus a no-objection certificate would suffice, but the reason for giving the passport matters, and Kings should sign him to a five-year deal.

Post says Vietnam naturalised 27 people in 13 years and Malaysia 28 in 10 years, while BFF, which once thought of giving citizenship to Africans, still says the coach should speak first before trying for Elita.

Post says Bishal Das scored two goals and one assist in just 127 minutes in five BPL matches, averaging 1.42 goals per 90 minutes, and argues Shadhinota should give him proper playing time while fighting relegation.
Post asks whether Fortis FC will play this current BPL.
Post says Muktijoddha is not playing in that invited tournament in Malaysia.
Post asks tomorrow when the BPL match is and what time the match is.

Post says there is no stupidity like giving a reception and prizes to the syndicate national team for one win and one draw at home against a Nepal B team that lost a third of its squad to corona, even after the Asia Cup qualifiers debacle.

Long post discusses bringing Hamza Choudhury, Robson Robinho, Solomon King and Samit Som into the national team, arguing Hamza will not make England's team, Robson should be given a passport and a five-year Kings deal, and Solomon King should be given a passport quickly before a South African club takes him.

Off-topic post says the Bangladesh Rugby Federation will host a rugby series against Nepal at Army Stadium for the first time on home soil, with a 10 lakh taka budget of which 7 lakh comes from sponsor Ha-Mim Group.
Post asks on what date Bashundhara Kings' match is.

Post argues the 24-team Asia Cup is not that hard to reach, since Lebanon, Syria, Palestine, Thailand, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Vietnam, India and Indonesia all qualified while Bangladesh lost all qualifiers, and says if Topu and Tariq had not been injured and Elita and Solomon King had been picked, this team would have qualified.
Post shows a journalist's question asking who will be BFF's successor if the president retires from football, with the BFF president's answer below.
Post shares unknown facts about the 1967 RCD Cup at Bangabandhu Stadium with Iran, Pakistan and Turkey, won by Turkey, with 65,000 total attendance and 55,000 for the Turkey versus Pakistan match.
Post asks whether everyone is ready for the Dhaka derby.
Post says they said there was financial stability, but later it changed a little, and when they had nothing to pay they avoided talking.
Post asks whether Samuel Hudson is going to Fortis FC, calling it transfer rumours like Transfermarkt, and asks whether he should update all BPL player transfers this way.

Post lists Bangladesh's top five matches by stadium attendance, from the 1989 Bangladesh versus Iran match at Azadi Stadium with 60,000 to the 1989 Bangladesh versus Pakistan match in Islamabad with 40,000.
Post just says Dhaka derby, with eyes emojis.
Post quotes a T-Sports commentator saying BK Arena is undoubtedly Bangladesh's best ground, adding in brackets that there is no grass under the goalposts.
Post just tags Saqlain Chowdhury, with a cowboy-hat emoji.
Post shares a YouTube highlight of the TV show Grassroots Football and the Bangladeshi Community in the UK.
Post wishes best of luck to the Bangladesh national women's football team, with football, muscle and Bangladesh flag emojis.

Post gives stats showing Hemanta Biswas got his first goal and assist of the season in 16 matches and Mannaf Rabbi his first goal in 15, and notes Sheikh Russel's win rate rose from 13 percent under Saiful Bari Titu to 38 percent under Mintu.
Post mocks the league's 2160-pixel photo in 2022, with a hugging emoji.
Post says performer of the day Hemanta Vincent Biswas had one goal and one assist, scoring into the bottom corner from the same spot where Biplu missed in an ugly way today.
Post says captain Sabina Khatun said Bangladesh will play a match against Malaysia fulfilling everyone's expectations.
Post says thanks to Dr. Abouali for all his help, and if everything goes right, Rahbar Khan will be going through surgery on June 28th.
Post says when the picture speaks, with the Elita hashtag and a broken heart emoji.
Post says our country needs a league like this, with a heart emoji.
Post says whatever anyone says, the Dhaka derby match now has no heat anymore.

Post says BCL champions Fortis FC will play in the Bangladesh Premier League next season, having already signed England-expatriate Samuel Hudson, and wants them to bring in more expatriates like Nawab and Yusuf Zulkarnain.

Post argues 18-year-old Mehdi Hasan, who saved five penalties to win the 2018 U15 SAFF title, could have rivalled Mitul Marma if he had played regularly, and Kings should have debuted him in the BPL by now.

Post says Fortis FC will get a big fan base in the BPL next season since Samuel Hudson, Joseph Nur and Saklayen Chowdhury play there, and if they pull Yusuf Zulkarnain and Max Rahman, next season will be Fortis time.
Post says dreams teach people to live and football tries to keep that dream alive, with many best wishes for Mong Marma Athui.
Post says official photographers using devices on the field could pass information to gamblers, recalling the Arambagh incident, and asks when the federation will act or bring them under the law.
Sarcastic post says the whole nation will be grateful to Mr. Salahuddin for bringing the 2022 Qatar World Cup trophy to Bangladesh.
Post asks readers to share the good news of the talented young footballers in their area.
Post says under the new manager, Adib and Nabil Rahim are on the bench, and something is going on.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post says Mohammedan played wonderful passing football, scoring a wonderful goal after 23 passes against eternal rivals Abahani.
Post says Abahani's social media handle is far better than Bashundhara's, since having money is not enough, it is a matter of taste.
Post just asks how much would you give out of 10.
Post just gives the score, Dhaka Abahani 4, Mohammedan 2.
Post says Cumilla's football lovers saw a total of six goals in the Dhaka derby.
Post says Shahriar Emon is the best talent in Bangladesh football in his view, a pure example of a box-to-box midfielder who should be taken into the national team immediately.
Post asks whether Saklayen Chowdhury is playing in today's Bangladesh Police FC versus Uttara Baridhara match.
Post says Mahfuza asked more spectators to come to the field and buy tickets for the women's match to help flood victims, with tickets at 50 taka and 10,000 printed by BFF in the first phase.
Post says Mohammedan played well against a strong team like Abahani with two fewer foreigners, and hopes they will turn around from the next match.

Post says he met Bangladesh football legend and Mohammedan legend Rumman Bin Wali Sabbir at Cumilla Stadium, who came to support Dhaka Mohammedan in the Dhaka derby and was its superstar, surpassing Rafael and Colindres.
Post asks why the Bangabandhu National Championship is held and what benefit Bangladesh football gets from it, with ready-made 25-26-year-old players who play neighbourhood khap matches.

Post suggests Fortis FC, which wants to bring players from its academy into the main team, should sign four quality expatriate footballers instead of four foreigners, benefiting both the club and the national team.

Post laments that the old Dhaka derby atmosphere is gone, with no supporters' boundless joy and Bangladesh no longer splitting into two, yet says the match is still their most awaited and congratulates dear team Abahani Limited.
Post announces Bangladesh versus Malaysia today at 6 PM, to be broadcast live by T Sports.

Post lists several rising young U-20 talents who played this BCL for Fortis FC, including 19-year-old goalkeeper Ishaque Akondo and defender Prakas Das, who played in the BPL for Brothers Union, and wishes them well.
Post just says goalkeeper, with Bangladesh flags and hearts.

Post says former Jessore district women's footballer Muslima Akter Moly, after completing the BFF-FAC goalkeeping Level-1 course, became the country's first woman goalkeeper coach, dreaming of one day coaching the national team.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post asks whether the inhuman Salahuddin does not see all this.
Post just says queen.
Post just says there is logic in what he says.
Post just asks offside.
Post says if Soccerway's information is not wrong, Muktijoddha lead 1-0 thanks to Nawab's goal.
Post says in the 43rd minute of today's match, Obaidul Rahman Nawab scored a goal.
Post says Bangladesh slipped four steps to 192 in the rankings.
Post says Kazi Sala Uddin's BFF is waiting for a double century, and he goes around saying becoming Asia's best team is his main goal, for which 450 crore taka is needed.
Post says not satisfied with just taking away the captaincy, the tyrant Saif has sent Jamal to Muktijoddha.
Post says best moments of the day, Saif Sporting Club Ltd versus Chittagong Abahani Ltd.
Post says star of the day Mohammad, Fahim and JR, with two goals and two assists.
Post says for a federation to be destroyed, one horrible president, sleeping supporters and some perverted journalists are enough.

Post says Nawab got his first assist on 25/04/2022 and first goal on 23/06/2022, coach Raja Isa rightly recognised the Aspire Academy product, and Nawab took a step forward in saving Muktijoddha from relegation.
Post says Mohammedan midfielder Shahed Hossain's goal was cancelled due to the referee's wrong decision.
Post quotes Kazi Salahuddin saying Liechtenstein, a European country, being below Bangladesh is the biggest achievement of his president career, with a note that something remains to be said.
Post says more and more friendlies should be arranged with teams ranked 70-100, then the ranking will jump quickly.

Post compares minutes and returns of Shadhinota's Bishal Das, Muktijoddha's Nawab and Kings' Mahdi, noting Bishal got only 76 minutes out of a possible 270 in Shadhinota's next three matches despite scoring against Mohammedan.
Post says Ankhi scored a brace.
Post says Bangladesh national team's recently departed former coach Jamie Day has joined England fourth-tier club Swindon Town FC as assistant coach.
Post says Faisal Ahmed Fahim's performance yesterday was two goals, one assist and one penalty won.

Post argues if Ben Garner and Scott Marshall could move from Swindon Town's staff to third-tier jobs, Jamie Day is not to be mocked for becoming assistant coach in the English fourth tier, which is still ahead of the BPL.
Post just says goalkeeper training in Asia.

Post uses market values to show the BPL is far below the English fourth tier, arguing Jamie Day went to a better league and position, and notes Bangladesh lost 1-0 to Qatar second-division Lusail SC in 2020.
Post says this one Super League has badly damaged their football, leaving them the 104th-ranked team, and it only makes him feel sorry.
Post says club teammate Dorielton Gomez was gifted his national team jersey by Tutul Hossain Badsha, with a heart emoji.
Post says Nawab's first goal.

Post says Kolkata giants Mohun Bagan signed Paul Pogba's elder brother Florentin Pogba for two years and brought Brandon Hamill from Australia after Tiri's ligament injury, leaving Bangladeshi clubs like Bashundhara and Abahani far behind.
Post lists Federation Cup facts from 1980 onwards, including the joint champions in 1980 and 1982, the six editions not held, and the first final tie-breaker in 1991.
Post just says Sabina Khatun apu, with football, goal and star-struck emojis.
Post asks why Pioneer League matches are played on such a bad field.
Post says memories, the broadcasting was just wow, but now the broadcast is not nice, with a sad emoji.
Post asks whether anyone knows anything about this expatriate girl footballer, who plays well, and why she is not taken into the Bangladesh women's team.
Post says Bangladesh football officials should be ashamed, since even neighbouring Myanmar, a weak economy, has good-quality stadiums and probably a better-quality league than Bangladesh's.
Post says thank you Golam Choton.

Post lists several young U20 footballers playing for Azimpur FC Uttara in the BCL, including 16-year-old goalkeeper Anik Ahmed and defender Uttam Chandra Roy, who also played for Brothers Union and the U16 and U19 teams.
Post is only a Facebook link, with no text of its own.
Post calls Bishwanath Ghosh the world number one defender, Sir Sergio Birgil Bishwanath Ramos Ghosh.
Post mocks the commentator who said Bashundhara Kings lead 2-1 against SRK, clarifying it is not Shah Rukh Khan but Sheikh Russel.
Post just says three years ago on this day.
Post just says Banglar Ronaldo, Bengal's Ronaldo.
Post just asks close enough.
Post says Bangladesh's girls brought home the title of the Bangladesh-Malaysia FIFA friendly series, with a Bangladesh flag emoji.

Long post argues the earlier players like Salahuddin, Salam, Aslam, Munna, Kanchon and Alfaz were better and could have taken Bangladesh to a 48-team World Cup, while today's players are fairly good and adding Solomon King, Elita and Hamza would bring results, though the former stars now lead the syndicate.
Post says it is 100 percent tactical failure, a foreign coach is needed, and Golam Rabbani Choton is a good coach in age-level teams and should stay there.

Post analyses the relegation fight, saying Rahmatganj has the easiest remaining schedule while Shadhinota's relegation is confirmed and Muktijoddha, despite bringing Nawab, Mithu and Sudi in the mid-transfer, should also be relegated.
Post says he has a Nokia E72 phone and will give it to BFF for free, since better photos will come out of it than this.

entities.name: Hill-tracts football fans group of Bangladesh

posts.summary: Long post from the Hill-tracts football fans group says talented young footballers in the hill districts cannot afford trials, boots or jerseys and are blocked by dishonest local leaders, and urges them not to give up, with a photo of Bandarban District Football Stadium.

Post says he is 23, practised for six months two years ago as an attacking midfielder, and asks for advice on whether he can go far if he starts playing again and which club's trial might give him a chance.

Post says Mohammedan's quality social media account was closed within two months, leaving only Dhaka Abahani, Bashundhara Kings and Chittagong Abahani with quality official accounts, and argues the sector still does not understand marketing and fan engagement.

Post asks whether guru Oscar watched Mursalin's game today, since he kept him on the side bench in the first leg, and says Kings management should pay attention to loaned players when selecting next season's team.

Post says apart from Robson, no foreign player is worth learning from, suggests all clubs together bring a foreign goalkeeper to learn from, and argues spectators should be lured with gifts since Salahuddin has been around since childhood yet football has not progressed.
Post says after being unbeaten against Mohammedan for the last three years, today they lost to Sheikh Morsalin's team.
Post asks how many clubs will play in the AFC Cup from Bangladesh in 2023.
Post says Mohammedan got their first win under new coach Shafiqul Islam Manik, beating Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi 3-1 at Cumilla Shahid Dhirendranath Dutta Stadium.
Post says he is only 16, Morsalin, with a raised hands emoji.
Post says well done Mursalin.
Post says well done Mursalin.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post asks whether Kiran is really worthy of the credit Sabuj bhai gave him, with an eyes emoji.
Post says these teams have one owner, with a smiling emoji.

Post says last season's third-division top scorer Morsalin signed with Bashundhara Kings, could not find playing time there, and on loan at Mohammedan caught everyone's eye on debut against Abahani before scoring a wonderful goal against Sheikh Jamal.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post says the greatest joy in the world is right here, with smiling and kissing emojis.
Post says so far Jalal is refereeing well, except for some decisions.
Post says Sheikh Jamal sacked Juan Manuel despite 5 wins and 6 draws in 11 unbeaten matches, while Afusi has 3 wins and 3 defeats in 6, and argues Juan is 1000 percent better than Afusi.
Post quotes referee Jaya Chakma saying if she gets the chance she wants to officiate in the Premier League too, and would be happy if she could officiate an Abahani-Mohammedan match at least once.

Post accuses referee Jalal of playing for Dhaka Abahani, showing Candy a card while Royel's slap went unpunished, and says Abahani and Bashundhara Kings have increased the burden of sin in domestic football so much that fans do not feel like supporting them in the AFC Cup.
Post asks whether the Sheikh Kamal Club Cup has been lost, with thinking emojis.
Post asks if any brother from Khulna or anyone who plays in a club is there, asking them to reply in the comments.

Long post argues Hamza Choudhury and Samit Som can still play for Bangladesh on paper, since Hamza never debuted for England and Samit's Canada appearance was only a friendly, and urges calling Max Rahman for the AFC U20 qualifiers to get his debut done.
Post says Ratul left his 50-taka day-labourer job for football.
Post says he watched the two Abahani match at a tea shop yesterday, the first time he has seen a Bangladesh league match at a tea shop.
Post says with this defeat, the relegation fear hanging over Muktijoddha has increased further.
Post says this nation will suffer and this country's football will keep suffering, as a linesman not calling an incident a few yards in front of him ruins a match's momentum.
Post says Rahbar Kahn's surgery went well, now it is time to rehab and relax, thanking everyone for all the support.
Photo-only post, no text.
Post recalls Bangladesh's historic 3-0 win against Pakistan in 2011, with a heart emoji.
Post says Bangladesh national football team player Ritu Porna Chakma's younger brother Parbon Chakma, only 16, passed away today in a sudden electrocution accident, and they are stunned by his death.
Post asks whether Obaidur Rahman Nawab was in the XI today and whether Saklayen Chowdhury has debuted for Bangladesh Police FC.
Post says in today's Kaler Kantho newspaper.
Post asks whether the five-year deal with Qatar is only in words or BFF has actually implemented it, linking a news report.
Post says Mohammedan's next match is against Bashundhara Kings, hoping Morsalin's performance will force Bashundhara to wonder why they kept this boy on the bench for so long.

Long article by Sanat Babla argues money is the ruin of football, as clubs spend crores on transfer fees of 80-90 lakh without performance while local players are overshadowed by foreigners and the league produces no players for the national team.

Post says ATK Mohun Bagan holds trials for U13, U15 and U18 teams while BFF, stuck in the so-called golden past, only talks big about an U18 league, though Fortis deserves thanks for building an academy.
Post says Salahuddin does not even have the money to send a U-13 team abroad, while he fills his own pocket from various sectors.
The fan simply posts 'Goalkeeper training in Asia'.
The fan agrees with a brother, laughing at the Bengali Facebook audience.
The fan asks whether the BPL is happening and requests the updated fixture if so.

The fan shares the last five matches' statistics between Bashundhara and Mohammedan, hopes Mohammedan do well tomorrow, and says a win seems almost impossible but if they lose he wants them to lose playing well.
The off-topic post notes Pakistan are returning to international football after a 15-month FIFA ban and can take part in all forms of football, so SAFF tournaments will regain some colour.
The post invites teams that want to take part to contact the organisers, Sohag United Academy.
The post previews today's second-leg BPL match between table-toppers Bashundhara Kings and Mohammedan, live from 4pm at Comilla's Shaheed Dhirendranath Dutta Stadium on T Sports and T Sports Digital.
The fan is dismayed that Biplu is in the XI again today after such a bad performance last match, and that Fahad may be played at centre-back by the greatest of all time Bangladeshi club coach.

The fan calls an unnamed boy fire, praising his beautiful body language, passing and shooting and the curvy goal he scored today, and says Bangladesh has more such talents needing only care and opportunity.
The fan notes the assistant referee ruled a goal out in response to Matin Mia's appeal, joking that he forgot the match is being shown on TV.
The fan simply notes that the referee raised his flag.
The fan asks whether Sheikh Mursalin is the wonder kid of Bangladesh.
The fan celebrates 16-year-old Morsalin scoring an extraordinary goal for Mohammedan.
The fan mocks Lord Jony's lord-like behaviour.
The post is only raised-hands emojis with no discernible football topic.
The fan calls a player Bengal's Roberto Carlos.
The fan contrasts HERO of the Day and ZERO of the Day in the same picture.
The post invites those who want to take part in the tournament to contact the organisers at Keraniganj Atibazar, Dhaka, organised by Sohag United Academy.
The fan says he will not troll today and only asks Imrul Hasan one question: which picture is more pure, beautiful and peaceful?
The fan says there is no time for introductions and tells others to ask their Oscar father who Morsalin is.

The fan calls Bashundhara the birthplace of destroying talented footballers, saying they give no chance to new players but play match after match the national team's third-grade makal footballers in the name of experience.
The fan notes one man's power spans the whole of SAFF, as SAFF president from 2009 to 2026, yet under him the SAFF region has completely failed except India, who plan for the Asian level instead.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan wishes Bangladesh football to move forward through Morsalin and his peers.

A Kings fan says Bashundhara Kings alone will destroy Bangladesh football, criticising the lack of build-up play, XI places decided by mama-khalu connections rather than merit under low-quality coaches like Oscar Bruzon, and the poor AFC Cup showing, while defending the biryani-for-fans practice and blaming management rather than the whole club.

The fan notes Saibur Rahman Morsalin came to Mohammedan on loan from Bashundhara in the second leg, played three matches in the black-and-white jersey and scored two excellent goals including the one against Kings, the best local goal in the Premier League.

The fan expects BFF to pick the Algeria U-13 tournament squad from the BFF Elite Academy, which had six U-13 players in this season's BCL, and says one young academy player caught his eye on stats alone and he hopes the boy becomes like Sheikh Morsalin.
The fan says if they are not given encouragement with jashri they will not watch any more games.

The fan asks why a Mohammedan goal against Bashundhara was disallowed, noting T Sports stopped broadcasting at 75 minutes for a mechanical fault, a Google notification then said Mohammedan scored, yet the match ended 1-1.
Photo-only post, no text.

The fan complains Chittagong Abahani vs Sheikh Jamal is shown on YouTube in good quality 1080p, while Saif Sporting vs Abahani Ltd is shown in 720p with a shaky camera and the game freezing on screen on TV and YouTube.
The fan mocks the royal BPL, saying even Juventus footballers have to pull the stretcher there.

The fan says Sheikh Jamal's Naim is Zico's perfect and solid backup and competitor, a consistent performer and penalty specialist who is now the national team's second choice and should be played in upcoming friendlies, while Sheikh Jamal should play him permanently and release Mitul Marma.

Comparing two photos months apart, the fan recalls goalkeeper Shahidul Sohel inciting Abahani supporters against Saif supporters in the Federation Cup, with Saif jerseys stripped and flags torn, and says Sohel single-handedly knocked Abahani out of the title race today, calling him Flight Lieutenant Sohel alias Ostrich.
The fan simply says they are watching and that others are watching too, with no discernible football topic.

The fan notes under Maruful Haque Chittagong Abahani lost three straight matches for the first time, at home, along with four straight defeats against Sheikh Jamal, and dreads the next match against Bashundhara whom they lost 5-0 to in the first round.
Photo-only post, no text.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan laments the same Colindres, the same shot and the same crossbar, calling him unlucky.
The fan says seeing Shahriar Emon and Morsalin's playing styles cannot fail to mesmerise, calling both like chillies and praising Emon's footwork as a treat for the eyes.

The fan calls Morsalin's goal against Bashundhara truly astonishing and rare from a local, notes Morsalin is Mohammedan's auto choice on loan from Kings who would not even bench him, calls Kings' team selection horrendous, and wants Elita, Nawab and Mahadi to change clubs, ideally to Fortis.
The fan defends Zico against criticism for a goal, saying those critics should look closely at the goal's initial direction, since it was of unbelievable quality and poor Zico had nothing to do.
The fan simply cheers Sufil with heart and football emojis.

The fan contrasts local and expatriate players, praising Rakib, Sajjad, Topu, Jamal's passing and Tariq Kazi but criticising the weak finishing and passing, and says Rahbar's skill alone is ten times any national player while Nawab, Mahdi, Saklayen, Yusuf and Elita are far better than Biplu, Jony, Fahad and Suman.

The fan says they watched 45 minutes of Rahmatganj vs Muktijoddha just to see how Nawab plays, calls him a good playmaker who can make things happen, and wonders why he is not getting a chance in the Bangladesh national team.
The fan says if Nawab has even a little sense in his head he will not go back to Kings, and should play for the league's worst team if needed.
The fan shares some stats of the Bangladesh U-12 and U-13 teams, apologising in advance for any mistakes in collecting them.
Quoting the satirical Daily Syndicate's Alo, the fan says Nawab's goal invited danger and drowned Muktijoddha in the shame of being served seven-up.

The fan says Oscar Bruzon's so-called academy player Nawab has two goals and one assist in six matches while world-class Biplu has no goal in this BPL, and calls each Nawab and Morsalin goal a shoe-slap in Oscar's face.
The fan tells others to ask Roxy grandpa who Nawab is, saying there is no time for introductions.

The fan argues Kingsley, Nawab and Morsalin should skip Kings next season for clubs where they get game time, with Kingsley going to Sheikh Russel, Nawab to Fortis and Morsalin staying at Mohammedan, and asks Kings to release them for a season while bringing in new expatriates like Samit Som.
The fan asks which goal others think is the best.

The long post praises the BFF Elite Academy's training but says academies should start at age seven or eight, doubts BFF's two new academies will last given past failures, notes the Pioneer League is shrinking and the Sohrawardi Cup is gone, and calls for collecting village and hill talents like Sushanta Tripura and Mitul Marma.

A rumour says Qatar-based Obaidur Rahman Nawab is leaving Bashundhara Kings to join Abahani Ltd, with talks quite advanced and an official announcement possible with one or two league matches left, mainly to get enough playing time.

The post quotes an unnamed speaker saying expatriate footballers are looked at crookedly and treated as if they have no guardian, with many feeling they should not be allowed to play here even though they are Bengali players.

The fan asks Fortis FC to sign Hudson, Max Rahman and Mitul Marma next season and play them to build a fan base, says Nawab joining Abahani would be good, and says Morsalin should stay at Mohammedan and prove himself before deciding.
The post warns to beware of fraudsters.
The post warns to beware of fraudsters.
The fan simply posts 'Tough competition.'
The fan says Saif Doha brightened Faridpur's face by being selected the country's best referee, after years without success for Faridpur district sports.

Abul Hossain shares his dream for his son, seen playing in Comilla: he wants the boy to become a big footballer, play regularly for Mohammedan, then earn a national team chance on merit, though he doubts how long the boy can stick with it.
The fan lists three reasons for no spectators in Bangladesh football: no clubs named after regions or places, syndicate or nepotism, and bad refereeing.
The fan wants two changes — Sheikh Russel Faridpur FC and Sheikh Jamal Barishal FC — so football's popularity grows with home-venue matches.
The fan simply posts 'Bangladesh Premier League' with football and fire emojis.

The fan defends Jamie Day as the best coach, recalling his prediction that this team could improve only two or three steps, his bringing in Tariq Kazi, Rahbar Khan, Nawab and Yusuf Zulkarnain, and his sacking by Salahuddin for wanting expatriates, while the syndicate still runs team selection and Cabrera has no power.
The post reports Mahmudul Hasan Kiron is leaving Rahmatganj to join Abahani Ltd, as Abahani rebuild to win the league title next season, and asks how the signing will be.

The fan imagines Brazilian Robson and English star Hamza Choudhury joining the national team, argues expatriates should earn places by performance like France's six or seven expatriates, and blames Salahuddin and Salam Murshedy for blocking expatriates while BFF pockets money that could have bought Asian Cup and 2026 World Cup qualification.
The fan asks whether paid fans are not ashamed to be called fans, and whether they are really fans at all.

The birthday post for Alfaz Ahmed calls him one of Bangladesh's best strikers and perhaps its luckiest, noting he played 105 national matches from 1995 to 2008, scored 16 goals, and was voted Asia's best footballer in August 1996, a honour no other Bangladeshi has had.
The fan notes the players pictured are from England and Spain but will play for Ghana at the Qatar World Cup, and laments that Bangladesh could not even play one Elita Kingsley.

The second birthday tribute to Alfaz Ahmed recalls his 105 matches and 16 goals, his club career at Abahani, Mohammedan, Brothers Union and Sheikh Russel, and his winning goal against Nepal in the 1999 SAF Games final at Dasharath Stadium that gave Bangladesh its first SAFF title.
The post reports defender Atiquzzaman left Sheikh Jamal to join Bashundhara Kings, with an official announcement coming soon.
Photo-only post, no text.

The fan says Bashundhara have bought football so they can punch whoever they want, points to Sohel, Bishwanath and Khaled's over-aggressiveness, and calls T Sports' two commentators brokers for halal-ising a clear two-footed foul as Shafi definitely getting the ball.
The post is only the hashtag Oc with no discernible football topic.
The fan threatens that Don Khaled will varnish anyone who comes to the neighbourhood and let them go.
The fan says Black Panther clearly told haters he does not listen to criticism at all and roars on the pitch instead.

The fan notes Chittagong Abahani last lost four league matches in a row in 2014-15, the season before Tarafder Ruhul Amin started building the team, so this is the first four straight losses of the Saif Powertec era.

The fan says a champion girl from a marginal area wants to play football alongside her studies, and if talented girls like Mrabui Marma get support and the right position, the women's football pipeline will become strong.
The fan says Rocky's pain from two broken teeth was covered by winning two trophies.

The fan says thieves steal in broad daylight and asks whether they have come to the football field for business, demanding corruption-free football and thanking Sadman Sakib for a timely report unmasking the thieves.

The fan argues Zico's record would have been nearly impossible at any club but Kings, that foreigners rule the defence, midfield and attack while locals only fill the rules, and that Fortis' academy focus offers hope if they do not later disappoint like Kings.
The fan asks whether O.R Nawbab is really talking to Abahani and wants the latest authentic update on Nawab's club transfer, saying a rumour without a source will not do.

A rumour says BPL clubs have their eyes on Benapole Secondary School captain Rahul and Nilphamari Chhamir Uddin School captain Naim, with some clubs already contacting them, citing a Dhaka Tribune report.
The fan says Colindres repeated against Saif Sporting Club his famous shot from the 2018 World Cup that shook the bar.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan shares a goalkeeper post for Bangladesh with camera emojis.
The fan says they came to Comilla not to flatter Bashundhara Kings but to flatter Imrul bhai, their beloved Imrul.

The fan asks how far the work on the FIFA-standard world-class stadium in Purbachal has progressed, worries Bangabandhu Stadium's slow renovation may not finish before next season, and asks how far the Sheikh Russel mini stadium and mini academy in each of the roughly 500 upazilas have come.
The fan scoffs at those hoping the coach will play Elita in place of Nuha.

The long rant against Salahuddin and Murshedy says the man who gave himself an A-plus in football development holds all football hostage, questions where FIFA's ten crore a year and the sports ministry's hundreds of crores go when BFF has built no turf ground or live broadcasts, and calls for boycotting both men and human chains at Ganabhaban or the sports ministry.

The fan wants the Mahdi Khan who lit up Kings Arena's inaugural match, saying Kings benched him and forgot that fiery performance, while loaning Nawab was like shooting themselves in the foot since Raja Isa used him properly at Muktijoddha and proved he is no academy-level player.

The Pioneer Football League ended with Barishal Football Academy beating Zara Green Voice Football Academy 4-3 on penalties in the final at Bashundhara Kings Arena, after a two-and-a-half-month, 46-team league.

The fan asks whether there is a syndicate even in age-level team selection, noting three young Muktijoddha players who played BPL matches as substitutes were not called for U-20 trials while players from other clubs who never played a BPL match were, and calls it unfair.
Photo-only post, no text.

The meme announces breaking news that Ronaldo has signed for Bashundhara Kings after they got a Champions League chance, with a contract offer of 21,000 taka a month, 20 kg of atap rice and two poa of coriander leaves.
The fan mocks 'President Salauddin' with laughing emojis.
The fan says they are mesmerised by this gentleman's play again and again, without naming him.

The fan recalls last year's viral night final of a school football tournament and describes the BBFC friendly tournament at Bindubasini Govt Boys High School in Tangail, with promo videos, a concert inauguration, Ballon d'Or-style awards and live talk shows, as more transparent and spectacular than any professional tournament.
The fan posts only the hashtag Rumours.
The fan simply posts 'dream Bangladesh'.
