The fan praises Nawab and Sudi Abdullah's understanding and position sense in the few matches they played together at Muktijoddha to save the club from relegation, and says they should pick clubs next season that give them regular chances.
The fan simply posts 'Mohammedan Sporting Club' with black and white heart emojis.
The fan compares the Nawab-Sudi Abdullah pair with the Robson-Jonathan pair, saying one pair saved a team from relegation and the other made a team champions, and that is the only difference.
The fan asks which teams will participate in the Indo-Bangla football tournament.

The fan reports Obaidur Nawab scored 3 goals and 3 assists in just 10 games for Muktijoddha under Raja Isa, one goal contribution fewer than Rakib Hossain despite half a season, and argues he should stay at Muktijoddha rather than join linked clubs Abahani, Sheikh Russel or Fortis FC.
The fan hopes Nawab and Sudi Abdullah will get even better teams next season.
The fan says Nepal fans' excesses may now reduce a bit.
The fan says Nawab, who was fading at Bashundhara for lack of playing time, is returning to his true form.
The fan wants to know which team Nawab will play for next season.

The fan argues the AFC should fix member countries' domestic calendars like UEFA does and BFF should follow it fully, with club licensing enforced and leagues finished within a set eight months so SAFF tournaments and invitational cups like the Bangabandhu Gold Cup can be scheduled.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan says an unnamed player proved himself again and hopes to see him in the national team very soon.
The fan claims that if Biplu had been in Nawab's place today he would have scored ten goals, that Biplu is far better than Nawab, and that Biplu played brilliantly all season.
The fan says that with proper care, grooming and enough game time, Nawab will one day rule football like a nawab.
The fan says if an unfit player with a torn ligament can still score goals and assists and win matches to end the season, then that torn-ligament player is the better one for them.
The fan jokes about being bored watching Bangladesh play Zimbabwe in cricket and invites others to read the post's comments and laugh.
The post notes Paul Pogba's brother is set to play for neighbouring country's ATK Mohun Bagan.
Robson Robinho says he wants to become Mohammad Robson and has lately been expressing his wish to settle permanently in Bangladesh in various ways.

The devoted Kings fan sarcastically says Zico, Sabuj and Ibrahim's personal photographer, actually the Bashundhara Kings Facebook page admin-cum-photographer, is on honeymoon, so there are no photo updates of the hat-trick champions, and asks fans to be patient until he returns.
The fan simply posts Dorielton with star-struck emojis.

Copying Salim Saad, the fan says Saif Sporting Club's bluster is over, and on the feet of Bengal's Nawab, Muktijoddha survived relegation, wondering how big a coach Oscar is to keep such a talented player on the side bench, with the full-time result Muktijoddha 3-2 Saif.
The fan asks for details about this tournament.
The fan asks what the news of Brothers Union is, whether Arambagh, Farashganj, Wanderers, NoFeL and Beanibazar have disappeared, and says BFF should keep a little track of them.
The fan asks who that coach is.
The fan asks how Tetsuaki Misawa and Soma Otani played in your eyes, and asks readers to follow his page.
The fan says a tournament should be organised every year with the BPL, BCL, Independence Cup and Federation Cup champion teams.

The fan says Shamsul Huda Football Academy in Jessore is among the first names among first-tier academies, supplying players to Dhaka football, the national team and top clubs, and wishes its head coach Kazi Maruf a happy birthday.

The fan praises Nawab's ball control, passing, receiving, dribbling and through passes, calls the mid trio of Fahad as defensive mid, Jamal as central attacking mid and Nawab as second striker one of South Asia's best, and says classless players like Biplu and Jony must be removed and Nawab must be called to the next national camp, having shown only 30 to 40 percent of his calibre.

The fan says Tareq Miah had a big role alongside Nawab and Sudi in saving Muktijoddha from relegation, and in earning 12 points in the second leg without a foreign defender, playing 20 matches and missing two to cards, and we will see him at a new club next season.

entities.name: Bangladesh India Friendship North Bengal International Gold Cup

posts.summary: The fan explains the Bangladesh India Friendship North Bengal International Gold Cup 2022, organised by FC Uttar Bongo, has only had its logo unveiled in Rangpur by Major General Abdur Rashid, CBIF chairman Shubhashish Samaddar and club president Azizur Rahman Dulu, and the participating teams have not been announced yet.
The fan requests the group admins not to approve any shared post for the next month, saying he is tired of seeing shared posts, unless something important comes up.

The fan reports former national team Argentine coach Andres Cruciani's third stint in Bangladesh ended on Sunday, as his contract ended with Saif's last Premier League match, and he is said not keen to continue with Saif while the club is also not very keen to keep him.
The fan notes the AFC Cup is returning to the home-and-away system from next season, and for two straight editions Bashundhara Kings and Bangladeshi clubs were deprived of the home advantage.

The fan reports former U-19 captain Fahim Morshed hinted at a new destination after leaving Bashundhara, quoting his Facebook post thanking the Kings after three years of world-class training, facilities and player protection and saying the time has come for a new challenge.

The fan says an identified match-fixing syndicate has brought the country's football to the verge of ruin over the last 15 or 20 years, and though the BCL also saw a festival of fixing this season and BFF's match-fixing identification committee first stirred then went silent, the syndicate's roots must be uprooted with harsh lifetime bans.
The fan says sixteen annas correct, citing Navil Khan as the source.

The fan says Tareq Miah had a big role alongside Nawab and Sudi in saving Muktijoddha from relegation, and in earning 12 points in the second leg without a foreign defender, playing 20 matches and missing two to cards, and wishes him luck at a new club next season.

The fan announces Mohammedan Sporting Club's last 2021-22 Premier League match today at Comilla Stadium against old Dhaka's Rahmatganj Muslim Friends Society, live on T Sports at 4pm, and wishes Mohammedan well next season.

The fan says if Yusuf, Morsalin, Rimon and Yasin had been sent to India with the U-20 team, the team would have been stronger, the title could have been hoped for, and they would also have been prepared for the national team.

The fan lists traditional football clubs about to disappear from the country's football, including Brothers Union, Arambagh, Team BJMC, Feni Soccer, Farashganj, Wanderers, Chittagong Mohammedan, Khulna Abahani, Cox City FC, NoFeL, Wari, Fakirerpool Youngmens, Victoria and Dhanmondi Club, and asks about their current state.
The fan sends best wishes to Fahim and tells others to keep their eyes on Navil Khan for local transfer deals.

The fan sarcastically repeats the claim that Nawab could not survive in Qatar so he came to Bangladesh, and by mistake scored three goals and three assists in ten matches, saying his temper is ruined by the picture and asking commenters to write two lines about the person.
The fan says he tried to make this season's best XI considering performance, goals-assists and impact, and welcomes any opinions.
The fan congratulates the Bangladesh U-20 team on confirming the SAFF U-20 final.
The fan notes just two more goals and it will be a half-century, with Sulaiman Diabate's goal count in Mohammedan's jersey at 48.

The fan notes Fortis FC Ltd's academy trials on 5, 6 and 7 August, saying only Fortis among Bangladesh's professional clubs has an academy as far as he knows, and urges talented players to come with papers and equipment to test their talent.
The fan congratulates Bangladesh.
The post is only a hashtag with no discernible football topic.
Citing today's Kaler Kantho, the fan notes Matin has disappeared after scoring two goals in the last three matches, and never played a full 90 minutes in any match this season.

The fan says domestic football is over for the year and clubs must start working now for next season, since no club can play in the Premier League without a club licence, and lists the AFC licence requirements of full coaching staff, gym, women's team, home venue and youth plan as not very hard.
The fan calls the BPL's last entertainment.

Quoting Prothom Alo, the fan reports BFF's disciplinary committee fined Saif head coach Andres Cruciani one lakh taka and banned him for six months after he entered the field in the 28th minute against Uttar Baridhara, argued with the assistant referee, head-butted the fourth referee and threatened to kill him.
The fan asks who got the red card in the Nepal-Bangladesh match and whether he will be able to play the next match.
The fan simply asks why, with no discernible football topic.
The fan announces the new management's surprise.
The fan says it is really painful to accept such a farewell of a club that supplies footballers to the Bangladesh team.
The fan reports the Khulna Premier Division League result, Mohammedan Sporting Club 2, Brothers Union Club 1, their third win in three matches, and congratulates Mohammedan Sporting Club.

The fan says he cannot understand Saif Sporting Club wanting to move away from football, suggests Tarafder speak openly about his pain over the election or players being taken, notes FIFA and AFC offer justice for contract breaches, and hopes Saif withdraws its application and plays next season.
The post is only an explosion emoji with no discernible football topic.
The fan says he wrote in this group in 2017 that no group came for football's sake, only to publicise their own companies, and the statement is waiting to come true.
The fan says from one Saif alone, how many footballers' lives changed and they played in the national team too, and this same Saif Sporting decided to step away from football.

The fan notes Saif Sporting Club entered professional football with quite a reputation and famous local and foreign players and coaches, but suddenly announced it will no longer run a football club, with Tarafder Mohammad Ruhul Amin saying they will withdraw from all football.

Quoting Suleiman Diabate in Bangla Tribune, the fan argues Mohammedan, Bashundhara Kings and Abahani should on their own initiative give citizenship to Diabate, Robson Robinho and Sunday Chizoba and play them on Bangladeshi passports, instead of waiting on BFF, since the clubs would benefit in the league, the ACL and the AFC Cup.
The fan notes the Bangabandhu Stadium is now in this condition.

The fan calls Saif Sporting's sudden goodbye sad and bad for the country's football, recalling its newness, the BSL proposal, its age-group work and five or six players now in the national team, and blames BFF's corruption and made-up rules while urging other clubs to motivate Saif to change its decision.
The fan simply asks whether it is possible for BK, with no clear football topic.
The fan asks whether Tarafder would have left like this if he had won the last election.

The fan says five days since the game ended, Muktijoddha Sangsad's players are still lying at the club with no money or news, though they saved the team and finished ninth in the league, and asks how football will move forward like this.

Quoting Soleman Diabate, the fan notes he has played in Bangladesh for a few years and wants to wear Bangladesh's jersey if he gets the chance, but first needs citizenship and then a team place, and the path looks hard seeing Elita Kingsley.

The fan says the league is over but Saif's players still have not been paid per contract and are still at the club four days later, and accuses Tarafder of losing his honour by dilly-dallying with players' money, saying Saif's withdrawal was pre-planned.

The fan previews Bangladesh's third straight SAFF U-20 final, notes Yasin Arafat, Morsalin and Fahim were not released by clubs and Yusuf Zulkarnain was not called, yet Mirajul, Nova and Asif shone, and explains how Hamza can use the country-of-origin rule to switch from England while Yusuf cannot, urging Max Rahman be capped in the AFC U-21 qualifiers to lock him to Bangladesh.
The fan tags Chittagong Abahani fans watching the Saif SC news.
The fan argues if Saif really had economic problems they should have looked for a new sponsor or given a notice to sell the club, so at least some of their investment could have come back.
The post reports Faisal Ahmed Fahim joined Dhaka Abahani from Saif, calling it a fire signing by Abahani.

The fan hopes Bangladesh win the title tomorrow with a Bangladeshi as sole top scorer, noting Bangladesh is a good youth and women's team in Asia with a third straight final, and hopes the team wins the SAFF U-20, tops the AFC U-21 qualifiers and takes Bangladesh to the 2027 Asia Cup main round.
The fan says expatriate and local rising footballers can take Bangladesh football to a good position.
The fan vaguely says maybe this is enough to withdraw, since resentment is a bad word and once someone is resentful bringing them back is very hard, with no clear football topic.
The fan simply posts Mohammedan with sparkles and a black heart.
The fan tells others to look at the poster carefully, since Saif Group and Tarafder are not moving away from football and are still with Chittagong Abahani.
The fan says Fortis will reportedly make this their home venue, then they will get good facilities.
The post announces the deal is done: Chittagong Abahani signed central-midfielder Farhad Mona from Mohammedan Sporting Club.
The fan complains his created video was copied exactly and posted in the linked video, and asks for action to be taken.
The post is only folded-hands and heart emojis with no discernible football topic.
The fan shares a Seven TV link for watching the game.
The fan says he stopped watching cricket and is watching football, cheering Bangladesh on.

The fan says he has no joy at Bangladesh U-20 beating India U-20 to win the SAFF U-20, since winning age-group tournaments has never benefited Bangladesh football, blaming age fraud and lack of structure.
The fan says the players are taking unnecessary extra pressure.
The fan says under final pressure, as soon as extra time started they conceded two goals and fell behind 4-2.

The fan says India's U-17 World Cup experience showed in their physical strength, yet Bangladesh were supposed to win, and laments the familiar story since 2015 of losing after playing well, though the U-20 team has reached a third straight final and must now focus on next month's AFC Cup qualifiers.
The fan laments losing in cricket too and football too.

The fan says as soon as extra time started the India juju got the boys and the scoreline became 4-2 within 92 minutes and 5-2 at 98 minutes, congratulates India's youth, and thanks Bangladesh's U-20 boys for a mesmerising tournament until extra time.
The fan posts the SAFF U-20 final's goal timeline, with India scoring at 1:57, 59:32, 91:06, 92:33 and 98:04 and Bangladesh at 44:25 and 47:32, for a 2-5 defeat to India.

The fan says Diabate is a very high-quality player and getting him would be good, while Solomon King will probably play in Portugal and try for the Gambia national team, leaving Diabate and Chinedu Matthew as alternatives.
Citing Naya Diganta, the fan reports Gafurov has joined Bashundhara Kings and Jonathan is also coming for a trial.
The post reports Sohel Rana's new address is Dhaka Abahani Limited, moving from one Abahani to another, citing Navil Khan.
The fan says India is busy winning SAFF after SAFF while Bangladesh are used to sinking the boat at the shore.
The fan asks whether there is a footballer crisis in Bangladesh.
The post reports Farhad Mona moving from Mohammedan to Chittagong Abahani.
The fan says a completely unfamiliar Bangladesh was seen in extra time.

The fan tells the U-20 players not to apologise to spectators for losing the SAFF U-20 final to India's youth, since they won a place in fans' hearts, and says BFF should apologise to them for failing to give improved facilities.
The fan simply asks for votes with Bangladesh flag emojis and no discernible football topic.

The fan argues Nawab will hardly get game time at Abahani, with Fahim and a foreigner on the wings, a foreigner at centre-forward, and Augusto, Maraz, Sohel Rana, Papon Singh and Emon Babu in midfield, and answers that he will not get the game time fans expect.

The fan says Bangladesh fans are used to last-moment losses since 2015 so the SAFF U-20 final defeat hurt little, and urges BFF to keep the U-20 team together and play them in next season's league like Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand did with their Olympic teams, then focus on the AFC Cup qualifiers a month away.

The fan says if all goes well, the next edition of the Bashundhara Kings BFSF U-14 Academy Cup 2022, known as the World Cup of the underprivileged, will be held in December, with details to be updated soon.
The post reports Dorielton is joining Bashundhara Kings, citing Offside.
The post reports goalkeeper Mitul Marma has joined Fortis FC.

The fan says there is no room to sit disappointed, since qualifying for the AFC U-20 main round in September would be a bigger achievement than winning the SAFF, and previews the group opponents Bhutan, Nepal, Qatar and Bahrain, saying Bangladesh must beat Bhutan and Nepal and can beat a token Qatar side.
The fan notes the Bangladesh national women's football team participated in the championship 2022 held in Nepal, and wishes everyone well and good luck to Monika Chakma.
The post announces the deal is done: Eleta Kingsley is joining Abahani Limited from Bashundhara Kings, the surprise announced a few days back.

The post announces the deal is done: Eleta Kingsley is joining Abahani Limited from Bashundhara Kings, the surprise announced a few days back, and calls it the biggest deal in the local quota and Abahani's big surprise of this transfer market.

The fan says if the rumour is true, thanks to both Abahani and Kingsley, and wants Elita played as number nine in the XI rather than as a super sub, since he is not a 25 or 30-minute player and will prove his fitness with enough game time.
The fan notes there is only one ground, so some are playing while others wait, in a scene at Kamalapur Stadium.
The fan says from the start he did not believe Saif's news and tells others to see the proof.
The fan reports Saif Sporting's youth team will play this season's second division league thinking of young footballers' future, but they remain adamant in their decision not to return to the BPL.

The fan notes that though the Saif Sporting youth team expressed interest in playing the second division league starting 10 August, Saif Sporting Club is still firm in its decision not to play in the Premier League.
Photo-only post, no text.
The post is only blue and yellow circle and folded-hands emojis with no discernible football topic.
The fan shares the rise story of goalkeeper Mehdi Hasan.
The fan celebrates Augusto for a third straight season.

The fan argues that at youth level anything is possible, citing Cambodia's U-17 beating Australia 4-2, and says Bangladesh can fight Qatar and Bahrain in the AFC qualifiers and reach the main round if good players like Yusuf Zulkarnain, Yasin Arafat, Max Rahman and Morsalin are added and the team gives 100 percent plus.
The fan recalls that memorable season in the country's football history.
The fan asks whether Chittagong Abahani is signing any players, saying he is not getting any updates.
The post reports defender Asaduzzaman Bablu is joining Dhaka Abahani from Sheikh Russel Krira Chakra.
The fan reports Riasat debuted yesterday as the first Bangladeshi in a South American league, playing for Venezuelan second-division team Rayo Zuliano.
The post announces the deal is done: Sheikh Jamal DC signed 20-year-old centre-back Md Tareq Miah from Muktijoddha Sangsad KC.
The fan praises Riasad as incomparable.

The fan notes the Philippines' Azkals Development Team and Singapore's Young Lions FC play in their countries' top tiers under their federations with only youth national team players and no foreigners, and asks whether Bangladesh will also see the BFF Elite Academy in the BPL after the BCL.
The post reports defender Monir Hossain moving from Abahani to Sheikh Russel.

The fan says if the BFF Elite Academy really plays in next season's Premier League it will be wonderful, wants a 16-team league at eight venues with 30 matches per team, and suggests BFF give one crore from a sponsor or its fund so each player gets three lakh taka.

The fan asks why Tahmid, playing in France's fifth tier and promoted to the senior team, cannot get into the Bangladesh U-20 team when Morocco's Bilal Oshraf and Algeria's Cyril Khetir made their U-23 teams from Spain's and France's lower tiers, and wants him in the AFC U-20 Asian Cup qualifiers.

The fan regrets that Reasat Khaton, the first Bangladeshi to play at Europe's highest club level with SC Freiburg's youth teams and German divisions, was rejected from the 2013-14 camp while Jamal was taken, and says today's Reasat would perform better than Jony and Biplu.

The post announces Fortis FC's age-based trials for Chittagong division players on 13 and 14 August at MA Aziz Stadium, with U-16 trials on the 13th and U-18 and U-20 trials on the 14th, listing the birth-date cutoffs and requirements.
The post reports Brazilian midfielder Rafael Augusto is staying at Dhaka Abahani next season too.

The fan welcomes the BFF Elite Academy news that its best squad will play in the BPL and the rest will form another team in the BCL, saying the developing phase between youth and senior football is most important and the exposure will grow the national team's player pool.
The fan asks whether an unnamed player is not better than Biplu.

The fan likes BFF's initiative to play the Elite Academy in the 2022-23 Premier League and select 30 more players for a BCL team, wants Paul Smalley to stay technical director, suggests six to eight friendlies against ASEAN and Middle Eastern U-20 teams, and argues for a 16-team league at eight venues including the two relegated teams and the Army team.

The post announces the Indira Road Football Academy's journey has begun, with practice on Fridays and Saturdays from 7:00 to 8:30 in the morning and Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 3:30 to 5 in the afternoon.
The post is only a Bangladesh flag emoji with no discernible football topic.
The fan calls Anisur Rahman Zico a world-class goalkeeper no less than Alisson, Neuer or Martinez, arguably Asia's best goalkeeper, and wishes him a happy birthday.
The fan says the country's football will move forward through Bashundhara.

The fan argues both Abahani and Mohammedan must do good work for Bangladesh football, saying Abahani should give Elita Kingsley the number nine jersey and play him in the XI and build an academy and stadium in its sports complex, while Mohammedan should naturalise Solomon Diabate and build a stadium and academy on its Savar land.
The fan says Bangladesh's football is still alive because of one or two players like Anisur Rahman Zico, and wishes him a happy birthday.
The fan notes Bangladesh will play Nepal and Cambodia in September's FIFA window.
The fan sends best wishes to Fortis FC.

The fan says the BPL needs a PSG-like club that does well internationally, hopes Bashundhara Kings become that club in the ACL, praises their fan-base building and bringing Nawab, Tariq and Mahadi home, but asks why such a strong club is syndicate-linked, why Tariq Kazi sits on the bench, and why Oscar has not been sacked.

The fan praises Saif Sporting Club as the first club to dream of making football a profitable institution and Fortis FC for starting with an academy, begs Saif not to leave football, suggests Tarafder Ruhul Amin contest senior vice-president rather than president in the next election, and wants Fortis to sign Samuel Hudson and new expatriate Bangladeshis.
The fan asks how others see this signing.
The post reports Mamunul Islam is joining Fortis from Rahmatganj.
The post reports Mamunul Islam moving from Rahmatganj to Fortis FC.
The fan asks anyone with a sheet of how many matches and goals all Bangladesh national team players have played and scored to comment it, with all matches for the national team.
The fan says Jamal's market value has dropped along with his performance.
The fan notes the pain and frustration of Taiyeb Hasan Babu, Bangladesh's second football referee to receive the National Sports Award.

The fan argues the BPL can become one of Asia's best leagues like the Thai and Malaysian leagues with a 16-team Premier League under AFC licence rules, and goes club by club urging Sheikh Russel, Sheikh Jamal, Muktijoddha, Rahmatganj and Brothers Union to fulfil licence conditions with academies, youth and women's teams, gyms and home venues.
The fan reports two U-20 players may get a chance in Javier Cabrera's camp, Hemanta Vincent may also be called, but Jibon's chances are low since he came late to camp in the past.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan calls Nawab iconic with a diamond emoji.

The fan questions why Saif Powertec sponsors Chittagong Abahani and Bashundhara Group sponsors Sheikh Russel KC, arguing corporate houses should instead focus on their own club's youth team and academy rather than sponsoring others for business and political interests.

The fan laments Dhaka Wanderers Club and Victoria Club disappearing, noting Bangabandhu himself played for Wanderers, and urges BFF, the government and football experts to save these historic clubs with new management, as India does with its century-old clubs.
The post is only heart-eyes and smiling-face-with-hearts emojis with no discernible football topic.
The fan says Mohammedan's season is over this time, many players may not stay next season, and hopes Mohammedan returns stronger next season.

The fan praises Police FC for producing the most new players since joining the Premier League, including 15 or 16 police members and expatriate Bangladeshis like Saklayen Chowdhury, Sanjoy Karim and Joseph Nur, and wants the club to build its own stadium and academy and reach the league's top five.
The fan mentions Ridon's special plan for greater Noakhali's football.

The fan argues professionalism and modernity are needed while preserving grassroots football, proposing the Sohrawardi Cup and Sher-e-Bangla Cup be held every year, district leagues in all 64 districts, an inter-division league, Pioneer football back to 100 plus teams, school and university football revived, and a mini academy and mini stadium in every upazila.
The fan hopes Kingsley, Nawab, Hemanta, Mahadi and Rahbar will be included in the team this time.
The fan simply says great with a heart emoji and no discernible football topic.
The post reports national team forward Mahbubur Rahman Sufil is joining Mohammedan Sporting Club from Bashundhara Kings.
The fan welcomes Rahmat Mia to the Mohammedan courtyard.
The fan welcomes Mahbubur Rahman Sufil to the Mohammedan courtyard.
The fan says Mohammedan is collecting good local players so far, and if they can bring three good-quality foreigners that will be enough.
The fan celebrates young footballer Shahin's extraordinary goal.

The fan reports Maruful Haque may return to Sheikh Jamal, since the Croatian agreed for next season cannot be given the job due to BFF's ban, and with Saif stepping away from the league Maruful and Titu are on the list while a foreign coach is also being sought.

Citing Naya Diganta, the fan reports three more clubs will not play in the league: Arambagh, banned from new registrations by FIFA after failing to pay Brazilian coach Douglas, cannot play the Senior Division; Dhaka City FC registered no players; and Dhaka United will not play the Second Division either.
The fan posts a fact about domestic football transfers.

The fan argues a 16-team Premier League is exactly the demand of the time, letting 400 homegrown Bangladeshi footballers play, with 15 licensed clubs plus the Elite Academy, and says next season clubs should be allowed to register five foreign players with one Asian while only four play on the field.
The fan simply says it happened, with no discernible football topic.
The fan asks why the ban's length is not specified.

The fan says the news of the ban on a neighbouring country improving in football is not at all joyful, noting FIFA banned the All India Football Federation indefinitely, though luck may favour them in the AFC Cup.
The fan notes Mohammedan's transfers are bringing one surprise after another and asks whether Mohammedan's good days are about to return.
The fan notes this World Cup was supposed to be held in India from 11 to 30 October.
The fan notes SAFF will not wait long for India.
The fan breaks the news that FIFA has banned India from all football indefinitely after finding proof of third-party interference in the federation.
The fan wonders how English Premier League clubs' academy systems work.

Citing Manobjibon, the fan reports coach Maruful Haque is going to join Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club with a formal contract in September, and complains he should have gone to a lower-mid club rather than the visionless, syndicate-ridden club that sacked him after he won them the Bhutan Kings Cup and Federation Cup.
The fan announces the coming of Damal with football and Bangladesh flag emojis.

The fan warns everyone to be careful in discussions about the football team's transfers, since a traditional club has issued a legal notice against a few pages, though it is heard a corporate club is fuelling the notice to secure their departed player.

Citing Naya Diganta, the fan reports Chittagong Abahani official Shakil Mahmud Chowdhury said almost all the old footballers will be released to build the team with new players, noting last season's best player Sohel Rana and vice-captain Monir have already been bid farewell and Maruful is also leaving.
The fan simply asks whether it is true, with no discernible football topic.
The fan asks whether Mohammedan club's complaint about various pages is legitimate and requests anyone who knows to inform him.
The fan tells the tradition-selling fools that their page username has a spelling mistake.

The fan calls Mohammedan, one of the two best clubs in the country's entire sports history, shameless for its notice strangling fans' throats and blocking football's road to popularity, and urges all pages and groups to unite in boycotting Mohammedan until the notice is withdrawn.
The fan says if India had followed Bangladesh, maybe India would not be in this state today.
The fan jokes that Rupu and Nipu are now the role models of world football.

The fan says everyone is happy FIFA banned India, and argues the ban benefits Indian football since fresh elections will bring an honest new AIFF president, while Bangladeshis will just watch because Salahuddin will remain president until his death.
The fan asks why Indian football was banned and invites readers to find out.

The fan argues Mohammedan's notice is anti-football and dangerous, says club management is the club since the notice came with the club's name, logo and seal, and calls the management cowardly for threatening young fan pages with legal action while top dailies also reported the transfers, urging everyone not to stay silent.

The fan notes the U-17 AFC Asia Cup qualifiers will be hosted at home in Bangladesh against Yemen, Singapore and Bhutan, hopes Bangladesh become champions and reach the main round for a seventh time, and says Bangladesh must first win the SAFF U-17 in Sri Lanka from 5 to 15 September.

Citing a newspaper report, the fan says if India's ban is not lifted soon, Bashundhara Kings as group runners-up may get a chance to play the AFC Cup inter-zonal semi-final instead of Mohun Bagan, since Mohun Bagan cannot play due to FIFA's ban rather than voluntarily withdrawing, though the final decision rests with the AFC.
The fan says meeting India's cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar is a huge thing for any fan.

The fan says the traditional club Mohammedan, the country's most successful internationally and most passionately supported, has not won a league trophy for 20 years, and calls its management Stone Age-brained and incompetent for forbidding young supporters from sharing transfer updates by press release.

The fan says Mohammedan's notice was issued by its 1980s-era supporters and old brokers through club officials, and accuses the so-called legends who sell the club of treating it as their forefathers' property, with no trophy for 20 years despite the second-biggest budget after Abahani.
The fan asks whether Kings will be able to play in Mohun Bagan's place.

The fan recalls that FIFA banned Bangladesh on 11 January 2002 for political or third-party interference, after Harunur Rashid's committee was removed in December 2001 and an ad hoc committee under S.A. Sultan was formed, and warns Bangladesh may be banned again in future.
The fan vaguely asks who of a team from a memory is more or less in line, playing in Bangladesh's broken league and the national team, with no clear football topic.

The fan calls it Asia's victory, describing Argentina versus Saudi Arabia, where Argentina led from Messi's 10th-minute penalty and had three goals cancelled for offside, then deflated after the break and conceded two goals in five minutes from Al-Shehri and Al-Dawsari, while Saudi goalkeeper Al Owais made five saves in the second half.

The fan Rashedul Islam says the vast sky is covered by Brazil and Argentina flags, with no place for Badal Roy, one of the crown jewels of Bangladesh football's emotions, whose second death anniversary passed silently today, and he remembered Badal da at the end of the day with his last writing about him.

The fan asks what the future of Bangladesh football is, whether there will be any improvement or it will stay the same year after year while fans fight over supporting foreign teams, and what people think of BFF's Elite Academy playing in the Independence Cup, whether they can do better than the current Bangladesh team.

The fan argues Saudi Arabia's win over two-time World Cup winners Argentina, Qatar's 2019 Asia Cup title, France's 2018 World Cup win and England's semi-final all came from the same method, that these teams' jerseys are mainly worn by African-origin footballers, brought over young or born there as citizens and trained in their academies, and says Bangladesh should learn from them since player exchange is now a regular thing in football.

The fan says Asia's football is running, with South Korea looking good, Qatar out of rhythm, Iran conceding six to England but repaying two, and even Sri Lanka, Pakistan and India building expatriate-based teams, while Bangladesh's football is in a demon's belly despite having world-class expatriates, and posts a dream starting XI of Zico, Yasin Arafat, Riyadul Rafi, Topu Barman, Tariq Kazi, Hamza Choudhury, Rahbar or Jamal, Nawab or Samit, Matin Mia, Elita or Sufil, and Rakib or Foysal Fahim.

The fan says that Takuma Asano, who scored a brace against Bangladesh, today scored a goal and beat Germany, recalling that in 2014 Japan U-21 beat Bangladesh 3-0 at Bangabandhu Stadium with Asano scoring twice, and four players from that team played for Japan against Germany today.
The fan says he did not know before that Spain has so many supporters in Bangladesh.

The fan analyses Brazil's World Cup squad, saying the attack, midfield, centre-back and goalpost are the world's best, with nine strikers like Neymar, Vinicius, Richarlison, Jesus, Antony and Pedro, and Alisson as the world's number one keeper, though the left-back is a bit weak and Dani Alves at 39 plus is a worry, while noting Brazil has not lost a World Cup group match in 24 years and joking that Rimon, Bishwanath or Rayhan will not play left-back.
The fan says Quazem Shah scores his first ever professional goal in Bangladesh, wishing him the best of luck.

The fan says for the first time in domestic football, Quazem Shah got his first goal on his first start in the first XI, and in an important match at the end of half-time, Police lead Sheikh Jamal 3-2.
The fan posts the Independence Cup knockout stage line-up.
The fan posts Siuuu, Cristiano Ronaldo's celebration.

The fan says the point keeps coming back that there is so much madness about football among Bangladeshis, yet when Bangladeshi supporters celebrate Brazil, Argentina and Germany in foreign grounds, supporters there ask what Bangladesh's FIFA ranking is and at what level they play, leaving nothing to answer, though everyone's dream is that Bangladesh will one day play in the World Cup and fly its flag on the world stage.

The fan says on Thursday night at Qatar's Lusail Stadium, Serbia committed 12 fouls against Brazil, nine of them against Neymar, the highest foul count against a single player among the 15 matches so far in this World Cup.

The fan posts the 2022 Federation Cup groups, with Group A of Sheikh Jamal DC, Dhaka Mohammedan SC, Rahmatganj MFS and AFC Uttara, Group B of Bashundhara Kings, Chittagong Abahani Ltd., Muktijoddha SKC and Fortis FC, and Group C of Dhaka Abahani Ltd., Sheikh Russel KC and Bangladesh Police FC.
The fan asks whether anyone knows the update, since about a month ago Hamza Choudhury said his father is in contact with BFF, and Hamza said he wants to come to Bangladesh in November.
The fan says the team's focus is not targeting any particular team, they have come to target the entire league, and hopes they will try their best to finish this league with success.

Even as a Brazil fan, the fan thanks the Argentine fans for sharing a video with their media to show how many supporters they have in Bangladesh, and urges Brazil fans to contact Brazilian media and show them the same, with big screens, big flags and Brazil house, and to ask them to help Bangladesh football so Bangladesh too can play in the World Cup.
The fan says today's Bashundhara Kings versus Mohammedan Sporting Club match will be shown on BTV World.
The fan says alhamdulillah, FC Brahmanbaria beat Barishal Football Academy 2-1, staying ahead 2-1 until the end of the match.
The fan simply posts stammering, with no clear football topic.

The fan says Brazilian media made a report during the 2018 FIFA World Cup, and hopes Bangladesh's Brazil fans make a beautiful report or video in the 2022 World Cup, like Argentina fans who connected directly to an Argentine talk show and showed clips of their support.

The fan says for the third time in Independence Cup history a Dhanmondi derby is going to happen in the knockout stage, recalling Abahani's 2-1 quarter-final win over Sheikh Jamal in 2014 with a brace from Leonildo Soares on debut, who later debuted for São Tomé and Príncipe at the 2016 Africa Cup of Nations, and Abahani's 6-0 semi-final win in 2016 with Sunday scoring four including a hat-trick and Lee Tuck a brace.
The fan asks whether people understand Mim's mystery.
The fan posts offside given.

The fan posts Sagorika's nice two-goal highlights from FC Brahmanbaria's 2-1 win over Barishal Football Academy in the Bangladesh Women's Football League 2021-2022 on 26 November 2022 at Kamlapur Stadium, Dhaka.

The fan says young and talented striker Pias Ahmed Nova played his first match in professional football, on loan from Bashundhara Kings to play for Sheikh Jamal this season, and is thought to be the future of Bangladesh football, so he needs to be cared for.
The fan asks whether Tottenham loves Bangladesh.

The fan analyses Spain's passing football at the World Cup, noting the coach picked a young team averaging 23 to 24 years with an eye on the 2026 World Cup and Euro 2024, and says he would not be surprised if Spain played the final, while Mbappe is taking France somewhere despite a shaky defence, and Latin American teams will have to beat Spain and France, with Germany and Croatia ready to interfere.

The fan writes a long syndicate essay, saying he and a few others began legitimate online criticism of the Bangladesh football syndicate in 2015 over Enamul Haque being syndicated out of the national team despite 18 goals for a weak Muktijoddha, got an indirect phone threat in 2016, and traces Rupu's game of benching Ashraful Rana for Shahidul, Mamunul being played over Emon, his advocacy for Sufil and Matin over Jibon, and the Bashundhara Kings pattern of benching Obaid and Elita, concluding he has quit following Bangladesh football out of disgust.
The fan laughs that they are not the committee's team.
The fan says someone is speaking his mind.
The fan says it is possible in every country now, just not ours.
The fan says we have arrived, and if you can come, come, and if you cannot come, watch our game.
The fan says brother, look at the people.

The fan thanks FIFA that Brazil and Argentina have learned how many followers they have in Bangladesh, and argues Bangladesh should host a Super El Clasico FIFA friendly with Messi and Neymar, who both want to come, at the renovated Bangabandhu Stadium for about 50 crore, recoverable from tickets and broadcast rights, while Brazil should give more football help and BFF should market Bangladesh's huge football market to FIFA to host the Asian Cup or co-host a World Cup.
The fan says Rakib scored in four consecutive Independence Cup matches.
The fan says Bashundhara Kings are on the path to a treble like Russel KC in 2013, offering advance congratulations.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan asks when the Bangladesh national football team's upcoming tournament or match is, saying he really wants to cheer his country loudly and celebrate, but does not think it is possible.

The fan profiles 22-year-old Zakaria Aboukhlal, Morocco's number 14 forward who scored the second goal against Belgium, noting he holds three citizenships, Moroccan through his mother, Dutch through birth in the Netherlands and Libyan through his father, and that Libya and the Netherlands both offered him a place, but in 2020 he chose Morocco, calling it his career's best decision.
The fan sighs, 'Ah, our football', with a pleading face emoji.

The fan says the 2026 48-team World Cup format is old news, but the new talk is Russia reportedly wanting to move from UEFA to AFC, and argues AFC should extract from FIFA that ten teams from Asia get World Cup chances instead of nine, by cutting one spot from CONCACAF, Africa or the Americas, so Russia's arrival does not hurt others and AFC's brand value grows.
The fan asks, with less than a week left for the Premier League, whether BFF has given the schedule, and if not, when they might give it.
The fan simply writes 'Please accept', with no clear football topic.
The fan simply posts laughing emojis, with no clear football topic.
The fan asks whether anyone can please tell him when Bangladesh has a national football match.

The fan says not to forget in the World Cup mood that on the 5th, dear Bashundhara Kings will play the Independence Cup final against Russel KC, and to keep up with the country's football and try to watch the country's matches, hoping Kings beat Russel and win the final, with the match starting at 1 pm at Comilla Stadium.
The fan says this time the syndicate's victim is national team regular Bishwanath Ghosh, and he wants to see dear dada in Bashundhara Kings' XI, kicking the syndicate in the face.
The fan says he really liked the colour of this Police jersey.

The fan says he does not know who this player is and does not need to know, but he wants to leave his club Inter Miami CF, and since beloved Bashundhara Kings need a perfect number 10, they should give him a chance.
The fan says for the sake of the country's football, we want a new champion.

The fan says since everyone got their money properly, a daylight robbery happened today, and it would be better to directly hand the trophy to a specific team for money instead of playing on the field.

The fan says how shameless Sheikh Russel must be to hand the match to Bashundhara like this, since everyone knows the two are from the same stable, but to expose themselves like this in front of so many spectators and media is unimaginably toxic for the country's football, noting in the tie-breaker Sheikh Russel started with three locals and missed two of three with two easy weak kicks to the same side in the same style.

The fan says Sheikh Russel deserve this trophy, since everyone played with their lives for 120 minutes, but after that the script changed in the dugout, and even if they become champions and tie the bundle, they will get beaten again in the AFC.

The fan says they did a good 120-minute drama that would beat even labourer-director Kajal Arefin, a low-budget drama, and Bashundhara be like, I am the hero of the story, I am the villain of the story.

The fan says anyone who compares the football World Cup with any other sporting event is definitely a fool, since football is the world's number one sport and Bangladeshis' favourite too, but Bangladeshis want to see Bangladesh succeed in sports, and amid the World Cup knockouts it did not escape notice that Bangladesh won in cricket against India yesterday, so if football brings success in international tournaments, people will pay attention to Bangladesh football too.

The fan says Bangladesh has plenty of Brazil-Argentina fans, which those countries already know, so they should give Bangladesh a chance to play as a guest country in the Copa America Championship, so our Rimon, Bisu, Biplu and Jony Alam can prove themselves a bit.
The fan says Cornelius Stewart is the best.
The fan asks since when does South Korea play in the SAFF Championship football.
Photo-only post, no text.

The fan says no high-priced local or foreign players, Sarah Resort, bonuses, dog squad on social media or pre-season are needed, a good-quality coach is enough, and after the Independence Cup final, Zulfikar Mahmud Mintu deserves applause for Sheikh Russel's performance.
The fan congratulates Morocco.

The fan says if Oscar Bruzon were in Spain's dugout today, perhaps he would have returned winning the World Cup, just as he keeps blooming titles one after another with Bashundhara Kings, adding that talented people are not valued these days and Spain got a fitting lesson for neglecting the home boy.
The fan asks whether any football intellect can tell him why this goal was disallowed, asking Arefin Zeesan to please help.
The fan shares what Argentina's former goalkeeper Goycochea said about Bangladesh.
The fan posts the Bangladesh Premier League 2022-23 schedule.

The fan says football is the king of all sports and his favourite, with good physical exercise and finished in just two hours so each prayer can be done, but he does not like adult men running in half-pants, noting football can be played without showing the knees, as Neymar's knees are not visible and many Qatar World Cup teams played with their knees covered.
The fan asks on which website he can get the best news on Bangladesh football.
The fan simply thanks Zahid Rahman bhai for making a beautiful post, with no clear football topic of its own.
The fan asks how people liked Fortis FC's match today.

The fan announces a Federation Cup traditional fantasy game that can be played in an app with a round-wise system, asking anyone interested in playing to say so in the comments, since whether they bring the league depends on people's interest.
The fan asks which team are you today.
The fan says Barrister Sumon Football Academy has its own bus too, and alas, many top-tier clubs in Bangladesh do not have their own transport bus.
The fan says to see the Bangladesh Premier League 2022-23 points table after the first round.

The fan says FC Brahmanbaria striker Sagorika has been called up to the BFF U-20 women's national football talent hunt, wishing her well and hoping she makes the final squad, and asking everyone to pray for her.
The fan posts Argentina with rock-on emojis.
The fan says registration for the Dhaka Pioneer Football League 2022-23 has started, with the league expected to get going on the field in March 2023.

The fan says amid the World Cup frenzy we are forgetting our own country's football, though Bangladesh was supposed to play in the 2022 Qatar World Cup, and Kazi Salahuddin showed that dream, yet Bangladesh sits at 192nd in the rankings, but there is still a chance for 2026 with 48 teams and nine from Asia directly plus a playoff, listing stars like Hamza Choudhury, Samit Som, Quinn Sullivan, Max Rahman, Nabil Irfan, Nawab, Yusuf Zulkarnain, Mahdi Khan, Nabil Karim, Rahbar Khan, Zico, Topu, Yasin Arafat, Faisal Fahim, Elita Kingsley, Robson Robinho and Sulaiman Diabate, and demanding Salahuddin's resignation if he keeps sleeping.
The fan says he thought Maldives was the only country without expatriate footballers, but now they too are calling expatriates into the team.
The fan simply posts a fire emoji, with no clear football topic.
The fan posts Topu da with a rock-on emoji.

The fan says the World Cup is almost over and December is half over, but Hamza Choudhury still has not come to Bangladesh, and asks when he might come and whether anyone has any information or idea, since he had said he would come during the World Cup in December.
The fan says they are going to organise a fantasy event around the Federation Cup, and asks anyone willing to sponsor to contact them soon.

The fan asks why the country's football did not improve in 19 years even after winning the SAFF in 2003, and whether the BFF president can avoid this responsibility, inviting everyone's valuable opinions.
The fan posts the next match, FC Brahmanbaria versus Cumilla United club tomorrow at 1:00 pm at BSSSMMK Stadium Kamalapur, Dhaka, wishing FC Brahmanbaria the best of luck.

The fan says everyone should talk about dear Shihab bhai, assistant fitness trainer and cameraman, who arranges everything for Kings superstars Zico, Sabuj and Fahad, local and foreign players and even their holiday resorts, and helps Oscar, Nipu and Roxy, arguing that just as the Kings official page recognised Wasim, Shihab deserves the same recognition and is the most qualified person to be Kings team manager.
The fan applies the proverb that a mullah's run ends at the mosque to football, saying Bangladesh football officials' run ends at the SAFF Championship.
The fan asks whether anyone here is from AFC Uttara.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan simply writes that Zahid Rahman wrote wonderfully, with no clear football topic of its own.
The fan asks what songs Argentina supporters sing during matches.
The fan posts Rahbar Wahed Khan with fire emojis.

The fan shares a Channel i Online interview in which former star footballer Khandaker Rakibul Islam tells journalist Zahid Rahman that France are ahead but Morocco are unpredictable, with Mbappe the main magic and Giroud in great form, while Morocco beat Spain on penalties in the second round and Portugal 1-0 in the quarter-final, and a France final would revive Argentina's pain from the 3-4 loss to France in 2018.

The fan tells those saying Croatia was ranked so low in 1993 to first learn the history of Yugoslavia and the Balkans, noting Croatia was part of Yugoslavia before 1991, which broke into Kosovo, Macedonia, Serbia, Bosnia, Montenegro and Slovenia, and Croatia became a FIFA member only in 1992, so a low 1993 ranking was natural, and nine of the 1998 World Cup third-place team had also played for Yugoslavia.

The fan writes a poetic tribute to Luka Modric, calling him nephew from Modraci village at the foot of the Velebit mountains, saying football lovers wonder whether he has lungs given how he roams the whole field without tiring, and that we may not see him at the World Cup again.
Photo-only post, no text.
The fan asks whether anyone knows anything about this, sharing only a YouTube link with no explanation.
The fan simply posts a cake emoji, with no clear football topic.
The fan says if our national football got even 10 percent of the support seen for Brazil and Argentina over the last month, our country would have gone far.
The fan asks in which grounds the Premier League is being played, and whose home venue is which.

The fan says Bangladesh never loses a match in which Topu scores, and despite being a defender he scored four goals in the SAFF Championship and six goals for the national team, wishing him a happy birthday.
The fan says it hurts when the new generation asks, 'Brother, does Bangladesh play football?!'
The fan says it is amazing to think that our Nawab's Nawabi is ending, since he went to such a club where he does not even get a place on the bench.

The fan explains the 2026 48-team World Cup format, with eight teams from Asia qualifying directly and the ninth playing a playoff, and 16 groups of three with two going to the knockouts, saying if Bangladesh proceeds correctly playing in the World Cup is not impossible, but if they cannot do what is needed they will not even get a chance in the Asian Cup.

The fan likes FIFA president Infantino expanding the World Cup to more teams, but argues giving CONCACAF six slots is wrong since besides the USA, Mexico, Canada and Costa Rica there is no good team, and proposes Asia's ninth team play Africa's tenth and Asia's tenth play CONCACAF's sixth in playoffs, so Asia gets ten chances while CONCACAF keeps six, with Europe at 16 plus a 17th playoff team.
The fan asks whether Abahani will win today's match, or drop points again like the first match.
The fan says Farhaan Ali is now very close to the English Premier League, and if he keeps his current form he may be seen in the EPL very soon.
The fan says Abahani supporters can now breathe a sigh of relief, otherwise they might not have been able to show their faces in shame.

The fan explains the AFC club competitions changing from 2024-25 to three tiers instead of the current two, the ACL and AFC Cup, with 24 teams in the first tier, 32 clubs in eight groups in the second tier and 20 clubs in five groups playing single-leg matches at a centralised venue in the third tier.
The fan hopes that after Hamza, Farhan will also play in the English Premier League.

The fan asks whether this is Asma's last World Cup, quoting Asma Abdul Hamid saying niqab and hijab are Muslim women's dress and she will not give up this dress even if she may not get volunteer duty at the 2023 Women's World Cup because of it.
The fan says at least this time he should be called up to the national team.

The fan says there is no alternative to taking Robson, Hamza, Samit, Kingsley, Max, Yusuf and Nawab into the 26-member national team squad if Bangladesh is to be seen at the next level, noting Robson is very keen to play for Bangladesh but he is confused whether the five-season rule still applies or FIFA has removed it so a passport and NOC are enough, and that the rest are fully ready with no FIFA rule problem.

The fan raises two issues, first that national team coach Javier Cabrera's contract ends this month and asks who the next coach will be and whether BFF will renew Cabrera or look for someone new, suggesting young good coaches for the six academies opening and an experienced heavyweight former national team coach for the national team, with good players first ahead of the World Cup and Asian Cup playoff, and second why Abahani and Sheikh Jamal are not giving Kingsley and Nawab chances.
The fan posts 'Rest In Peace Legend', a tribute to Pele.
The fan hopes the Sylhet division's expatriate players will help advance the country's football, and that we will see Hamza, Samit Som, Nawab, Elita and Yusuf Haque in the national jersey.
The fan says Elita Kingsley is the hero of Abahani's win, scoring against Muktijoddha.

The fan thanks Abahani and Mario Lemos for fielding Kingsley today and asks them to field him as a Bangladeshi footballer in future matches, congratulating Elita Kingsley on scoring on his debut against Abahani to win the match and hoping he scores 16 to 18 goals in 20 or 22 league matches and is seen in the national team.

The fan asks who everyone wants as the next national team coach, whether Cabrera should be renewed or someone new and better should come, recalling Edson Silva Dido and Lodewijk de Kruif as very good coaches, arguing coaches need freedom, proper pay and to be above the syndicate and need good players first, and personally wanting Cabrera and Jamie Day kept for youth development while the national team gets an experienced former national team coach like Tom Saintfiet or Nikola Ilievski, with a contract requiring 300 of 365 days in Bangladesh.
The fan asks whether there is any chance of Bashundhara Kings playing Al Nassr in the AFC Champions League.
The fan says Bashundhara Kings will play the AFC Champions League qualifiers next year, and if they qualify we may see Bashundhara versus Al-Nassr FC.
The fan shares the advice BFF vice-president Ataur Rahman Bhuiyan Manik gave to referees.
The fan praises a T Sports cameraman.
The fan recalls that the current BFF president then wanted to bring Pele to Dhaka.
Fan scoffs at the Bangladesh Football Federation's professionalism.

The fan says Bashundhara Kings should organise a friendly match against Saudi club Al Nassr at Kings Arena, so a player like Cristiano Ronaldo plays on Bangladesh's ground and our footballers get to see him up close and play with him, and BFF should help with it, since both are Asian clubs so it is very possible.
Fan posts a mock-respectful salute to BFF president Kazi Salahuddin.
Fan post hyping Swedish-Bangladeshi player Max Rahman.
Fan praises organizer Sharafat, who loves developing new footballers rather than building a title-winning team.

Fan notes the new class-six history textbook tells the story of the Bangladesh women's team's football triumph.
Fan post saying football is not just a game, it is an emotion.
Fan maps Bangladesh's path: win the playoff to reach the top 18 and qualify for the 2027 Asia Cup and World Cup qualifying.

Fan celebrates Dorielton Gomes's bicycle-kick goal from Rakib's assist.
Fan calls Dorielton a beast and says he is eager to see him score in the AFC competitions.
Fan notes Elita Kingsley scored both goals for Abahani today.

Fan argues Bangladesh needs both grassroots development and an immediately strengthened national team with Hamza, Samit, Sullivan and Kingsley for the playoff and SAFF.
