posts.summary: Argues expatriates benefit football short- and long-term alongside grassroots work, tells Alfaz and Shayek to make their clubs contribute to grassroots, and calls Shayek's public opinions a conflict of interest.
Shares that Cuba Mitchell's last two matches and today's match can be watched live on YouTube and praises his playing style.

Attacks TV pundits for joking about origin players and claiming talent will run out in five to seven years, citing Jamaica, Morocco and Indonesia, and defends Fahamidul as a Sampdoria academy product.
Recalls that in 2017 Moroccans mistook a visiting Hamza Choudhury for their own origin player and begged him to play for Morocco.
Rant saying fans do not respect former footballers enough and many ex-players deserve constant abuse.

Reports 15-year-old UAE-based keeper Mohammad Uzair Hasan Chowdhury, a top Dubai academy-league performer now at Athletic Bilbao branch club Atletico Juniors, has been called to the U19 camp for the SAFF U19 in India in May.
Emoji-only fan post with Bangladesh flags and a tiger.
Laments Bangladesh is about to lose a gem to the syndicate, saying these are Bangladeshis born and raised in football-advanced countries whom locals pull down instead of lifting up.
Asks why they cannot be called Bangladeshi footballers spread across the world instead of expatriate, origin or foreign players, since they are part of Bangladesh's roots.
Hashtag post demanding the syndicate step down and Fahamidul be brought back.
Argues expatriate talent brings results, sponsors and youth interest, and tells critics to ask their club bosses to build academies instead of using grassroots as an excuse.
Praises Saeed Hasan Kanan's tactical analysis and says Cabrera must be sacked over the Al Amin, Ibrahim and Chandon calls, since even without Hamza Bangladesh drew four of five against India.
Asks football experts why two current Palestinian players play regularly in Israel's top tier while Israel carries out genocide in Palestine.

Long analysis of the women's Asia Cup qualifiers draw arguing Bangladesh can beat Bahrain and Turkmenistan and have a real chance against hosts Myanmar, while backing Butler's selection and warning BFF against sabotage.
Profiles UAE-born Manzurul Karim, now a Dhaka Wanderers left winger in the BPL with a Manchester City training-camp past, who is rumoured to get a senior national team trial.

Claims local coaches and ex-players oppose expatriates because club contracts share huge sums with syndicate people and coaches earn commissions from their own players, which expatriates would not pay.
Notes Hamza Choudhury was the brightest player on the pitch even though Sheffield lost.
Says the two easy ways into Cabrera's XI are playing for Bashundhara Kings or befriending a clique of national players like Topu Barman and Sohel Rana, whose backing extended Cabrera's tenure.
Urges BFF to act now and approach a talent before Jamaica hijack him.
Asks whether Qatar's Stars League is better than the BPL and whether a Qatar top-tier player is better than local Bangladeshi players, noting India lost defensively to Qatar.
Says Palestine slogans and flags will fly across Bangladesh tomorrow and it is time to take to the streets again.
Vague fan post saying 'Because I'm a human being'.
Long essay arguing FIFA is not apolitical, recounting the 2018 and 2022 World Cup hosting bribes, the FBI and Swiss probe, Chuck Blazer's testimony and Blatter's ban.
Welcomes a player to Bhutan's Paro FC.
Celebrates Arham having a great time in Australia.
Reports US-based attacker Farzad Aftab, 18, who played MLS Next, has been called for the SAFF U19 trials and can play winger or forward.

Hopes the National Stadium is ready before the June Singapore match so Hamza plays his first home game there, and wants the government to allocate stadiums in all eight divisions so Bangladesh can dream of hosting the 2031 Asia Cup.
Scoffs at how little research the country's top reporters do before making videos.
Calls for a general strike in Bangladesh on April 7 in solidarity with Gaza, urging schools, offices and exams to shut down.
Praises a recent report by Arefin Zeesan as one of the best.
Asks whether Solomon King, after five straight BPL seasons and a return, can still play for Bangladesh or must complete five fresh seasons, and what the obstacles are.
Hashtag post standing with Gaza.
Asks for photos of Bangladesh's 1980 AFC Asian Cup team, having found none on Getty Images or Google.
Notes Hamza Choudhury has been silently protesting since 2021.
Fan post cheering 'Our Hamza Chowdhury'.
Meetup notice for Cumilla Stadium at 2:30pm on April 8, urging everyone to unite for football's sake.
Shares Ronan Sullivan highlights, calling him a pure striker who will be perfect for the national team once stronger and older.
Claims Jamal Bhuyan is being held hostage by the syndicate and BFF has barred him from speaking to the media, saying if he spoke like Tamim everything would be exposed.
Contrasts Indonesia, which understands long- and short-term planning and is going to the U17 World Cup, with Bangladesh's syndicate and brokerage.
Defends Kanak Mahmud by weighing his overall positive work, distinguishes Fahim Rahman from cricket migrants, and thanks journalists who covered the India match despite Cabrera behaving like a clown.
Uses Indonesia's rise to argue expatriates lift grassroots too, attacks Bashundhara's syndicate takeover, and demands Cabrera be sacked for a proven coach answerable to Tabith Awal.
Remarks that a club coach is more qualified than the national team coach.

Warns Ronan Sullivan could suffer the same fate as Yusuf Zulkernain and Arham from politics and jealousy if he only plays youth teams, and says he should go straight into the national team like Hamza.

Says origin players are clearly ahead in basics and physique but the heat is against them, rejects Zidan Mia-type players, and warns the BFF president that media ignorance lets the syndicate exploit the issue.
Defends Zidan Mia, saying critics judge him without watching, his fitness and free kicks are excellent, and he should get a chance to prove himself.

Argues the six regional BKSPs should be converted into sports hubs with only two new ones built, then all 64 district stadiums renovated, and BFF given eight stadiums for 25 years for FIFA Goal Project upgrades.
Complains local players just cross aimlessly whenever they take the ball into the box.
Says broadcasting on Mycujoo seemed better than the current coverage.
Reports ten-man Abahani beat Bashundhara Kings 1-1 (4-3 on penalties) in the Federation Cup qualifier to reach the final, with keeper Mitul Marma man of the match.
Vague post hoping BFF and Tabith Awal are serious about an unspecified ongoing discussion.
Shares a stunning free-kick goal from outside the box by Bangladeshi-origin footballer Ayman Samrat.
Misses seeing Barrister Syed Sayedul Haque Suman in the jersey, saying it has been a long time.

Reports Abahani beat Bashundhara 4-2 on penalties after a 1-1 draw over 120 minutes to reach the Federation Cup final, with Mitul Marma man of the match again, while Kings face Rahmatganj on April 15.
Lists ASEAN's active tournaments, eight more than SAFF including futsal and a club championship, and argues joining ASEAN would bring infrastructure and club-culture benefits.
Asks why no news mentioned the match was in Cumilla, naming the stadium but not the district or place.
First-person account of anti-syndicate protesters being detained, abused and beaten after the Bashundhara vs Abahani match, with one companion given death threats, and a demand for justice.
Says BFF and the clubs still do not fully understand the importance of media presentation.
Emoji-only fan post.
Shares the profile of Ayman Samrat, who plays for Norway's fourth-tier SF Grei.
Reports English-born Bangladeshi centre-back Tofael Tanim, 22 and 6'2" at Southend Manor FC, is coming to Bangladesh for the June trials.
Fragment post reading only 'EFL Commentator', apparently sharing a clip.
Asks how Panama, a nation of four million with no world-class player, rank so high and routinely beat the USA, and what Bangladesh can learn from them.

Notes Fahamidul starts regularly at Olbia Calcio, Al-Amin is the league's local top scorer and Taj-Uddin among its best right-backs, yet the India draw was celebrated, and warns Cabrera's staff will damage BFF's positive image.
Addresses Samit Shome directly, reminding him he promised a decision by April 10-12 and begging him not to delay as fans wait like thirsty birds.
Complains the broadcast cameras are never right, or else the sound is wrong.
Asks what the new update on Samit Shome is.
Fan post saying 'Bro is conspicuously marvelous!'
Tells people in Sylhet and Chittagong to get ready because Hamza is coming.
Asks why Fahamidul cannot play when 15-year-old Jeremy Monga debuted for Leicester City in the Premier League at 15 years 271 days, calling the age and experience objections unprofessional.
Declares Dhaka, Chittagong and Sylhet will tremble with Hamza fever.
Condemns an attack on an anti-syndicate protester by local coach Tuhin and associates at the April 7 Bashundhara vs Abahani match in Cumilla, which seriously injured him and included death threats.
Joke post saying 'Kaka is innocent' with laughing emojis.
Notes Bangladeshi-origin players are coming for BFF's June trials and asks whether BFF can arrange a proper professional international-standard trial, a rare chance for the future.
Says many have opposed the Bashundhara syndicate since before the BFF election, backing it with data, while the other side offers only 'coach's style' and hides behind the freedom BFF gave the coach.
Reports US-based Farzad Aftab is creating a storm of pace in U19 training, scoring in a practice match after a run of about 30 yards.
Shows off the renovated Dhaka National Stadium in its new form, with new expectations for the country's football.
Compares Mitul Marma to Emiliano Martinez, saying he is equal in smartness.

Reports Farzad Aftab is catching the eye in U19 training; the 18-year-old can play attacking midfield, both wings and forward, and played for San Jose Earthquakes youth and Ballistic United in MLS Next.
Argues a good coach can transform a bad team, as Arsenal prove, and Bangladesh badly needs an Otto Pfister or Kottan-quality coach.
Shares a link saying the real test is now for Maria, Sanjida and Krishna under women's coach Peter Butler.
Vague post asking what hypocrisy this is from FIFA.
Wishes happy birthday to captain Jamal Bhuyan, calling him the pride and fighting captain.
Celebrates Jamal Bhuyan's 34th birthday, noting his 87 caps and hoping he reaches 100 as the first Bangladeshi, wins SAFF 2025 and qualifies for the 2027 Asia Cup under his captaincy.
Teases a Bangladeshi-origin footballer who played in Denmark's league and for a national team ranked between 1 and 100, with details promised in D-BOX.
Says Hamza was Bangladesh's best player against India and asks who will be the first Bangladesh-born player to outperform him in a match, guessing Morsalin.
Says Bangladesh really needs Jey Uddin, calling him the most talented footballer in Bangladesh.
Profiles high-profile Bangladeshi-origin footballer Molik Jesse Khan, 21, six feet tall, central midfielder at Slovakia first-tier AS Trencin.
Announces Samit Shome is coming home, sharing Pakistani YouTubers' reaction.
Repeats the Molik Jesse Khan profile, adding he carries Bangladeshi blood from his father and has represented Trinidad and Tobago internationally.

Explains Jesse Khan cannot switch to Bangladesh because he played 14 minutes against Jamaica in the 2023 Gold Cup, like Adama Traore with Spain at Euro 2020, and urges BFF to pitch legacy to Quinn Sullivan.
Retells Jamal Bhuyan's early struggle: a Copenhagen offer after a Brondby youth goal, being shot four times in a gang fight, 12 surgeries, and his rise to Bangladesh's most-capped player.
Quotes BIDA chairman Ashik Chowdhury on Hamza centring attention and urges BFF to work with the sports ministry for academies in every district and world-class stadiums in every division.

Long birthday tribute to Jamal Bhuyan, born in Copenhagen in 1990, shot four times, debuting against Nepal in August 2013 as the first origin player and paving the way for Tariq, Kazem, Rahbar, Nawab and Hamza.
Asks on which YouTube channel today's BCL matches can be watched.
Argues traditional Dhaka Mohammedan, never a professional league winner and four-time runners-up, must win the title this time, leading Abahani by three points with eight games left.
Profiles Barcelona Academy USA product Amir Sami, 18, now with Long Island Slammers, who is coming to Bangladesh for the June open trials.
Reports Bangladesh may play Hong Kong on October 14 at MA Aziz Stadium in Chittagong in an Asian Cup qualifier at home.
Announces Bangladesh will face India in Sylhet on November 18, 2025 in an AFC Asian Cup qualifier, special because Hamza Choudhury's home is in Sylhet.
Fan post saying '0% performance, 100% attitude'.
Tags BFF saying an unnamed player is highly needed right now.
Proposes a Southampton St Mary's-style 33,000-capacity stadium for a divisional city like Chittagong, Rajshahi or Sylhet, funded via NSC, BFF and partners for 70 to 90 million dollars.
Praises BFF's work for sprinter Imranur Rahman and regrets he got eligibility late, or Bangladesh could have had an Asian Games medal and Olympic 100m semi-finalist.
Reports the U19 camp will be held at Jessore's famous Shamsul Huda Academy and three of four U19 triallists survived, with the UAE-based goalkeeper likely dropped.
Fan post naming Shamsul Huda Football Academy in Jessore, apparently a photo caption.
Profiles Welsh second-tier winger Sameer Miah, 20, of Bangladeshi paternal blood from Sylhet, who is coming for BFF's June trials.
Shares a Bangla Outlook article by Subail Bin Alam, calling it significant coming from someone of his profile.
Reports Samit Shome is coming, has started Bangladeshi passport work, hopes to play against Singapore in June, and should be welcomed like Hamza.
Reports Samit Shome is coming, has started Bangladeshi passport work, and hopes to play against Singapore in June.
Reports Samit Shome is coming and has started Bangladeshi passport work, hoping to play against Singapore in June.
Reports Samit Shome is coming and has started Bangladeshi passport work, hoping to play against Singapore in June.
Announces Samit Shome has agreed to play for Bangladesh.
Reports Samit Shome is keen to play against Singapore in June for Bangladesh and has already started passport work.
Reports Canadian Premier League midfielder Samit Shome has agreed to play in the red-green jersey.
Emoji-only fan post.
Vague fan post saying 'Our next deliberate' with a heart emoji.
Welcomes Samit Shome to Bangladesh with heart emojis.

Confirms Samit Shome's agreement is official and lists the three documents needed, passport, Canada FA NOC and FIFA approval, hoping Hamza, Samit and Fahamidul play together against Singapore in June.
Notes a Cambodian club is heading to the AFC Challenge League final after a 3-0 first-leg semi win over Indonesia's Madura, and asks 'And us?'
Celebrates a long-cherished dream coming true as Samit Shome agrees to play for Bangladesh.
Questions how realistic June service is for Samit Shome given parents' passport renewal, birth registration, Canada FA clearance and FIFA approval, and hopes Arefin Zeesan analyses it.
Says he predicted two weeks ago that Samit Shome would come since he showed interest himself, and now it is time to welcome him like a king in June.
Breaking news post saying Samit Shome has decided to play for Bangladesh, BFF is working on his passport, and his debut could come against Singapore.
Laments BFF's neglect lost forward Robson, who could have played another season, saying with him Bangladesh would not worry about goals.
Urges BFF to go all out for 19-year-old Cuba Mitchell, a Sunderland U21 regular with an assist, before Jamaica take him or he debuts for Sunderland's senior team.
Fan post saying 'Welcome to home' with fire emoji.
Profiles Cuba Mitchell and Farhan Ali Wahid as the next big origin names, urging BFF to send a representative to Sunderland to convince Cuba's mother before Jamaica takes him.
Says breaking the syndicate requires boycotting T Sports and supporting other channels instead.
Shares Sofascore ratings mocking Saad Uddin's India performance: 26 touches, one of nine ground duels won, nine of 20 passes misplaced, possession lost 14 times.
Vague celebratory fan post calling something a huge achievement for Bangladesh in South Asian and Asian football.
Fan post saying they are trying to make something with AI.
Shares a video of Samit Shome's goals, assists and skills.
Praises BFF vice-president Fahad Karim's work since his election and urges him to prioritise Cuba Mitchell, the Sunderland U21 No. 10, since Quinn Sullivan will not decide now.
Lamets the state of the domestic league over a Bangladesh Police FC versus Fakirapool Young Men's Club match.
Vague fan post saying a player will be a great addition to the team.
Fan waits to see Hamza Choudhury's foot magic against Singapore.
Celebrates a new wave in Bangladeshi football after Hamza, now Shamit Shome, one from the English Premier League and one from Canada's national team, and asks who is next.
Asks Arefin Zeesan to look into getting Cuba Mitchell, saying Bangladesh needs him.

Argues Quinn Sullivan, Farhan Ali Wahid and Rikuto Hashimoto will not come for two or three more years, so fans should stop pestering them, and says Hamza, Samit and Fahamidul should play against Singapore.
Shares a BPL Matchday fixture for April 12, Dhaka Wanderers versus Dhaka Abahani at Shahid Barkat Stadium in Gazipur, live on T Sports.
Fan calls it another memorable day for Bangladesh football supporters.
Welcomes extra police at Kings Arena as a good decision to avoid sudden incidents.
Says this is the state of local Bangladeshi footballers, who cannot do what they were picked for yet keep playing because a big club backs them.
Fan post saying 'Here we go!'

Celebrates Samit Shome trending at the top after eight years since Ashiqur Rahman Rajon found him in 2017, thanks BFF and Fahad Karim, and warns Fahamidul-type profiles must not be deprived on the field.
Shares a link saying Rituparna won readers' hearts and became the best athlete.
Passes on the family's request to write his Bengali name correctly as Somit Som, not Samit Shome.
Says after Samit the biggest name is Cuba Mitchell and BFF should start preparing for him now.
Demands Javier Cabrera be removed, saying a head coach of real calibre is needed to get the best out of players like Hamza and Samit.
Proposes a full XI and 23-man squad for June against Singapore in a 4-4-2 diamond, with Fahamidul and Morsalin as 60th-minute impact subs and Jamal starting to hand the armband to Hamza.
Fan post cheering Samit Shome with fire emoji.
Shares a news link calling Samit Shome's arrival undoubtedly great news for Bangladesh after Hamza.
Quotes Samit Shome's agent Amit Hasan saying Samit's parents have not renewed passports since 1993, so new passports are needed before he visits the Bangladesh embassy in Canada.

Reports Cuba Mitchell is football's most trending topic and Horizon Spots founder Sakib Mahmud, bringing 30-plus origin players for June trials, will travel to England to meet Cuba at the end of April.
Welcomes Shamit Shome home, saying he has given the green signal to BFF and passport work has started.
Welcomes footballer and electrical engineer Samit Shome, noting he is also an EEE graduate from Concordia University.
Recalls dreaming of a Jamal-Hamza-Samit midfield since Rajon flagged Samit in 2016-17, and expects his debut in June before a full gallery during the Eid holidays.
Notes two-time Asian champions Qatar field Al Hashmi Al Hussain from Spain's fifth tier with three caps, yet only Bangladesh's upstarts and syndicate members fret about lower tiers.
Wants friendly matches against Indonesia and Malaysia before the Singapore game.
Welcomes newcomer Shamit Shome to Bangladesh.

Says even ignoring Cabrera's skill, tactics and syndicate dealings, it is time to farewell him with dignity since the incoming stars need a high-profile coach with top man-management, as the Fahamidul incident proves.
Emoji-only fan post.
Says after Hamza and Samit the big name in the country's football is Cuba Mitchell and hopes BFF tries hard enough to get him.
Tells Arefin Zeesan that BFF needs him as general secretary, saying he thinks about football more than the current office-holder and could convince more origin players with Fahad Karim.
Boasts two of Bangladesh's finest players come from the world's top leagues, the English Premier League and Major League Soccer.
Asks why the pipeline must be mentioned whenever origin players come up and who forbade strengthening it.
Celebrates that Bangladesh is finally about to get Samit Shome.
Describes the Federation Cup semi-final where Bashundhara and Abahani drew 1-1 before Abahani won on penalties amid fans' celebrations.
Fan post wishing Muzaffar Muzaffarov a happy birthday.
Long tribute asking whether Bangladesh can play without Jamal Bhuyan at 35, recalling how he carried the team in its darkest days, fought the syndicate and stood with students in the July movement.
Fan agrees with someone but notes others will not delay in taunting him as an expatriate.
Suggests a football league with one club from each division would be good.
Says with Samit's arrival Bangladesh now has one of South Asia's best midfields and only the scoring problem remains to solve.
Notes Hamza and Samit Shome are now Bangladesh's and asks who the next target should be.
Argues getting Cuba Mitchell as the next No. 10 and versatile Niloy van der Pol would complete the national team for years, noting neither needs FIFA approval, only passports.
Quotes BFF vice-president Fahad Karim saying the work is tough but they will proceed keeping June 10 in mind and try their best, targeting the next match if June fails.
Tells former and current players opposing expatriates that they strengthened the syndicate and lined their pockets through politics instead of developing football.
Fan post saying the dream is about to come true.
Reports Farzad Aftab made Bangladesh's preliminary squad for the U19 SAFF, with the coaching staff satisfied by his dribbling, speed and vision.
Says Aminul Haque always has an itch about origin players and should build an academy with his own money, as great players elsewhere do, instead of just talking.

Satirical special warning ahead of a match alleging a club's players import foreign liquor from the Maldives and thugs were hired to spread violence at the stadium, mocking a corporate group's land grabs and corruption.
Hypes Fahamidul Islam as the next focus after Hamza and Samit, saying a Rakib-Fahamidul wing duo could end the goal drought in the June 10 Singapore match.
Notes India has bid to host the 2031 Asian Cup and says co-hosting such an event would boost Bangladesh football.
Calls it disappointing not to beat India in Shillong, India's weakest team in years, but says the exposed weaknesses matter and the Singapore, Hong Kong and home India matches will show improvement.
Shares a Daily Star interview where Jamal Bhuyan says Hamza's presence does not threaten his position, since under Cabrera he played as a wide midfielder or No. 10, not Hamza's role.
Fan post saying 'Our Bangladesh.'
Says after becoming Transfermarkt champions he was sure they would post about Bangladesh, and it started with Samit Shome.
Fan post cheering the Black and White Warriors entering the stadium in style.
Attacks self-styled gentlemen who lecture against expatriates, saying they fear losing commissions from placing players and run propaganda from inside Bashundhara, Abahani and other clubs.
Celebrates that Rakib Hossain finally scored a goal.
Fan post saying 'Boss in action' with a party emoji.
Notes a red card means Kings will have to play with ten men.
Praises a talented young player called Junior Topu and asks someone to send him to Europe for a trial for a few months.
Celebrates Souleymane Diabate's goal as Mohammedan beat Bashundhara Kings 2-1.
Mocks Bashundhara's Rimon Hossain, once a striker turned right-back, who was sent off with a red card after a long layoff yet will still be put in the June Asia Cup qualifiers squad by the syndicate.
Praises Souleymane Diabate's superb finish and wishes BFF's vice-president would manage him with the professionalism shown in handling Samit Shome.
Fan asks whether viewers could mistake a photo for a ground in Bangladesh at first glance.
Asks whether captain Jamal Bhuyan will be lost amid the arrivals of Hamza and Samit.
Says the match was maneuvered from February to April, but off-field influence cannot touch on-field performance, and people will remember Diabate's name.
Reports table-topping Mohammedan beat Bashundhara 2-1 away with Palestine and Mohammedan flags, reaching 30 points from 11 matches ahead of Abahani on 26 and Bashundhara on 20.
Alleges the referee gave 12 minutes for Bashundhara to score, calling it the referee syndicate for the Kings.
Asks BFF to move the June youth trials to June 15-17 to avoid Dhaka traffic, since roads are empty for days after Qurbani Eid around the June 10 Singapore match.

Long attack on Oscar Bruzon's Bashundhara legacy: no core local group, wing-dependent football, sacked only for clashing with a management-close official, while Robinho and Miguel fled and the stadium sits empty.
Headline post on the story of Bashundhara Kings' downfall.
Asks how a management can be so bad that a keeper like Srabon gets a place while a keeper like Zico sits out.
Declares Mohammedan is returning to glory.
Praises Al Amin's superb position sense, saying he would score more if he got the ball at the right time.
Shares a news link that Mohammedan won an important match, brightening their title dreams after beating ten-man Bashundhara Kings.
Praises the Mohammedan Ultras at Kings Arena for their royal entry, huge flags, outsanging Bashundhara fans and protecting their players when a bottle was thrown at Sujan.
Says the country's best goalkeeper Srabon sank his team once again.
An Abahani fan declares 'today, we all are Mohammedan', saying he was happier at Bashundhara's defeat than Abahani's win and wants Mohammedan to win the league and play in Asia.
Notes these posts are now appearing on Rantages Goatposting and asks where footballers will seek justice and how they will play.
Shares a video of superstar Hamza Choudhury's feelings about representing the Bangladesh national team.
Fan post saying 'Performance 0%, Attitude 100%' with a clown emoji.
A fan with cold, fever and headache still went to the ground with Tariq bhai to cheer Mohammedan on, confident the club would win.
Says when Bashundhara first signed Sohel in 2022 he knew Sohel Rana would trouble the national team for years.
Appreciates a club president directly listening to fans and their complaints, saying direct dialogue can be effective for the club.
Emoji-only fan post.
Jokes that the biryani should have more meat next match because the portion does not fill the stomach, or he will not come to the ground.
Asks whether it is not yet time to think about Diabate.
Scoffs that even a lame neighbourhood pick-up player has played for the national team, thrown into defence whether he can play or not, protected by a big club.
Fan sarcastically asks what the heroism is in a shared post.

Long analysis that Asian club inexperience hurts the national team, noting Lion City Sailors beat Sydney FC while Bashundhara fell to the third tier, and arguing quality expatriates plus sacking Cabrera is the way out.
Notes Hamza Dewan Choudhury's market value was 10 million euros in 2019.
Calls Bangladesh's press resistance the worst he has ever seen, saying the team panics and loses the ball against legit teams like Australia and two players cannot fix it.
Asks whether Kolkata Mohammedan and Bashundhara Kings are playing tomorrow.
Asks whether Hamza, Samit Shome and Fahamidul will ever play together in Cabrera's team.
Vague post saying BFF should pay attention to these matters.
Tells fans to watch MLS Next player Farzad Aftab at the upcoming U19 SAFF Championship for his dribbling, speed and sudden long-range shots.
Asks whether Fahamidul will no longer be kept in the national team and predicts 12 or 13 of the 23 will come from Bashundhara Kings while Sohel Rana and Chandon Roy survive.
Fan post saying 'Mood Right Now' with ninja and shushing emojis.
Says irrational decisions cost Bangladesh victory against India, proving the coach's incompetence, and demands an immediate coaching change.

Long history asking whether Dhaka Mohammedan, South Asia's best club in Asian football history with a 75-match unbeaten league run and three top-tier Asian qualifications, is returning to Asian football.
Profiles talented young origin footballer Neil Das, 18, at Jefferson Men's Soccer after DC United U-16.
Claims Jamal was dropped from the team because coach Cabrera did not like him.
Alleges a player in the 2024 U17 SAFF was 19 or older and had reduced his age, withholding his name, and says this age-fraud culture mostly runs in Bangladesh football.
Calls on Mohammedan Sporting Club to take initiative now to take over the Savar land.
Says fans dreaming Fahamidul Islam will be called to the national team in June are completely wrong and asks whether BFF officials notice how far the syndicate has gone.
Fan says in Hindi he cannot abuse someone because he is a Kings fan.

Recounts Cuba Mitchell telling a press conference he is partly Bangladeshi through his mother, never playing at the U20 World Cup and skipping Jamaica call-ups, and urges BFF to get his passport done fast.
Asks whether Fahamidul will no longer be seen in the red-green jersey.
Asks who runs Bangladesh football and argues Rahmat Mia and Saad Uddin are not genuine defenders, lacking the height and physicality defenders need.
Urges everyone to unite against the syndicate and take to the field, saying either the syndicate stays or football stays.
Shows the poor condition of the pitch the national team practices on, saying he has no words.
Fan idiom post implying someone pretends innocence, like one who cannot even flip a fried fish.
Decodes a Kalbela report naming Topu Barman, Sohel Rana and Saad Uddin as the leaders of the syndicate that bullied Fahamidul out of the team, sidelining Taj, Isa Faisal, Kazem Shah and Jamal.
Notes former national footballer and Fortis FC manager Rashed bhai watched Fahamidul Islam's match from the ground, tagged #Bringbackfahmedul.
Shares a post on Samit Shome's fitness.
Praises Rashed bhai for fighting with all his might hoping for Bangladesh football's improvement.
Asks football lovers to give love to Rashedul bhai, saying however far the road, love is always near.
Notes Fahamid said on T Sports he has good relations with everyone, a video released a day after Kalbela's clear syndicate report, and thanks journalists who covered the story.
Fan asks how the guy in the black T-shirt is doing currently.
Accuses T Sports of using Rashed bhai to make Fahamid say he has good relations with everyone, right after Kalbela's syndicate news.
Says Fahamidul is a footballer of another level whose demeanour will move fans emotionally.
Says many are trying to bury the bomb that exploded over the Fahamidul issue, but it is clear a club's syndicate players and management are behind the cover-up.
Urges BFF to call Anwar Uddin, former England C team coach and West Ham player, as Bangladesh team coach.

Attacks T Sports' mind game of taking credit for Rashed bhai's Italy video of Fahamidul, noting Navil and Rifat began the first propaganda against Fahamidul while Kalbela worked hard on the syndicate story.
Link-only fan post sharing a Facebook video.
Taunts Navil Khan for turning off his comment box, saying he has sunk so low he does not dare keep comments open.
Quotes Rashedul Islam saying every player of Fahamidul's team is worthy of Bangladesh's best XI.
Summarises Rashedul Islam's praise of Fahamidul and demands Cabrera be sacked for a proven coach under neutral staff answerable to Tabith Awal, after multiple outlets proved the syndicate.
Thanks Rashed bhai for watching Fahamidul's match in Italy and says he asked Olbia Calcio's president about trial chances for other Bangladeshis, hoping Hamza, Samit and Fahamidul all play in June.
Notes the similarity between Hamza Dewan Choudhury and sprinter Imranur Rahman, both Sylhetis living in Sheffield where Hamza plays for Sheffield United.
Praises Khela Joga and hopes T Sports' eyewash attempt does not succeed.

Fan asks what the syndicate achieved by dropping Elita Kingsley, noting no qualifier group-stage win since 2013 and the last significant opponent beaten in 1989 against Thailand, while eleven corners against Singapore produced nothing.
Fan says the Robson issue is being raised to make people forget Cabrera, insisting he will not do and now is the time for everyone to raise their voice.

Fan recalls going alone to Kolkata for the Bangladesh-India match, where his friend Hrisav Bhowmick gave him a ticket and Indians were surprised but said nothing at his cheering, and asks that no one beat a supporter like Tiger Shoaib.
Fan says Cabrera is a bad coach, and the bigger problem is he is not a full-time coach, warning a seasonal coach will destroy Bangladesh.

Fan says fake news is a good business now, with everyone acting like Romano and football experts, creating confusion among ordinary people while pages run by so-called experts keep approving such posts.

Fan suggests Gary White as national team coach, who lifted Hong Kong, Chinese Taipei and Guam, costs 250-400 thousand dollars a year and is currently a free agent, urging president Tabith Awal to consider him and a technical director.
Fan cuts his list to four coaches and asks Tabith Awal whom he will bring: Kim Pan-gon of South Korea, Simon McMenemy, Nelo Vingada as a dream technical director, or Gary White.
Fan shares news of preparation to change the grass, with all football events at the National Stadium suspended.

Fan warns BFF not to catch the clubs' coaching disease, recounting how Abahani, Mohammedan, Sheikh Jamal and Bashundhara all hired budget or syndicate-chosen coaches, and argues Hamza and Shamit deserve a much better coach who will not bow to the syndicate.
Fan posts 'Alhamdulillah' with a heart emoji.
Fan says the coach's failure is complete in all sixteen arts, and it is surprising he still holds the job after such performances, since no Bangladesh coach survived so long after failing.

Fan says when the match was under Bangladesh's control and Singapore's defence was being torn apart, officials struggled to make a substitution, first sending the wrong number and then not deciding whom to take off, damaging the team's spirit.
Fan quotes National Teams Committee member Shakhawat Hossain Bhuiya saying he is seeking Cabrera's resignation to free 180 million Bangladeshis, and removing Cabrera is his only agenda.

Fan thanks National Teams Committee member Shakhawat Hossain Bhuiya Shaheen, saying the people's demand of 180 million is to dismiss academy coach baby Pep Cabrera, which he stated directly before the press, media and federation.
Fan shares senior sports journalist Mozammel Haque Chanchal's question about Mahfuza Akter Kiron and BFF president Tabith Awal's answer.
Fan shares senior sports journalist Mozammel Haque Chanchal's question about Mahfuza Akter Kiron and BFF president Tabith Awal's answer.
Fan posts 'Respect' with saluting emojis.
Fan says Shaheen has caught the frog's son, with frog emojis.
Fan says Shaheen has spoken the words in the hearts of 180 million people.
Fan shares a post-Singapore match analysis with Rahik Sumail on YouTube.
Fan posts satirical breaking news that the Club World Cup has no spectator interest and FIFA is adding a special Group X with four wildcard teams, citing joke sources like Ditiyo Alo and Channel 69.
Fan says bro woke up and chose to speak facts, with respect.

Fan says Khelajog, Riasad Azim, Deb Chowdhury and Not Out Noman do not want football's good, only views, likes, comments and controversy, and urges people to boycott and report their content before football follows cricket's ruin.
Fan notes the day after the match, Khelajog discussed Cabrera's 'best striker' theory, which the group had already written about.
Fan says beautiful clear words.
Fan shows how Khelajog spreads propaganda, captioning expatriate Bangladeshi players as foreign players simply because they play in outside leagues, deliberately creating a division.
Fan posts a transfer signing alert.

Fan says it is interesting that Tabith Awal claims he first raised dual citizenship with FIFA in 2016 at the Singapore congress, when he was BFF vice-president and in charge of the National Team Committee.
Fan shares Samit Shome's brilliant performance against HFX Wanderers.

Fan says the Philippines Football Association is bringing 15 top-class origin players onto the national radar for their October AFC Asian Cup qualifier, including four or five playing in Major League Soccer.
Fan quotes BFF president Tabith Awal in Dhaka Post saying those willing to play for Bangladesh will get a chance, with merit and ability checked and the best players getting the jersey.
Fan says even ChatGPT does not want Cabrera as coach, and ChatGPT even named who could be Bangladesh's national team coach.

Fan explains why they keep talking about Al-Amin, showing his positioning between two defenders and movement to draw a through pass from Shamit, and says the syndicate and Cabrera deliberately played games with him at every step, giving him only 15 minutes against Singapore.

Fan says for the September window only Gibraltar, Malta and San Marino are available among European teams, noting San Marino beat Liechtenstein who beat Hong Kong, and urges BFF to act fast or try brave options like Albania and North Macedonia.
Fan asks why Samit Shome came onto the field wearing the Canadian flag alongside his own country's flag on his chest.
Fan debunks a fake rumour, saying Irish league player Al-Amin Kazim was born in Nigeria and moved to England at five, with no relation to Bangladesh.

Fan laments the state of the first division league, asking when an AFC-standard professional league will be made, and suggests following Malaysia, Indonesia or Japan's league structure with area-based teams.
Fan says Tariq needs to move to a quality overseas league.
Fan says despite tight security inside the field, several thousand spectators broke the gate outside and entered the stadium.

Fan says media hype matters for expatriates' decision-making, recalling Shamit Shome came two years ago unknown to most, and arguing the hype they gave him helped convince him to choose Bangladesh, with Hamza playing a big role.
Fan says as far as he knows, Shaheen is Tabith Awal's close man, even his right hand, handling everything from Feni Soccer to NoFeL Sporting Club, and asks what happened suddenly.

Fan shares a 2019 photo of Tariq Kazi celebrating the Finnish Cup at 18 with Tampereen Ilves, saying Jamie Day called him and he gave up a promising European career because of the unwritten rule that playing for Bangladesh meant playing in the local league.
Fan asks if Bangladesh cannot fill the goal void unless a good striker joins the team.

Fan says football was very popular once, the craze moved to cricket in the late 90s, and after 25-30 years it is moving back to national football, asking why neither sport improves internationally and sharing a video on the cancer in their structure and culture.

Fan says listen from 16:00 to 17:05, saying he was never for a franchise league after seeing cricket's state, and Bangladesh need clubs from divisional cities like Sylhet and Chittagong brought into the BCL by any means.
Fan says they have patience, it must be said.

Fan says the Tabith Awal and Fahad Karim board is doing a lot of good work, but they do not listen to people on Cabrera or player selection, and reminds them fans found Hamza and Samit five to six years ago, so the board's credit is only the paperwork.

Fan tells honourable BFF directors that fans do not want to enjoy the game or one point, they want three points, citing Cabrera's record of 9 wins, 7 draws and 16 losses in 32 matches with 23 goals scored and 47 conceded.
Fan says domestic league clubs will be able to take origin footballers from the trials in the last week of June.

Fan says Karim Hasan Smith cannot play for Bangladesh, since under FIFA's eligibility rule a player, parent or grandparent must be born in the country, and none of his family with links to Bangladesh, Jamaica, Somalia and England was born in Bangladesh.
Fan says the one everyone had their eyes on for the upcoming trials is heartbroken.

Fan says Karim Hasan Smith's case is unfortunate but a chance remains, since playing five years in the BPL would let him naturalise like Elita, and at just 22 he could come to the BPL and do very well if fit.
Fan says Mirajul Islam Rahul should leave his club to get more game time, since he could be a big asset for the national team.
Fan shares a rumour that fast right winger Rakib Hossain, one of Bashundhara Kings' best performers, may join Dhaka Abahani next season.

Fan says Karim Hasan Smith himself clarified he cannot represent Bangladesh, since FIFA's rule requires a parent or grandparent to be born in Bangladesh and none of his parents or grandparents were, though his great-grandfather was Bangladeshi.
Fan praises an outstanding finish by Ronan Sullivan.
Fan shares a Dhaka Post story tagged Cuba Mitchell and Hamza Choudhury.
Fan says Karim Hasan Smith wants to follow Elita's path, meaning naturalisation through playing in Bangladesh.
Fan says Topu Barman is the best at scoring with headers.

Fan asks how many more failures it will take for the officials to wake up, saying the coach's profile is weaker than the players' and asking how many more matches must be lost before Cabrera is sacked.
Fan announces Al-Amin has joined Abahani for the 25/26 season.

Fan profiles 17-year-old Newcastle U18 left-back Jake Durrant, who played 15 matches with one assist in the Premier League Cup and carries Bangladeshi blood through his mother, urging BFF to plan for him for the AFC U-23 Asian Cup qualifiers.

Fan laments that while Hamza, Samit and Jamal are talked about everywhere, Nawab and Rahbar, once names of dreams and possibility, were lost in the syndicate's shadow and neglect, and asks if anyone thinks about bringing them back.
Fan asks if there is any update on Trevor Islam.
Fan calls Nawab and Yusuf Zulqarnain two lost stars.
Fan reports a transfer update that Abahani have signed Police FC's Al Amin Islam.

Fan says Denmark-based Sakib Mahmud is coordinating BFF's open trial for origin footballers in Dhaka at the end of the month, with about 48 players over three days for the U17, U19, U23 and senior teams, all paying their own costs, and he is also working to place women footballers in Danish clubs.

Fan says most transfer rumours from new pages are unrealistic, noting Mohammedan's old football committee chairman resigned and no new committee has formed, yet people claim they are signing Rakib, Zico and Morsalin from Bashundhara.
Fan says Tariq, Rakib and Zico are staying at Bashundhara Kings.
Fan says Bashundhara Kings are working to sign Bangladeshi-origin footballer Zayn Hakeem.

Fan defends Zayn Hakeem, noting his hat-trick for Antigua U20 and that he last played for their senior team in 2023 when Antigua ranked 132-142 and Bangladesh 192, and that playing more for Antigua would have ended his chance to switch.
Fan says watch Zayn Hakeem's goals, his finishing is good and that is what Bangladesh needs.
Fan says BFF's professional league committee is about to decide to have no relegation in order to increase the number of clubs in the upcoming league.

Fan accuses champions Mohammedan of still not paying their local players' due wages while foreign players were paid in full, calling it discrimination and saying the local pipeline must be fixed before hunting for the next Hamza or Samit.
Fan shares a Sunderland Echo link about Cuba Mitchell's transfer.
Fan notes India lead hosts Tajikistan 1-0 at half-time in a U23 friendly ahead of September's U-23 Asian Cup qualifiers and asks what Bangladesh's news is.

Fan accuses the Dhaka and Chittagong syndicates of lasting damage, saying a coach who wrecked the BFF Elite Academy's second team by bringing in 8 Chittagong and 4 Brahmanbaria players is nearly appointed U23 coach for September, and suggests Peter Butler or Maruful Haque instead.

Fan shares Cuba Mitchell's interview saying he left Sunderland, his Bangladesh registration was a couple of hours late so he must wait until October, and he is definitely considering a move abroad to find the right pathway.
Fan argues June trial players in good foreign leagues should stay abroad to improve their skills, and local clubs should instead produce better quality players and help them get chances overseas.
Fan cheers Cuba with fire emojis.
Fan says the league champions cannot pay players' salaries while more teams are being added, predicting fixed points will follow and telling readers to save the post.
Fan says it is officially confirmed Hamza Choudhury is going on loan again, this time to a top Greek club playing in UEFA competitions, after proving his class in the Premier League and Championship.
Fan says BFF vice-president Fahad Karim spoke with Niloy's agent last night about when he should come to Bangladesh, what process to follow, and which tournament he can join the team for.

Fan says he warned before Hamza arrived that results would only change with Shamit and a striker too, and that the syndicate's Cabrera is wasting the chance while Sri Lanka and India remain better balanced on paper.

Fan argues for including Cuba in the U23 team since the Asian Cup is a distant hope but the U23 Asian Cup in Vietnam is the closest success, needing just three wins, and says Cuba, Arham, Niloy and Tanil are booked while Morsalin, Al-Amin and Fahmidul must also be included.
Fan says BFF wants to play Zayn Hakeem in October, has already collected all possible documents for his passport, and is contacting the relevant people to complete the process.
Fan announces Mission Zayn Hakeem is on, with BFF about to start all the procedures to play him in a Bangladesh jersey.
Fan announces Mission Zayn Hakeem is on, with BFF about to start all the procedures to play him in a Bangladesh jersey.
Fan says this is what they expect from Navil bhai, and hopes such news comes from him regularly before the supporters.

Fan cites T Sports that Abahani's AFC Challenge League home match is in Sylhet against Kyrgyz club Muras United and Bashundhara's away match is against Syria's second representative, and predicts both will lose the playoff, offering to eat biryani and post a selfie if either wins.
Fan says Zayn Hakeem will be a big blessing and warns not to discard him after two matches like Elita, arguing he should be judged after 12-15 matches with 5-7 goals and two competitive wins.
Fan says the water incident felt very bad and they could not understand why such a thing was done with water.

Fan slams BFF committee members for saying Cabrera will stay until the Hong Kong match when the India match is just a month after Hong Kong's two games, warning that by the time he is sacked everything will be destroyed.
Fan shares a market value update that Mitul Marma's value rose 25,000 euros to 200,000 euros at Abahani Ltd.
Fan says a sad picture of grassroots football comes through in the voice of the goalkeeper who became champion for Rangpur division.
Fan asks if there is any update on Nawab, Yusuf and Arham.
Fan asks when Zayn Hakeem will be seen in a Bangladesh jersey, says they want Cuba Mitchell in the national team in September rather than the U23s, and asks for a Niloy Van der Ploeg update.
Fan asks where Sandata is now.

Fan says 6'2 Zayn Hakeem, 6'1 Niloy Van der Ploeg and 6' Cuba Mitchell are technically and physically superb, recalling Singapore had five six-footers while Bangladesh had only Topu and conceded the first goal from a set piece, and wants all three in the September window.

Fan argues September's U23 Asian Cup qualifiers matter more than the national team's FIFA friendly, since the U23 Asian Cup is also an Olympic qualifier, and wants Cuba, Niloy, Fahmidul, Fahim, Morsalin and Mitul in the U23 squad.
Fan asks why Karim Hasan Smith is not coming to the trials and whether that is his last way to play for Bangladesh.
Fan challenges others to show a better squad than this one if they want to be group champions.
Fan asks what the state of Abahani's sports complex is and how far the work has progressed.
Fan shares a 4-3-1-2 lineup and says it might just be Bangladesh's strongest future lineup yet, asking what others think.

Fan says if BFF sends Cuba, Niloy and Fahmidul to the U23 qualifiers they must also send Mitul, Shakil Ahad, Morsalin, Al-Amin and Nova, warning that splitting players between the two windows will leave both sides failing.
Fan says making Choton coach would cause a fight, and David Gomez or Butler would be the perfect choice.

Fan says Nawab and Fahmidul play the same position so choosing Nawab means dropping Fahmidul, and with only 11 on the field and 23 in the squad the team needs depth and more origin players in the league.
Fan says BFF could have given group admin Arefin Zeesan a chance.

Fan says Saiful Bari Titu and Julfikar Mahmud Mintu are the most honest and capable local coaches and wants them for the Olympic or U23 team, saying no other local coach builds bonding between origin and homegrown players like them.
Fan says Bashundhara Kings, the country's only professional club, has not paid former coach Tita or even his flight ticket, claiming it has no money, and he may complain to FIFA.

Fan praises BFF's U23 planning with a 4-6 week camp and Bahrain friendlies, says Peter Butler would be best as coach or Titu himself, and argues Fahmidul and Cuba should play the September friendly with the national team to build combinations instead of being swapped around.

Fan shares a long philosophy post arguing Bangladesh's sporting failure has deeper causes than corruption, from farmers' physique and low meat consumption to British-era famines, and says individual sports should be targeted for an Olympic medal.

Fan says BFF is about to make the right decision, moving Cabrera to the Elite Academy until his contract ends on 31 March 2026 while a new national team head coach is searched for in July and takes charge in August.
Fan celebrates Abdur Rahman Alif winning gold in the men's recurve at the Asia Cup archery in Singapore, beating Japan's Gakuto Miyata 6-4 in the final.
Fan mockingly calls winger Fahim the khyap master.
Fan says national team winger Fahim is dominating khyap matches and argues Bashundhara not paying him forced him into khyap out of need, so nobody should blame him.
Fan says they want this pitch design for Dhaka National Stadium after the new grass is laid.
Fan jokes that pre-season khyap star and one of Bangladesh's best left wingers Faysal Ahmed Fahim is also known as Nicolas Jackson.
Fan says guess who's back again, tagging Hamza Choudhury and Leicester City.

Fan wants a new head coach in July on a six-month contract to December, Cabrera kept at the Elite Academy until March 2026 and coaching the U23 qualifiers in September, and Malta as the European opponent that month.
Fan shares former footballer Jahid Hasan Emily's view that match reading is crucial, Cabrera's match reading was weak in several internationals, and now is the best time for BFF to change the coach.

Fan welcomes BFF's new technical director Lodewijk de Kruif, noting he was positive about origin and naturalised players, tried to take local talents like Hemanta Vincent to Europe, and has been a member of this group for 11 years.

Fan calls Lodewijk de Kruif the torchbearer who opened the door to origin players by bringing Jamal Bhuyan in 2013, raised naturalisation of foreign league players, and now returns as technical director after coaching the national team in 2013-14 and 2015-16.

Fan calls Lodewijk de Kruif their all-time favourite coach, saying he thought most about origin players, tried to get locals into foreign leagues and naturalise three players, but BFF never gave him a long contract for lack of money.
Fan posts crying, heart and Bangladesh flag emojis.
Fan says Jeremy Faruk on this list is still playing professional football and his profile is rich enough for the national team, leaving the rest to BFF or the coach.

Fan says Bangladesh is the only country where someone becomes a fan favourite without notable performance, arguing amateurs who worked three stints like daily labour should not decide how the federation runs or pick a technical director for Hamza and Samit.

Fan praises de Kruif for bringing quality origin players like Jamal and Joseph Noor, never compromising on substandard ones, sending Hemanta to a Netherlands trial, and arranging the Sylhet academy deal with the Dutch ambassador, while warning the current committee to settle his salary first.

Fan recounts de Kruif's three stints since June 2012, from beating Nepal and Mariana Islands in AFC Challenge Cup qualifiers and the U19 win over Kuwait to his September 2014 sacking with Rene Costa, and hopes his new role as technical director goes differently.
Fan says Austrian player of Bangladeshi origin Simon Ershad is coming to the June trials for the Bangladesh U17 team.
Fan asks what the basic job of a technical director is and how urgent it is in Bangladesh's context.

Fan says the league committee has no plan for the Premier League at the National Stadium due to renovation and maintenance, though Federation Cup and Super Cup matches may be held there, while the Challenge Cup will be at league champions Mohammedan's home venue.
Fan wishes Bangladesh had the courage to take this opportunity.
Fan says they searched everywhere for a U23 lineup, could not find one, so made one themselves, and asks if the rest is right since they only need a left-back and a centre-back.

Fan quotes Bangladesh's top international scorer Ashrafuddin Ahmed Chunnu backing origin players and urging Cuba Mitchell be brought quickly, and blaming Mitul Marma for both goals conceded against Singapore.
Fan jokes there will be a fight over who plays in the striker position.

Fan bids farewell to Quinn Sullivan, saying his appearance for the US against Haiti in the Gold Cup group stage cap-tied him to the US and ended his eligibility to switch nationality under FIFA rules.
Fan asks what a coach candidate's profile is like and whether BFF can afford him.

Fan says Quinn Sullivan playing the Gold Cup against Haiti leaves no chance for Bangladesh, expects Cavan for Germany, Quinn for the US and Ronan and Declan for Bangladesh, and notes Nabil Irfan will also be lost once he plays the 2026 Asia Cup for Qatar.

Fan tells people posting about Zidan Mia every two days to send him to this month's open trial, saying paid training at Rayo Vallecano's academy does not make a good footballer and if he does not come he is a fraud.
Fan asks what the real job description of a technical director in Bangladesh football is.
Fan asks who actually takes the trials and whether the syndicate could drop good players, noting very good players are coming this time.
Fan suggests BFF check whether trial-bound Iman Alam could be considered for the futsal team, saying his dribbling clips are literally insane and he shows futsal potential.
Fan asks why BFF removed this post.

Fan profiles 17-year-old Newcastle U18 left-back Jake Durrant, who played 15 matches with one assist in the Premier League Cup and carries Bangladeshi blood through his mother, urging BFF to plan for him for the AFC U-23 Asian Cup qualifiers.
Fan says Nawab deserves a chance, recalling sitting by the TV waiting to watch Nawab's Nawabi.

Fan recounts coach Edson Silva Dido's 2006-2009 era, when a 20-match winless streak ended with debutants beating Cambodia and qualifying for the AFC Challenge Cup, contrasting Dido's discipline and legacy with Cabrera, whom he calls the syndicate's puppet sabotaging Bangladesh football.

Fan says Nawab was warned not to come to Bangladesh or join Bashundhara, hid an injury, and chose the club for money and its syndicate under coach Oscar, and now cannot make the playing XI with his fitness level.
Fan asks which country's player Taj Uddin is.
Fan posts Tofael Tanim with a Bangladesh flag, tagging origin football.
Fan profiles Serbian coach Milovan Rajevac, who took Ghana to the 2010 AFCON final and World Cup quarter-final, arguing his defensive strategy and youth development could help Bangladesh.
Fan suggests forming a futsal team from the trial, captained by Rahabar Wahed Khan, since the trials may find skilful talents better suited to futsal ahead of the AFC Futsal Asian Cup qualifiers.
Fan says wonder kid Iman Alam and his cousin Ifaz Abed are on their way to Bangladesh and will arrive tomorrow.
Fan says the Mamuds' business is about to close, arguing if Bhutan or Nepal national team players can be got with local money, why take substandard locals, and whatever BFF decides is final.
Fan reports several origin footballers coming for BFF's trials are stuck in the Middle East, with at least seven confirmed in Qatar and elsewhere, as war has disrupted airspace and transit.
Fan says BFF contacted Afghanistan, Yemen and Chinese Taipei in Asia for the September FIFA window, and Bangladesh has been invited to play Nepal and Sri Lanka at their venues.
Fan says Malaysia-based Tamzid Rahman is coming to Bangladesh for the June trials and, like Iman Alam, could be considered for the futsal team.
Fan says Singapore's national team head coach has resigned, leaving the Singapore FA in trouble at an important time in the Asia Cup qualifiers.

Fan reports breaking news that BFF proposed FIFA friendlies to seven European countries for the September window, listing Faroe Islands, Lithuania, Moldova, Malta, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein and San Marino with their FIFA rankings.

Fan argues BFF should play Sri Lanka's four-nation tournament in September with Hamza and Samit, and play Lithuania at home in November before the India match, while giving the U23 Asian Cup qualifiers top priority.

Fan supports BFF's proposal to allow eight foreign players in a league XI with five from SAFF countries, arguing local players must compete and citing Saudi Arabia, Malaysia and Kyrgyzstan's expanded foreign quotas.
Fan says 6'2 Ikramul Casper Haque, of English, Russian and Lithuanian origin, is now in Bangladesh for the trials.

Fan says two of Navil Khan's stories face challenges, on the AFC Challenge League playoff draw and Lodewijk de Kruif's appointment, but adds the newly published AFC fixture supports Navil's news on the playoffs.
Fan announces the group will be temporarily hidden and posting suspended for members as a precaution after reports that some Facebook groups are being disabled due to a bug.

Fan recalls this day in 2019 when Dhaka Abahani advanced in the AFC Cup with four wins and a draw in six matches, finishing ahead of ISL champions Chennaiyin, I-League champions Minerva Punjab and Nepal champions MMC.

Fan says Indonesia, then Malaysia, now Vietnam are becoming World Cup-qualifying teams, and urges Bangladesh to allow dual citizenship so foreigners can keep their own passport, since not everyone will give theirs up like Elita.

Fan says the trials are about recognising origin players' right to play for Bangladesh, expects only seven or eight to make the U17 to U23 teams, and praises Titu's eye for talent, noting he invited Jamal after seeing his video.
Fan posts the AFC Futsal Asian Cup Qualifiers Group G draw of Iran, Malaysia as hosts, UAE and Bangladesh.
Fan says Bangladesh face a tough test on their futsal debut against Iran and Malaysia, with no alternative to good preparation.
Fan announces that from now anyone can post in the group and the wall has been opened.

Fan describes a huge crowd at the final match in Nagarpur, Tangail, saying football in Bangladesh's villages is an emotion and a cultural madness, and dreams the national team will one day play the World Cup.

Fan wants Bangladesh in Sri Lanka's four-nation tournament in September with Zayn Hakeem in the national team, and lists a dream U23 squad for the Asian Cup qualifiers against Singapore, Vietnam and Yemen, calling it the strongest and most balanced in a decade.
Fan asks for an update on Swiss-based Safwan Kazi, who came to Bangladesh for a trial in 2022 with deadly foot skills.

Fan says BFF's three-day trials start tomorrow and urges a transparent process, a U23 team formed by mid-July, and a 40-45 day residential camp at BKSP ahead of the U23 Asian Cup qualifiers from 1 to 10 September.
Fan asks the trial selectors to find one or two free-kick specialists if possible, saying it will be useful.
Fan asks to name the biggest wonder boy in the photo, a youth national team player of a Nordic country.
Fan says veteran English manager Sean Dyche, formerly of Everton, Burnley and Nottingham, is leading the race to become Hamza's coach.
Fan says Sweden's Messi, Taseen, should be called to Bangladesh's youth national team as soon as possible.
Fan says this player cannot be put in a car because of his great physique, and if his quality is right he should be called for national duty since such a player is much needed.
Fan notes Bangladeshi striker Zayn Hakeem is at Barwell Football Club's pre-season camp.
Fan announces the inauguration of the Kutubdia Kriangan Football Academy in Kutubdia upazila, Cox's Bazar, calling it a historic day for Kutubdia sports.
Fan reports massive news that Sweden U15 national team player Taseen Hossain is in BFF's future plans.
Fan says the tide of origin footballers is sweeping Bangladesh football.
Fan calls Trevor Islam another future star of Bangladesh from Stanford Men's Soccer.

Fan profiles seven promising young wingers, from Fulham's Farhan Ali Wahid with seven goals and three assists in 17 matches to Sweden U15 call-up Taseen Hossain, saying Bangladesh's wings are safe for the next dozen years.

Fan accuses BFF executive committee member and Mohammedan official Manjurul Karim of already knowing at most ten players will pass the trials, mocking him as a football astrologer seated between Cabrera and Fahad Karim.
Fan says now is the ideal time to organise futsal properly, suggesting a tournament before the qualifiers with 15 or 20 teams that could finish in three weeks.

Fan wants two pairs of twin brothers in the U23 team, Ronan and Declan Sullivan plus Swedish-based nephews Ashik and Onik, and proposes a 35-man camp from mid-July narrowing to a final 23 with Cuba, Niloy and Fahmidul added.

Fan says Fulham U21's Sri Lankan-origin talent Seth Kai Rizon is being chased by Liverpool and Manchester City, and imagines him facing Man City's American-Bangladeshi wonder Cavan Sullivan in the 2028 Premier League season.
Fan complains a fitness-less player gets the wonder kid title in Bangladesh, while tested talents like Fahmidul, Yusuf, Nawab and Arham are left helpless before these khyap goods.

Fan rants that journalists, Ultras and BFF ruined the players' focus before the Singapore match, from reporters asking about Hamza's cow and prayers to BFF's free promotions and Ultras fasting for tickets, exposing the Fahad Karim versus Imrul Hasan rivalry.

entities.name: FIH U21 Men's Hockey World Cup

posts.summary: Fan posts the FIH U21 Men's Hockey World Cup 2025 Group F draw of France, Australia, South Korea and Bangladesh, to be played in India in November-December.
Fan shares an effortless stunning goal by Sweden U16 player Taseen Hossain, noting the goalkeeper was a Bangladeshi local player.
Fan notes three Bangladeshi players are in FIFA 19, Hamza Choudhury at Leicester City, Shamit Shome at Montreal Impact and Zayn Hakeem at Mansfield Town.

Fan calls Taseen Hossain the future of Bangladesh football, noting the Sweden U15 winger now in Bangladesh plays for Djurgardens IF, whose senior side reached the UEFA Conference League semi-final this season.
Fan asks what Manjurul Karim is doing among the coaches and how transparent the trial process can be with people like him involved.
Fan bids farewell to the group, saying it shaped his Ultras spirit and roadmap from 2014 to 2019 and thanking mentor Arefin Zeesan and Kazi Sajib, but leaves rather than stand against the group.
Fan says those who earlier behaved discriminatorily or commented against origin players have been honoured with places on the trial selection panel.
Fan mockingly calls the dear faces all together with clown emojis, apparently about the officials gathered at the trials.

Fan calls the trials a gathering of origin-player-hating coaches, naming Golam Rabbani Choton, Alfaz Ahmed and syndicate pet Mahbub Roxy in the dugout with biased committee man Manjurul Karim, supervised by syndicate guru Cabrera and assistant Hasan Al Mamun.

Fan argues the Ultras' movement is unjust because there was no contract with BFF, explaining under the Contract Act 1872 that offer, acceptance, consideration and a judicial stamp are needed, and says standing before the BFF building with unjust demands hurt the players' focus.
Fan says a match should be organised between the national team and the origin players so the country's football situation can be understood.
Fan mocks Saeed Hasan Kanan for seeing fitness and technical deficiencies in the origin footballers who came for the trials.
Fan says some days the Bashundhara syndicate runs Bangladesh football and some days Mohammedan does, that is the situation.

Fan reports day one of BFF's Next Global Star trial, where 25 of 52 players showed their talent for the U23 team at the National Stadium in 28-degree heat that felt like 33, and notes observer Sayed Hasan Kanan doubted the players' fitness.

Fan says the national team craze came from Hamza, Samit, Cuba and Fahmidul, warns the trial players are mostly children of expatriates not yet at senior level, and fears syndicate brokers on the selection panel will downgrade them and pick lobbied amateurs.
Fan says if the Bangladesh team can move forward through this trial, that is what the people of the country want.

Fan replies to Arif's post recalling the Fahmidul protest before the India away match, when Deen Mohammad, Nayon Sorkar and Saiful Islam Jitu met president Tabith Awal, and accuses Arif of double standards and slow-poisoning the Ultras.

Fan asks whether you miss mycujoo to watch Bangladesh's football league matches in 2025, saying better a blind uncle than no uncle.
Post says media and content creators are busy with their view business around Hamza when the national team plays, while the league's Friday and Saturday matches were not broadcast at all.
Fan asks whether a football federation president can contest a mayor or MP election for a political party, and what FIFA's rules say.
Fan says two match days of the Bangladesh Football League ended yesterday with no match shown live, asking if the four cameras were kept inside BFF.
Fan asks why Bangladesh Football League matches cannot be watched live, demanding an answer from BFF.
Post asks which is Hamza's best moment of the year, inviting comments.
Fan jokes whether league matches will now be shown on TikTok.

Post says the syndicate wants to keep spectators away from football to hide its corruption and economic interests, which is why the coach is never changed and league broadcasts are stopped when criticised.
Post says after men's football, BFF also organised the worst broadcast in women's football.
Post reports Shamit Shome's contract with Cavalry FC is about to be renewed for another year, confirmed by journalist Abu Sadat.

incidents.title: Fans complain no channel shows Bangladesh matches as Asian Games go untelevised
incidents.summary: No TV channel or stream shows Bangladesh's Asian Games matches; fans ask if the country will ever get a sports channel.

incidents.title: Abahani humiliated in Bhutan as King's Cup campaign collapses
incidents.summary: Dhaka Abahani lose 1-0 to Bhutan's Ugyen Academy and stumble through the King's Cup in Bhutan; fans call it shameful and question why Abahani, not stronger clubs, were sent.

incidents.title: U16 girls lose to India after disputed penalty and red card as fans demand better support for women’s football
incidents.summary: Fans blame a penalty and red card for the U-16 girls’ 2-1 loss to India and urge BFF to give the women’s team proper training, facilities and regular matches.

incidents.title: Fans protest foreign-player quota as Sheikh Jamal benches local stars
incidents.summary: Sheikh Jamal sign Jamal Bhuiyan on 350,000 taka a month yet bench local players while foreigners play; fans demand BFF limit foreigners to two registered and one in the XI.

incidents.title: Foreign players crowd out locals as franchise plan allows seven imports
incidents.summary: Fans argue foreign players crowd out local talent in clubs and mock a franchise league plan allowing seven foreign players and only four locals per team.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Gold Cup 2015 hit by postponement, fixture clash and crowd trouble at the final
incidents.summary: Bahrain’s postponement, a Bangabandhu Cup reschedule clashing with Sheikh Russel’s AFC Cup playoff, Mamunul’s resignation threat and fans throwing shoes at the referee in the final.

incidents.title: Power cut blacks out the Gold Cup match for fans
incidents.summary: Fans complain a power cut during the Bangabandhu Gold Cup match left them unable to watch, and sarcastically thank the power department.

incidents.title: BFF arranges no friendlies as Asian rivals play qualifiers
incidents.summary: Fans note Bangladesh play no friendlies in March while Asian rivals play qualifiers, and ask BFF to arrange games against Uzbekistan, China or similar opposition.

incidents.title: League calendar chaos as BPL stops for tournaments and skips Fridays
incidents.summary: Fans attack BFF for stopping the league for tournaments, benching national-team forwards behind foreigners, holding no Friday matches and publishing no usable league calendar.

incidents.title: De Kruif's future unknown as coach stays away before World Cup qualifiers
incidents.summary: Head coach Lodewijk de Kruif is not in Bangladesh for the Federation Cup or league and may not return for the qualifiers; only the goalkeeping coach turns up and BFF cannot say if he stays.

incidents.title: Match-fixing allegations resurface, from a BFF-page comment to the 2009 fair-play trophy
incidents.summary: Fans ask if match fixing still exists after a BFF-page comment on Sheikh Jamal, then a copied post alleges BFF gave Abahani the 2009 fair-play trophy despite 12 fixed matches that season.

incidents.title: Nepal earthquake cancels the AFC U-14 girls’ final in Kathmandu
incidents.summary: The 7.9-magnitude Kathmandu earthquake cancels Bangladesh’s AFC U-14 girls’ final against Nepal and fans fear for the girls’ safety.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Stadium pitch unprepared days before the qualifiers
incidents.summary: Fans complain the Bangabandhu Stadium grass is long and uneven, and BFF only realise days before the qualifiers that major turf work is needed.

incidents.title: League confined to Dhaka as outstation venues are axed
incidents.summary: The professional league is organised on a single ground with clubs having no grounds of their own, and BFF axes all venues outside Dhaka except Chittagong.

incidents.title: Fans slam de Kruif's World Cup qualifier squad selections
incidents.summary: Fans erupt over the qualifier squad: Mishu, Hemanta, Toklis, Reza and Emon dropped while out-of-form Wahed, Sajib and Liton keep their places, and rumours say de Kruif prefers naturalised foreigners.

incidents.title: Rain postpones BPL matches as waterlogged pitch exposes drainage failure
incidents.summary: League matches are postponed by rain on a waterlogged Bangabandhu pitch fans photograph as a paddy field; BFF is told to fix the drainage before World Cup qualifiers.

incidents.title: Big clubs poach young stars then bench them, fans fear another Toklis/Rony case
incidents.summary: Shakhawat Rony loses his club and national place at Sheikh Jamal, then both Sheikh clubs chase young sensation Jewel Rana; fans fear another talent ruined by bench-warming.

incidents.title: Fitness crisis: 51 players injured after rushed BPL first leg
incidents.summary: Fifty-one players are injured after the rushed BPL first leg and fans demand BFF bring a trainer, physio and video analyst, warning fitness will cost the World Cup qualifiers.

incidents.title: Fans tire of fake transfer rumours naming Elano, Torres and Gayle
incidents.summary: Fans complain the group is flooded with fabricated rumours that Elano, Fernando Torres and Dwight Gayle are joining the Bangladesh league. Suggested new category: transfer_rumours.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal sack coach Maruful Haque after Abahani defeat
incidents.summary: Sheikh Jamal sack Maruful Haque, who says he was prepared to lose his job and blames foreign players who were not sincere in training.

incidents.title: Fans demand de Kruif sacked after winless World Cup qualifier start
incidents.summary: De Kruif admits he works a daily-wage, part-time job from Holland; after the Kyrgyzstan defeat and Tajikistan draw fans call for him and Titu to go, one post naming a players' syndicate and Dido's expulsion.

incidents.title: Former national footballer Tanvir Chowdhury fights for life after road accident as fans raise funds
incidents.summary: Former national footballer Tanvir Chowdhury is in intensive care after a serious road accident and needs about 50 lakh taka for treatment, with fans appealing for help.

incidents.title: Reasat Khaton frozen out of the World Cup qualifier squad
incidents.summary: Expatriate hopeful Reasat is left out of the 23-man squad, suffers dysentery in camp and is not welcomed by local players who fear for their places.

incidents.title: Sheikh Jamal set to lose Wedson and Emeka to Mohun Bagan
incidents.summary: Reports that Wedson Anselme and Emeka Darlington may join Mohun Bagan leave Sheikh Jamal’s AFC Cup hopes in ruins and fans urge president Manjur Kader to act.

incidents.title: Fans turn on Zahid Hassan Emily as de Kruif keeps starting him
incidents.summary: Fans fume as Emily, unfit and missing chance after chance, stays in the XI while in-form Enamul is played out of position or benched; one post wishes him injured so the forward line changes.

incidents.title: Captain Mamunul Islam hit by food poisoning before the qualifiers
incidents.summary: Mamunul suffers food poisoning days before the World Cup qualifiers, days after Zahid Hossain’s ulcer, and fans question how professional footballers fall ill like this.

incidents.title: BFF move to naturalise three African players splits fans
incidents.summary: Samad Yusuf, Ismail Bangoura and Kingsley Chigozie sign citizenship forms with BFF; ex-coach Manik calls citizenship too cheap and Alfaz Ahmed calls it a conspiracy, before BFF backs away and cancels the project under pressure. Suggested new category: foreign_player_naturalisation. De Kruif later says foreigners from the league must be played for immediate success.

incidents.title: George Kottan leaves Abahani and says no improvement is visible
incidents.summary: Abahani coach George Kottan leaves when his six-month contract expires to work on FIFA’s grassroots goal project, saying the national team has not visibly improved.

incidents.title: Empty galleries expose BFF marketing failure
incidents.summary: Fewer than a thousand spectators attend a Chittagong league match and fans blame BFF’s marketing department, which does not even put up banners around stadiums.

incidents.title: Clubs block national call-ups as BFF warn Sheikh Jamal
incidents.summary: Chittagong Abahani threaten U19 pick Shafayat Hossain Munna with suspension if he joins camp, Sheikh Jamal hold back Jamal Bhuyan and Mamunul from trials, and BFF vice-president Badal Roy warns of strict action.

incidents.title: Franchise league debate splits fans as BSSL plan takes shape
incidents.summary: Fans argue over the proposed franchise Bangladesh Super Soccer League, fearing it will kill the Premier League in a country with no infrastructure, calendar or professionalism.

incidents.title: Fans demand a restructured home-and-away national league
incidents.summary: Fans propose restructuring Bangladesh football into professional tiers with a 20-team home-and-away national league, blaming BFF inaction and greed.

incidents.title: No coaching staff scouting as Australia and Jordan qualifiers loom
incidents.summary: With Australia on 3 September, de Kruif is unwell, the goalkeeping coach is with Sheikh Jamal and assistant Titu is busy with the U19s, so nobody is scouting league players; fans note the ranking fell from 168 to 169 under Kruif.

incidents.title: Waterlogged pitches turn league matches into paddy-field football

entities.name: Sailor BFF National U-15 Football Championship

incidents.summary: League matches are played on muddy, waterlogged pitches fans call paddy fields, and BFF is warned the Bangabandhu pitch cannot survive the Jordan qualifier plus AFC U16 and U19 tournaments in the same month.

incidents.title: Farashganj suspended two years for giving a walkover
incidents.summary: Farashganj give a walkover and BFF suspend them from the Premier League for two years, fine them 5 lakh taka and order 13 lakh taka returned.

incidents.title: De Kruif banned and fined, misses Australia dugout
incidents.summary: Four weeks before Australia, Kruif has still not come to Bangladesh; FIFA then ban him two matches and fine him 8,500 Swiss francs for indiscipline, and fans say a syndicate stopped him dropping players while BFF blocked stopping the league.

incidents.title: Expatriate hopefuls frozen out as fans allege a selection syndicate
incidents.summary: Akmol Ali, Rizwan Ahmed and Reasat Akmal are frozen out of the national team through the World Cup qualifiers and after de Kruif’s exit, and fans allege a selection syndicate keeps expatriates out.

incidents.title: U16 SAFF champions neglected as AFC qualifiers expose grassroots gap
incidents.summary: A month after winning the SAFF U16 title, Bangladesh concede 11 goals to Saudi Arabia and the UAE in AFC qualifiers while India and Nepal qualify; fans say the talents will be lost and the half-dead BFF academy cannot even send food expenses on time.

incidents.title: Fans slam Titu's defensive tactics as U19s crash out of SAFF and AFC qualifiers
incidents.summary: Titu's five-defender, park-the-bus tactics are blamed for the SAFF U19 semi-final exit to India and the AFC U19 failure against Bhutan and Uzbekistan; BFF say he will never again head-coach a national team.

incidents.title: No channel shows Bangladesh's Australia qualifier as TV blackout returns
incidents.summary: Channels show the English Premier League and Indian Super League but not Bangladesh's World Cup qualifiers against Australia and Kyrgyzstan; fans demand a protest.

incidents.title: BFF sack de Kruif in salary row and appoint Fabio Lopez
