incidents.summary: Fans sarcastically hail ultra slow-motion in BPL broadcasts and mock commentator Nabil Khan for still not telling a shot from a cross after years of commentary.

incidents.title: Selection rows dominate the March World Cup qualifiers against Palestine
incidents.summary: Around the March qualifiers against Palestine, fans attacked selections: Mehedi overlooked, Emon unused, Srabon picked ahead of Zico and Pritam, Tariq Kazi overlooked as under Jamie Day, in-form Rahul given no time, Sheikh Russel bench players picked over Mohammedan regulars, and a right-back played at centre-back; a former coach alleged coaches take commissions to field players.

incidents.title: Javier Cabrera's job under threat after the Palestine defeats
incidents.summary: Fans accuse BFF of sacking coaches just as they organise the team, fear Salahuddin will ask Cabrera to resign, and argue Salahuddin blames Cabrera to save himself after 22 coaching changes since 2008.

incidents.title: Fans demand Hamza, Samit and Diabate for the June qualifiers
incidents.summary: Fans demand BFF act on Hamza Choudhury, Samit Som and Souleymane Diabate before the June qualifiers, warning Sri Lanka and Pakistan's expatriate-heavy teams could surprise, and say BFF treats citizenship like a golden deer while Diabate's case dies from lack of goodwill.

incidents.title: BFF Elite Academy thrashed by Fakirapool, called an academy in name only
incidents.summary: BFF Elite Academy were thrashed by a huge margin by Fakirapool Young Men's Club, and fans slam the academy as an academy in name only with no success at age level.

incidents.title: BPL broadcasts: single cameras, 360p streams and poor commentary
incidents.summary: Fans complain only big matches get T Sports' quality cameras while other teams get BFF's 360p stream, contrast the 2016 multi-camera broadcasts with today's single-camera YouTube streams, and slam commentary that misses goals and mispronounces names.

incidents.title: Saif Sporting Club's collapse wastes the players it unearthed
incidents.summary: Fans lament that players Saif Sporting Club unearthed like Matin Mia and Yasin Arafat are fading away along with the club itself, with careers discarded after moves to Bashundhara Kings brought no game time and national-team exclusion.

incidents.title: FIFA bans and fines five BFF officials for corruption
incidents.summary: FIFA punished five BFF officials for corruption and irregularities over false information and fake documents in FIFA fund spending: senior vice-president Salam Murshedi fined about Tk 13 lakh, former general secretary Abu Nayeem Sohag banned three years and fined about Tk 26 lakh, and two more officials fined and banned two years.

incidents.title: Fans mock BFF's YouTube channel
incidents.summary: Fans mock BFF's YouTube channel, joking viewers can learn English in seven days there. (Other: BFF media output ridiculed.)

incidents.title: Historic Brothers Union relegated from the Premier League
incidents.summary: Fans lament Brothers Union's decline, calling them a skeleton of tradition, as the historic club are officially relegated from the Premier League to the Championship League.

incidents.title: Sheikh Russel forward Iqbal Hossain vanishes mid-season and flies to Canada
incidents.summary: Sheikh Russel forward Iqbal Hossain vanished mid-season and flew to Canada without telling the club, ignoring two show-cause notices.

incidents.title: Squad selection rows before the June World Cup qualifiers
incidents.summary: Before the June qualifiers, Mohammedan coach Alfaz Ahmed asks how much more his players must prove for the national team while players from a relegation-bound side are picked, and fans attack the continued selection of Johnny, Rimon, Rafiqul, Shakil and Topu while in-form Kazem Shah, Emon and Arif Hossain are ignored, asking on what quota the pictured players play.

incidents.title: U-18 league bylaws let senior players crowd out youngsters
incidents.summary: Fans criticise BFF's U-18 league bylaws letting BPL and BCL players take part, asking where new players will get their chance, and slam the BPL U-18 tournament for letting Premier League players take part at one club's wish.

incidents.title: Abahani Limited's collapse: no trophy and a raid on Mohammedan
incidents.summary: Abahani Limited ended the 2023-24 season without a single trophy and no league win over Bashundhara in five seasons, amid internal conflict over the captaincy and Jamal Bhuyan benched, while building their side by taking Emon, Jafar and Yasin Arafat from Mohammedan.

incidents.title: Age fraud in youth football: fake birth certificates and an over-age U-17 player

entities.name: Bangabandhu National Gold Cup U-17 Football Tournament

incidents.summary: A grassroots coach urges coaches to send only correctly-aged children for trials as fake birth certificates get caught at BFF medicals, and fans question how a player of that fitness and age could play in the Bangabandhu National Gold Cup U-17 tournament.

incidents.title: Federation Cup final refereeing under fire
incidents.summary: Mohammedan's team manager says five specific referees handle almost all Kings matches without neutrality, fans call the final's refereeing strange and claim Kings have received favourable decisions at crucial moments for three or four years, with commentators unable to find fault in the controversial incident on replay.

incidents.title: Kings accused of bussing in paid fans with biryani and jerseys
incidents.summary: A fan defends Kings bringing crowds with biryani, jerseys and money as good for football while rejecting the referee-buying claims. (Other: paid-fans allegation — a syndicate watch item.)

incidents.title: Federation Cup final presentation mocked as a shambles
incidents.summary: Fans mock the Federation Cup final's presentation in Mymensingh, where only 13 people stood on stage with the general secretary at the very corner and the host and presenter got tangled up.

incidents.title: Women's football neglected: Krishna Rani show-caused, no AFC club licence
incidents.summary: Bangladesh Football Ultras issue BFF an ultimatum after women's committee chief Mahfuza Akter Kiran threatened a show-cause notice against injured star Krishna Rani Sarkar, fans ask whether injury will end Krishna's career and whether Sabina Khatun's career is under threat, and Bangladesh has no club in the AFC Women's Champions League while India, Nepal and Bhutan do.

incidents.title: Obaidur Rahman Nawab's talent wasted after giving up Qatar chances
incidents.summary: Fans lament that Nawab gave up chances with the Qatar national team and top clubs to play for Bangladesh, only to lose his position and match time and face neglect, insult and corruption.

incidents.title: Hamza says he wants to play for Bangladesh; fans ask why BFF stalls
incidents.summary: Hamza Choudhury himself says he wants to play for Bangladesh, fans ask whether BFF is even interested in calling him up, and argue the team urgently needs a real striker like Diabate while Hamza helps the midfield but cannot fix the scoring.

incidents.title: Calls for Kazi Salahuddin not to contest the BFF presidency again
incidents.summary: Fans urge Kazi Salahuddin not to contest the BFF presidency again, saying he has squandered the respect he earned as a player by clinging to the chair while football declined, and mock him as the godfather.

incidents.title: Chattogram Abahani threaten to quit the BPL
incidents.summary: Chattogram Abahani threaten to skip the BPL over player trading, biased refereeing and Salahuddin-Salam failures, say they will not play the U-18 BPL and apply to be relegated in place of Brothers Union, as a first step toward withdrawing from professional football.

incidents.title: Cabrera's tactics slated after the Lebanon defeat
incidents.summary: After the Lebanon defeat, fans attack Cabrera for playing midfielder Morsalin as a winger, winger Emon in Jamal's midfield role, and Shakil ahead of Bishwanath and Sushanta, calling the bald coach a false mastermind who only harmed football.

incidents.title: Oscar Bruzon sacked by Bashundhara Kings
incidents.summary: Kings part ways with coach Oscar Bruzon after questions over his domestic success but international flop, with the president vowing to clear out weeds inside the team, and Bruzon then says some officials run clubs without knowledge and put self-interest above the club.

incidents.title: Players turn to unofficial khep matches as clubs delay wages
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings are accused of keeping players' payments pending, with regular Bishwanath Ghosh playing khep matches, and a long essay argues khep both harms football and provides players a livelihood since clubs do not pay on time or in full.

incidents.title: BFF AGM rows: more councillors and a sari for every delegate
incidents.summary: BFF increased the number of councillors at its AGM, ignoring FIFA's instructions, and each association received a 10,000-taka cheque plus a sari as a gift, drawing mixed reactions since most delegates are men.

incidents.title: Post-upheaval campaign to remove Salahuddin and free BFF
incidents.summary: After the 5 August political change, fans demand the BFF building be freed from autocracy like Ganabhaban, call for a siege of BFF until Salahuddin resigns, warn a new syndicate has arrived under a different agenda, and condemn players and officials who went to bow before him.

incidents.title: Sheikh Russel and Sheikh Jamal fold after the political upheaval
incidents.summary: Sheikh Russel KC and Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club tell their players they will not form teams next season amid the unstable situation, leaving contracted players' livelihoods in doubt, and fans accuse those who promised development of coming only to whiten black money.

incidents.title: Diabate pleads to play as Hamza gets his passport and NOC
incidents.summary: Souleymane Diabate says it feels like he is begging to play for Bangladesh, Hamza Choudhury gets his passport and the FA's NOC with BFF sending documents to FIFA, but BFF has no good news for Diabate, and coach Maruful Haque's interview attacking expatriate and naturalised players is slated.

incidents.title: Captain Jamal Bhuyan left without a club for 2024-25
incidents.summary: Bangladesh captain Jamal Bhuyan found no club for the 2024-25 season after he and Abahani could not agree financially on the last day of transfers.

incidents.title: U-20 team go from SAFF champions to AFC collapse amid the Kings-Marful ego fight
incidents.summary: A month after winning the SAFF U-20 Championship, Bangladesh's U-20 team collapsed in the AFC Asian Cup qualifiers, conceding heavily to Syria and Guam with goalkeeper Ismail Hossain Mahin's errors under fire, as coach Maruful Haque blamed an ego fight with Bashundhara Kings over player releases and a parallel organisation challenging the federation.

incidents.title: Bhutan tour exposes the senior syndicate in selection
incidents.summary: Around the Bhutan tour, fans attack the regular selection of out-of-form seniors Topu Barman, Saad Uddin and both Sohel Ranas, criticise Faisal Ahmed Fahim starting both matches despite no notable league performance, and ask when the senior syndicate will end, while Kazem Shah is left out despite regular Police FC performances.

incidents.title: BFF election race begins as Salahuddin steps aside
incidents.summary: As Salahuddin announces he will not contest the next election, the race to succeed him begins: Tarofdar Ruhul Amin and Tabith Awal emerge as contenders amid accusations over Chattogram Abahani, Saif Sporting Club and unpaid Sheikh Kamal Cup prize money, and warnings that Salahuddin's circle will return through the new committee.

incidents.title: Matin Mia's career lost through neglect
incidents.summary: Fans call Matin Mia a king who lost everything through neglect and ask who will take responsibility for losing him.

incidents.title: FIFA-banned Abu Nayeem Sohag's rehabilitation feared
incidents.summary: Fans claim Sohag, banned by FIFA from all football activity for corruption, may be brought back, note he is planning a rehabilitation despite a life ban, and fume that his blueprint will be implemented with the sports adviser indifferent.

incidents.title: BFF election 2024: vote-buying claims, old-guard conditions and no manifestos
incidents.summary: The October 2024 BFF election is fought amid claims of vote-buying at 25-30 thousand taka per vote, Salahuddin's three conditions for supporting Tabith Awal including no investigation into sixteen years of irregularities, election rules signed by FIFA-banned Abu Nayeem Sohag, a sit-in at the BFF building, and candidates offering no written manifesto, with the old guard's ghosts still sitting in BFF afterwards.

incidents.title: Arham Islam frozen out by teammates in the U-17 Asian Cup qualifiers
incidents.summary: In the AFC U-17 Asian Cup qualifiers, expatriate winger Arham Islam was repeatedly denied the ball by teammates Morshed Ali and captain Faisal, who attacked down the right instead, as Bangladesh lost to ten-man Cambodia and failed to qualify; fans call it a syndicate, demand bans, and note team manager Jahid Hasan Emili had opposed expatriate players in 2015.

incidents.title: Kazem Shah dropped from the national team
incidents.summary: Fans lament that Kazem Shah's football skills are wonderful, yet he was dropped from the team in the last window.

incidents.title: Oscar Bruzon succeeds with East Bengal after leaving Kings
incidents.summary: After leaving Bashundhara Kings, Oscar Bruzon took charge of bottom-of-the-table East Bengal days before the Challenge League and got them through the group, prompting fans to ask whether the problem was the plan, the local players or the syndicate, while Bruzon is accused of unethically pulling Robinho and Miguel to East Bengal.

incidents.title: Mohammedan reverse Diabate's loan to Bashundhara Kings
incidents.summary: Mohammedan first allowed Souleymane Diabate to play for Bashundhara Kings in the AFC Challenge League, then reversed the loan within a day after fan protests, with fans questioning who would pay his salary and compensate Mohammedan if he suffered a big injury.

incidents.title: Eight months' unpaid wages: Robson Robinho and Chattogram Abahani
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings delayed paying Robson Robinho's salary for eight months, with fans alleging the money funded Imrul Hasan's BFF election campaign, and Chattogram Abahani went eight months without paying wages, as players demand their hard-earned money.

incidents.title: Elita Kingsley's stalled national career after naturalisation
incidents.summary: Elita Kingsley took Bangladesh citizenship in 2021 after much struggle and giving up Nigerian citizenship, was called to the 2021 SAFF preliminary squad but got no FIFA permission, and after two years got only 68 minutes in two matches against Seychelles, while he now pushes for the naturalisation process to be expedited for Diabate and others.

incidents.title: Peter Butler quits after the SAFF triumph amid the Sabina syndicate rift
incidents.summary: After the women's team won the SAFF Championship, head coach Peter Butler announced he will leave on 31 December and refused the open-top bus, amid a senior-junior split: Butler alleged an outside party wants the girls to lose and that eight to ten people do politics, while a seniors' syndicate led by captain Sabina Khatun is blamed for benching juniors and clashing with the coach, with former coach Golam Rabbani Choton accused of interfering from outside.

incidents.title: Bangladesh still without a kit sponsor while even Guam and Macau have one
incidents.summary: Fans point out that even Guam U-17 have Macron and Macau have adidas as kit sponsors while Bangladesh still has no kit sponsor and does not appear on the Football Kit Archive website. (Other: commercial and sponsorship failure.)

incidents.title: Bashundhara Kings lose all three AFC Challenge League matches
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings ended their AFC Challenge League campaign with three straight defeats and zero points, conceding seven and scoring one, losing 1-0 to Nejmeh on a Saad Uddin own goal, 4-0 to Oscar Bruzon's East Bengal and to Paro FC, in a sixth straight first-stage elimination in Asia, with fans blaming coach Valeriu Tita, quota players, man-management and the club's domestic refereeing cushion.

incidents.title: India-Nepal women's SAFF semi-final halted for 70 minutes
incidents.summary: In the other SAFF women's semi-final, Nepal scored into an empty goal after India left the field, the referee disallowed it after India's coach ran on, Nepal walked off, play stopped for almost seventy minutes, and Nepal won 4-2 on penalties.

incidents.title: Syndicate of coaches accused of taking commissions for national call-ups
incidents.summary: Fans say there is a group of syndicate coaches in the country's football: if a player is theirs that player gets chances in the national team and big teams, with the coaches getting a hefty commission from those players every year.

incidents.title: SAFF-winning women's team went two months without pay
incidents.summary: The women's national team went two months with no salary and played their last four matches without match fees yet brought the SAFF title home again, were offered a Tk 20,000 bonus each, and were kept in bachelor rooms on the fourth floor of the BFF building with cheap food.

incidents.title: BFF officials hog the camera with the women's team
incidents.summary: Fans ask whether the media manager's job is to stand close to the girls and note the culture of coming into focus never went away, even though the committee changed.

incidents.title: U-20 boys got Tk 7 lakh, SAFF-winning girls got Tk 1 crore
incidents.summary: Fans note the boys became U-20 champions and were given seven lakh taka, while the girls were given one crore taka, exclaiming at BFF's justice.

incidents.title: Fans say Kazem Shah must be picked to fix the syndicate midfield
incidents.summary: Fans argue playing Kazem Shah has become necessary to increase technical skill in midfield, saying the midfield has long been filled with syndicate-backed players like Sohel Rana Sr, Sohel Rana Jr, Mujibur Rahman Joni, Masuk Mia Joni and Biplu Ahmed who never delivered results.

incidents.title: Imrul Hasan reappointed league committee chairman despite conflict of interest
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings president Imrul Hasan is again made professional league committee chairman while also running his club, skipping the first meeting in anger after wanting the national teams and finance committees, and is accused of using both roles for his club's benefit, including the Challenge Cup final being held at Kings' home ground.

incidents.title: BPL broadcasts still phone-quality into December
incidents.summary: Fans slam T Sports' awful BPL broadcasts without scorecards or commentary and with poor camera angles, contrast the 2018 Bangabandhu Gold Cup's broadcast quality with six years of decline, and note Indonesia's third-tier pitch and broadcast quality are far better than Bangladesh's top tier.

incidents.title: First-ever home defeat to Maldives and calls to sack Cabrera
incidents.summary: Bangladesh suffered their first-ever home loss to Maldives, leaving Asian Cup Pot 3 lost, as fans slated Fahim's crossing, Mitul's keeping and Cabrera's substitutions and called for the coach to be sacked after a 28-match record of 15 losses and 7 wins.

incidents.title: Indonesia's rise spurs the expatriate debate; Samit Som refuses Bangladesh
incidents.summary: Indonesia's 2-0 win over Saudi Arabia with nine expatriate players is held up against Bangladesh's stalling on Hamza and Diabate, Sri Lanka beat Yemen with Brisbane Roar defender Jack Hingert while Bangladesh still cannot get Hamza, and Samit Som says he is not interested in playing for Bangladesh right now after the latest contact from BFF.

incidents.title: Top players caught playing unofficial khep matches
incidents.summary: Top Kings players are accused of playing khep matches two days before the Challenge Cup opener, allegedly on chairman Imrul's instructions, a BPL player named Tushar is called a khep master, and Bangladesh Ultras give a goalkeeper 24 hours to delete his khep-match videos.

incidents.title: Goalkeeper Zico hints at the syndicate in the media
incidents.summary: Goalkeeper Anisur Rahman Zico dropped a bombshell in the media, hinting at the syndicate. (Other: syndicate hint by a national-team player.)

incidents.title: Challenge Cup final: flare thrown at Mohammedan players and Sujan's bribery claim
incidents.summary: In the Challenge Cup final at Kings' home ground, a flare was thrown at Mohammedan's defenders and keeper Sujan, and BFF later asked Mohammedan to explain why Sujan should not be punished for telling referees they took bundles from Kings, while the disciplinary committee still had not ruled on the flare incident.

incidents.title: BPL pitches in shocking state as the new season starts
incidents.summary: Fans show dead, brown pitches at Munshiganj's Matiur Rahman Stadium and Gazipur's Barkat Stadium, ask how the league committee approved them, note a cricket pitch being made on a football field in Sylhet, and quote Rakib Hossain saying top domestic football is played on hard, yellow-grass pitches that will injure players.

incidents.title: Shekh Morsalin accused of blackmailing his wife; Kings players' scandals listed
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings footballer Shekh Morsalin was accused of blackmailing his own wife, and fans ask why players of the so-called professional club keep getting into scandals, citing drug addiction, players banned for carrying drugs and a Facebook accusation.

incidents.title: Hamza cleared for Bangladesh; BFF rules out Diabate
incidents.summary: Hamza Choudhury's clearance is celebrated as fans urge BFF to keep the diaspora process going and bring in Diabate and Samit Som, but a BFF executive member says there is no possibility of getting Diabate, mocked for claiming it is because he is married.

incidents.title: Cabrera's future debated after Hamza's arrival
incidents.summary: With Hamza bringing new life to Bangladesh football, fans debate whether a good squad alone brings results given Cabrera's 27.57 percent win rate, whether a high-profile coach is needed for an EPL player, and whether Cabrera should stay until 31 March 2026 for the Asia Cup qualifiers.

incidents.title: Backlash against hyping every diaspora player
incidents.summary: Fans criticise supporters who inbox every diaspora player they find and hype unproven ones, arguing being of Bangladeshi origin does not mean come play for the national team, and that unproven players like Rahbar and Tahmid failed after going straight to the national team.

incidents.title: Kings' offside goal row without VAR
incidents.summary: Fans argue over whether Bashundhara Kings' goal was offside, with a shared photo unable to prove it and calls for VAR, asking how long Kings will win or draw thanks to referees and linesmen.

incidents.title: One Hamza will not qualify Bangladesh: Cabrera compared with Jamie Day
incidents.summary: A long analysis argues one Hamza will not qualify Bangladesh for the Asia Cup, compares Cabrera with Jamie Day, warns syndicate and quota players will cost results, and says Diabate is now out of the question while Elita Kingsley should be kept in the squad.

incidents.title: Anwar Uddin as national coach debated
incidents.summary: Fans argue against Anwar Uddin as coach, noting he refused to play for Bangladesh in 2000 and 2008, never made a Bangladeshi passport, has no UEFA Pro licence and has never been a head coach, preferring Sean Lane or Peter Butler.

incidents.title: Bangabandhu Stadium renovation still unfinished after four years
incidents.summary: Fans ask how much longer the stadium renovation, going on for four years, will take, joking that if Bangabandhu Stadium had a mouth it would say forgive me now.

incidents.title: Hamza Choudhury watch: Sheffield United debut and the coach shortlist
incidents.summary: Hamza Choudhury's Sheffield United debut and BFF's new-coach shortlist dominate early-2025 talk as fans await his Bangladesh arrival.

incidents.title: Sullivan brothers: early diaspora recruitment talk
incidents.summary: Fans debate recruiting the US-based Sullivan brothers for Bangladesh, with Quinn Sullivan's future the main question.

incidents.title: Preliminary squad row: in-form players overlooked, Kings players favoured
incidents.summary: The January preliminary squad sparks complaints that in-form players were overlooked in favour of Bashundhara Kings players.

incidents.title: Mohammedan risk losing their AFC spot over licensing
incidents.summary: Mohammedan are warned they could lose their AFC spot to Abahani or Bashundhara over licensing unless they win the league.

incidents.title: Women's team revolt against coach Peter Butler
incidents.summary: SAFF-winning women's players revolt against coach Peter Butler; Butler demands seven players be removed, players threaten mass retirement, and fans split over the standoff.

incidents.title: India squad selection row: in-form players dropped, quota picks kept
incidents.summary: The February India squad announcement draws fury as Yasin, Mithu and other in-form players are dropped while quota picks are kept.

incidents.title: Fahmidul in the preliminary squad: media propaganda and selection doubt
incidents.summary: Fahmidul Islam is named in the preliminary India squad amid media propaganda questioning his Serie D credentials and the syndicate's quota picks.

incidents.title: Hamza Choudhury arrives for his Bangladesh debut
incidents.summary: Hamza Choudhury lands in Bangladesh amid a media circus, visits Habiganj, joins the camp and prepares for his debut against India.

incidents.title: Sullivan brothers: Quinn's USA choice and the brothers' futures
incidents.summary: As the March window approaches, fans follow Quinn Sullivan's choice between the USA and Bangladesh and debate the younger brothers' futures.

incidents.title: India 0-0 draw in Shillong: missed chances and selection fury
incidents.summary: Bangladesh draw 0-0 with India in Shillong as missed chances, a weak bench and the Fahmidul absence fuel fury at Cabrera and the selectors.

incidents.title: Women's team after the revolt: rebuilding under Butler
incidents.summary: After the revolt settles, the women's team rebuilds under Peter Butler toward its next assignments.

incidents.title: Diaspora trials announced: 30-plus origin players to be tried in June
incidents.summary: BFF vice-president Fahad Karim announces trials for 30-plus Bangladeshi-origin players in June, raising commission and selection fears.

incidents.title: Former players attack expatriate recruitment: Jibon, Alfaz and Aslam
incidents.summary: Former players including Nabib Newaj Jibon, Alfaz Ahmed and Aslam attack the recruitment of expatriate players, drawing a furious fan backlash.

incidents.title: Fahmidul Islam dropped and sent back to Italy; fans protest
incidents.summary: Fahmidul Islam is dropped from the India squad and sent back to Italy from the Saudi camp, triggering a wave of fan protests, exposés and marches on BFF.

incidents.title: Fan protest wave: ultimatum to BFF and the march against the syndicate
incidents.summary: Fans give BFF an ultimatum and organise protests and a march against the syndicate after the Fahmidul dropping.

incidents.title: Sack Cabrera campaign after the India draw and the Fahmidul row
incidents.summary: The campaign to sack coach Javier Cabrera grows after the India draw and the Fahmidul affair.

incidents.title: Bashundhara Kings accused of withholding players from the U-20 SAFF squad
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings are accused of withholding players from the under-20 SAFF and Asia Cup squads over starting-XI guarantees.

incidents.title: Samit Shome's eligibility and passport clearance for Bangladesh
incidents.summary: Samit Shome's route to Bangladesh — passport, Canada FA clearance and FIFA approval — is followed step by step, with warnings his case must not end like Fahmidul's.

incidents.title: Fahmidul bullying revelations: senior players accused of freezing him out
incidents.summary: Reports emerge that senior players bullied Fahmidul in camp, denying him passes and branding him an expatriate outsider, as media outlets split over the story.

incidents.title: Ahmed Shayek and the media campaign against expatriate players (media propaganda against diaspora players)

entities.name: Ahmed Shayek
entities.role: Bashundhara Kings media and marketing manager

incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings media chief Ahmed Shayek leads a media campaign against expatriate players, drawing accusations of a conspiratorial anti-diaspora agenda.

incidents.title: BPL refereeing rows: Kings Arena penalty calls and referee intimidation
incidents.summary: BPL refereeing comes under fire after controversial penalty calls at Kings Arena, with referees accused of favouring Bashundhara Kings.

incidents.title: Cuba Mitchell: recruitment drive and stalled paperwork
incidents.summary: Cuba Mitchell's recruitment stalls over paperwork, with fans urging BFF to move before Jamaica take him and blaming BFF negligence.

incidents.title: Syndicate exposé wave: rigged signings, Jamal 'held hostage'
incidents.summary: Long exposés allege the Bashundhara syndicate rigged signings and selection, and claim Jamal Bhuyan is barred from speaking to the media.

incidents.title: Singapore-match ticket row: Ultras demand a quota, fans cry foul (ticket syndicate row)
incidents.summary: Supporters' groups demand ticket quotas for the Singapore match, sparking a row over ticket syndicates, touts and who gets into the stadium.

incidents.title: Mohammedan end 23-year wait for the BPL title (league title with licensing and AFC-spot worries)
incidents.summary: Mohammedan win the Bangladesh Premier League for the first time in 23 years under Alfaz Ahmed, amid worries over licensing and their AFC spot.

incidents.title: SAFF U-19 Championship: Choton's tactics and the semi-final exit
incidents.summary: Bangladesh's SAFF U-19 campaign ends in frustration as coach Golam Rabbani Choton is blamed for long-ball tactics and benching players like Farzad Aftab.

incidents.title: Women's team build-up: Butler's wider role and the U23 link
incidents.summary: Peter Butler's role widens toward the U23 setup as the women's team builds toward its next assignments.

incidents.title: Singapore qualifier build-up: tickets, stadium and squad questions
incidents.summary: Build-up to the June 10 Singapore qualifier is dominated by sold-out tickets, stadium preparations and questions over the squad.

incidents.title: Fahmidul returns: June camp, Bhutan debut and BPL interest
incidents.summary: Fahmidul Islam returns to the national team for the June window, plays against Bhutan and Singapore, and draws BPL transfer interest.

incidents.title: Sack Cabrera campaign renewed after the Singapore defeat
incidents.summary: The campaign to sack coach Javier Cabrera flares again after the home defeat to Singapore.

incidents.title: Cuba Mitchell: passport race before Singapore and the U23 question
incidents.summary: Fans press BFF to finish Cuba Mitchell's passport before the Singapore match, then debate his place in the U23 setup after he misses the squad.

incidents.title: June window selection rows: Kazem, Jamal and Al-Amin benched or dropped
incidents.summary: The June window revives selection rows as Kazem Shah, Jamal Bhuyan and Al-Amin are benched or dropped while out-of-form favourites keep their places.

incidents.title: Bhutan friendly: Fahmidul's debut and the June window XI debate
incidents.summary: Bangladesh play Bhutan in a June friendly as Fahmidul finally debuts on home soil and fans argue over the XI for Singapore.

incidents.title: Broadcast quality row: T Sports pictures and National Stadium floodlights slammed
incidents.summary: Fans slam T Sports' blurry, shaky broadcast pictures and the National Stadium's jaundiced floodlights ahead of the June matches.

incidents.title: 6 million taka theme-song money for the Singapore and Bhutan matches questioned
incidents.summary: Fans demand Tabith Awal and Fahad Karim account for 6 million taka taken from the NSC for a theme song and TVC for the Singapore and Bhutan matches.

incidents.title: Singapore 1-2 home defeat: penalty row and selection fury
incidents.summary: Bangladesh lose 1-2 at home to Singapore as a denied penalty, refereeing and Cabrera's selection draw fresh fury.

incidents.title: Goalkeeper row after Singapore: Mitul defended, Zico accused of hiring fans
incidents.summary: The goalkeeper debate erupts after the Singapore defeat, with Mitul Marma defended as the league's best and Zico accused of hiring fans to attack him.

incidents.title: June diaspora trials: origin players tried out amid fan chaos
incidents.summary: Dozens of origin players arrive for BFF trials in June; fans storm the field at one session and debate who deserves a place.

incidents.title: Fahim playing khyap matches amid unpaid-wage claims against Bashundhara
incidents.summary: National-team winger Fahim is reported playing khyap (unofficial) matches, with fans saying Bashundhara Kings not paying him forced him into it.

incidents.title: Diaspora trials: staged show, self-funded call-ups and six players barred from the U-23 camp
incidents.summary: Fans allege BFF's June global talent hunt was staged: technical director Saiful Bari Titu is quoted admitting he did not watch all the trialists yet judged none worthy, trialists who paid their own way are asked to return at their own cost, and six diaspora players including Kasper Haque buy tickets but cannot join the U-23 camp; trial coordinator Sakib Mahmud is later accused of secretly signing players to his unlicensed agency.

incidents.title: Aminul Haque's Dhaka Post comments attacked as short-sighted
incidents.summary: Former goalkeeper Aminul Haque is criticised as thick-headed and short-sighted over his Dhaka Post comments, which fans say show little football knowledge and a negative attitude to diaspora players. (Media misreporting/bias: kept in 'other' per the user's taxonomy call.)

incidents.title: Women's Asian Cup qualification and the exiled seniors: Butler's discipline against the Sabina rift
incidents.summary: Bangladesh women qualify for the AFC Women's Asian Cup for the first time, beating Myanmar 2-1, but the triumph is shadowed by coach Peter Butler's dropping of senior players Sabina Khatun, Masura Parvin, Sanjida Akhter, Krishna Rani Sarkar and Matsushima Sumaiya over discipline; fans split between hailing Butler's uncompromising methods and demanding reconciliation, while others recall Salahuddin's BFF once refusing to send the team to qualifiers at all and demand BFF now fund analysts, physios and a proper camp.

incidents.title: SAFF players as locals: the foreign-player quota row
incidents.summary: BFF's decision to let five players from SAFF countries play as locals in the Premier League draws fire: fans ask who benefits from clubs signing Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Nepal players, mock Arambagh for bringing an Indian fifth-tier player into the first tier, question Police FC signing Nepal's old goalkeeper Kiran Chemjong, and note Vietnamese club Nam Dinh fielding an all-foreign XI in Asia.

incidents.title: Women's league stillborn, SAFF bonus unpaid
incidents.summary: Despite the women's Asian Cup qualification, fans demand BFF pay the promised 1.5 crore taka SAFF bonus, restart the women's league so players outside the national pool can earn money, and run talent hunts beyond Dhaka; Bangladesh has no club in the AFC Women's Club Championship while below-average clubs from Bhutan, Nepal and India prepare for it, and women's committee head Mahfuza Akter Kiran is accused of sleeping on the job.

incidents.title: Sack Cabrera: the July campaign and the Nepal fixtures row
incidents.summary: The campaign to sack men's coach Javier Cabrera builds through July: fans slam the September friendlies against Nepal after European opponents were dangled, call Cabrera the syndicate's first choice who survives despite tactical errors costing points against India and Singapore, and attack BFF president Tabith Awal as an establishment man who will never reform the board; Bashundhara Kings later question Cabrera's competence in a letter to BFF.

incidents.title: U-23 coach: the Zulfikar Mintu blueprint
incidents.summary: Fans allege a BFF blueprint is underway to make Zulfikar Mintu U-23 coach despite his 2024 qualifier record of three losses, blame him for destroying the BFF Elite Academy, and complain no U-23 coach or preliminary squad is named even as the AFC registration deadline passes.

incidents.title: Club officials incompetent
incidents.summary: A fan complains about how incompetent the people running the clubs are, with no club or person named.

incidents.title: Diabate leaves Mohammedan for Abahani
incidents.summary: Mohammedan's biggest star Souleymane Diabate joins arch-rivals Abahani after six years and 100-plus goals, with heartbroken fans blaming Mohammedan officials for letting the title-winning architect go and noting the champions' lack of an AFC licence kept them out of the Challenge League; Al Amin's game time is feared to suffer from Diabate's arrival.

incidents.title: BFF's flower-bouquet bill while players' airfare goes unpaid
incidents.summary: BFF is accused of taking sponsors' money in its name yet being unable to pay players' airfare while claiming 20 lakh taka for flower bouquets.

incidents.title: Pitches and grounds unfit for football
incidents.summary: A running complaint that Bangladesh has nowhere decent to play: the National Stadium's durba grass habit, a pitch so bad football cannot be played in the rainy season, Mohammedan training on a paddy field with no ground of its own, and the grassless, uneven Gazipur ground set to host Premier League matches for Police FC and PWD; fans contrast Somalia's Mogadishu City Club owning a 65,000-capacity stadium.

incidents.title: Zayn Hakeem and Niloy: passports stuck
incidents.summary: Fans slam the slow passport work for diaspora players Zayn Hakeem — whose grandfather's passport is still unfinished after 15-16 days — and Niloy, with passports for Ashik and Anik also said to have stalled a year after being issued.

incidents.title: BFF rejected Mizuno; Dour's kit promises unkept
incidents.summary: BFF is reported to have rejected 119-year-old Japanese kit maker Mizuno's offer to sponsor the national team jersey in favour of a local firm, while kit sponsor Dour is slammed six months on for unfulfilled promises — no offline store, late deliveries, sudden price rises and poor quality — and vice-president Fahad Karim and his wife are reported barred from leaving the country.

incidents.title: Kings' coach chaos: Farias quits for Duhok days before the AFC tie
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings lose new coach Sergio Farias to Iraqi club Duhok SC two weeks after appointing him, leaving the country's only professional club without a coach 24 hours before an AFC tournament match, with the team not yet having started training for the Doha tie against Al Karamah.

incidents.title: Arham Islam overlooked by BFF
incidents.summary: The first wave of the Arham Islam story: the Bangladesh-born Western United U-23 starter is ignored by BFF while Gibraltar debut a 16-year-old in World Cup qualifiers and Mauritius call up 18-year-old Leon Alizart, with fans saying politics can block chances, not dreams.

incidents.title: Kuba Mitchell joins Bashundhara Kings: career ruined, Imrul's pre-plan
incidents.summary: Teenage diaspora forward Kuba Mitchell's move from Sunderland's orbit to Bashundhara Kings splits fans: many call it the end of his European career and blame Kings president Imrul Hasan, alleging his passport effort was a pre-plan to bring the player to Kings and that a national-team spot was guaranteed in exchange, while others defend it as an informed economic decision; Kings are also accused of refusing to release players for the SAFF U-20 winning team.

incidents.title: U-23 Asian Cup qualifiers: Titu's fever, Hasan's XI and the Yemen heartbreak
incidents.summary: Bangladesh's U-23 Asian Cup qualifying campaign in Vietnam collapses amid coaching farce — head coach Saiful Bari Titu is reported ill and assistant Hasan Al Mamun takes charge, with fans questioning whether the fever is real — plus selection rows over Fahmidul Islam, Joni's three yellow cards and a red in two matches, and Rimon Hossain's starting place; the late loss to Yemen ends qualification hopes, though Fahmidul's debut and the win over Singapore end a 12-match goalless run.

incidents.title: Age fraud in the youth teams: Rimon, Miraj and the U-17s
incidents.summary: Age fraud allegations sweep the youth teams: 'baby Rimon' is accused of playing the national team at 15 and the Premier League at 13, Mirajul Islam is accused of age fraud and poor physicality, and 25-year-old Nazmul Huda Faisal is alleged to be playing in the U-17 team for a third time, with a long essay arguing Bangladeshi footballers vanish by 25/26 because of falsified ages; fans condemn the mentality that age fraud is fine if it wins cups, and U-17 coach Golam Rabbani Choton's disorganised football is slammed as Bangladesh lose the SAFF U-17 final to India.

incidents.title: U-20 women lose to South Korea in Asian Cup qualifying

entities.name: AFC U-20 Women's Asian Cup Qualifiers

incidents.summary: Bangladesh's U-20 women are outclassed by South Korea in the AFC U-20 Women's Asian Cup qualifiers, with fans unsurprised given Korea's skill and speed and a long tactical critique of coach Peter Butler's approach in the defeat.

incidents.title: Maruful Haque destroying young footballers at Abahani
incidents.summary: Abahani coach Maruful Haque is accused of destroying young footballers, turning top age-group talent into also-rans, as part of a wider charge that Bangladeshi clubs ruin their own youngsters.

incidents.title: Khyap money matches are ruining careers: the Jillur Rahman warning
incidents.summary: Fans forbid professional players from playing khyap (unsanctioned money) matches, citing Jillur Rahman as the real example of how harmful they are to a career. (Khyap money matches: fits no category, named here.)

incidents.title: BFL rebrand: renamed league, no logo or sponsor
incidents.summary: The domestic league is renamed the Bangladesh Football League, but the second round starts without a logo or sponsor and the new logo is mocked as the old one with AI swapping P for F, letters misaligned. (League rebrand shambles: fits no category, named here.)

incidents.title: Sohel Rana's childish behaviour criticised
incidents.summary: Senior footballer Sohel Rana's behaviour is criticised as childish and unbecoming of a senior player.

incidents.title: September Nepal friendlies: protests, diaspora dependence and the U-20s
incidents.summary: Bangladesh's September friendlies against Nepal go ahead amid deadly anti-government protests in Nepal that put the fixture in doubt; the win is then dismissed by fans because five U-20 SAFF players were fielded, with the match held up as proof Bangladesh football would be dead without diaspora and naturalised players.

incidents.title: Fahad Karim's BPL sponsor and OTT promises questioned
incidents.summary: BFF vice-president Fahad Karim's unfulfilled promises of BPL sponsors and OTT broadcasts are questioned, with fans asking whether he will keep his word.

incidents.title: Hong Kong at home: the 4-3 collapse, the syndicate XI and the Cabrera-out eruption
incidents.summary: Bangladesh lose 4-3 at home to Hong Kong in the Asian Cup qualifier and the group erupts: Cabrera's XI — eight Bashundhara Kings players, Saad Uddin at left-back ahead of Zayyan Ahmed, Fahmidul Islam, Shamit Shome and Jamal Bhuyan benched — is blamed for all four Hong Kong goals, with Saad mocked for the goal through his legs and his history of costly errors, Mitul Marma blamed in goal, and Hamza Choudhury sympathised with for carrying the team; the fallout runs for days with Cabrera-out protests, calls for street programmes, and claims Cabrera was appointed as Oscar Bruzon's puppet by Imrul Hasan and Salahuddin.

incidents.title: No development under Imrul Hasan's watch

entities.name: Bangladesh Football- Walking Around The Dreams

incidents.summary: October arrives with no trace of promised football development, and Imrul Hasan is mocked for keeping fans waiting on his pledges.

incidents.title: Diaspora scouting and paperwork failures
incidents.summary: A running indictment of BFF's diaspora handling: Cape Verde recruit Pico Lopes via LinkedIn and play 13 diaspora players while Bangladesh's paperwork for Trevor Islam, Zayyan Hakim, Ronan Sullivan, Niloy and others drags on for months; Afghanistan call up an 18-year-old Millwall defender while Bangladesh ignore Tasin Hossain trialling at Brentford, Amit Hossain's Fulham CV and Norway interest in Almas Ayman Samrat; Haiti take an amateur-league goalkeeper to the World Cup while BFF stall.

incidents.title: BFF removes Mohammedan Ultras banner targeting Imrul Hasan
incidents.summary: BFF is accused of having a Mohammedan Ultras banner targeting Imrul Hasan removed, with fans reading it as the federation suppressing criticism. (Federation suppressing criticism: kept in 'other' per the user's taxonomy call.)

incidents.title: Kuba, Tariq and the Kings contracts: trapped diaspora players
incidents.summary: The Kings diaspora thread turns into a contracts row: Tariq Kazi cancels his contract with Bashundhara Kings over a salary issue, Kuba Mitchell is said to have been trapped into signing by Imrul Hasan and gets only 13 minutes in his first match then the bench, Zayyan Ahmed signs for around 5 lakh a month, and fans say Kings did justice to none of the three diaspora players who came; a post notes forcing young players to stay at clubs against their wishes violates FIFA's Article 19.

incidents.title: Ticket black market and the boycott calls
incidents.summary: A ticket syndicate is alleged for the Hong Kong match, and for the India match 22,000 tickets are said to finish in two minutes before sales even start, with black-marketeers blamed and Fahad Karim called 'fraud Karim'; fans split between boycotting the Nepal and India matches until the syndicate breaks and arguing a boycott means surrender, while the Save Bangladesh Football gallery announces it will not attend any national team match.

incidents.title: U-17 women's Asian Cup qualifying struggles
incidents.summary: Bangladesh's U-17 women struggle in Asian Cup qualifying, with little hope for the campaign, ugly play under coach Saiful Bari Titu, and a must-win match against Chinese Taipei after Jordan's loss.

incidents.title: BPL matches not televised
incidents.summary: BFF's broadcast failures pile up: the country's only sports channel cannot even show its own match, BFF is hiring content creators who do not understand football, and fans trying to watch the top-tier league on Toffee find nothing.

incidents.title: BFF money: kit deals, Fahad Karim and match income questioned
incidents.summary: The money thread around BFF vice-president Fahad Karim: he is accused of losing Mizuno as kit sponsor through commission business, the Dour kit deal is said to give BFF nothing from jersey sales while Karim takes 30 lakh, Thailand's Warrix deal worth 2.7 million dollars a year is held up as contrast, BFF members are accused of enriching their own businesses through sponsorships and tickets, and fans question BFF's reported 3 crore 93 lakh taka income from three National Stadium matches and where friendly income went.

incidents.title: Hong Kong away: the 1-1 draw that ends the Asian Cup dream
incidents.summary: Bangladesh draw 1-1 away at Hong Kong's roofed Kai Tak Stadium in front of 50,000 fans — Tariq Kazi's slip gives away a penalty, Fahmidul Islam misses an easy chance in the 73rd minute, and Saad Uddin is in the XI again — and the result ends Asian Cup qualification, with fans calculating the home loss cost the group and demanding Cabrera and Hasan Al Mamun be sacked; the keeper debate rolls on as Shrabon is mocked as the poor man's Onana.

incidents.title: Morsalin's flag: the social-media storm over a foreign flag
incidents.summary: Sheikh Morsalin is criticised for putting another country's flag beside his photo on social media.

incidents.title: Zayyan Hakim's passport: fans must take responsibility
incidents.summary: Fans say they will have to take responsibility for getting Zayyan Hakim's passport themselves, asking BFF president Tabith Awal and the authorities to act, while Trevor Islam and Zayyan Hakim look unlikely to be ready before the India match and the 23-man squad debate centres on which passport-holding diaspora players can play.

incidents.title: Salahuddin's 15-year syndicate rule revisited
incidents.summary: After the Hong Kong failure, fans revisit Kazi Salahuddin's 15-year BFF rule as a syndicate mafia regime, recounting a 2018 Westin Hotel event to show how he used political connections, with Tofayel Ahmed, Sheikh Jamal and others named as part of the network.

incidents.title: Bashundhara Kings' Asian collapse: knocked out at the group stage again
incidents.summary: Bashundhara Kings are knocked out at the group stage in Asia for a fifth consecutive time — losing 0-3 to Al Ansar, setting a Bangladeshi record of six straight group-stage exits and losing all group matches in two straight Asian campaigns — with fans blaming the squad, the marking of Rimon Hossain and Taj Uddin, Sohel Rana's impact off the bench and goalkeeper Shrabon's own goal, and noting Kings lead Bangladeshi clubs with four FIFA transfer bans; Abahani's eight group-stage Asian exits are held up as the record being chased.

incidents.title: November window: Nepal draw, India win, Asian Cup elimination
incidents.summary: The November window: Bangladesh draw 2-2 with Nepal at home despite two Hamza Choudhury goals, with Saad Uddin's mistake conceding again and Topu Barman accused of repeatedly ignoring Zayyan Ahmed on the left, then beat India 1-0 — but the win brings no joy as Singapore's qualification confirms Bangladesh finish third and miss the Asian Cup, fans calculate nine points and top spot were possible with the right XI, and the Cabrera-out movement is called for while India debut watch centres on Ryan Williams' delayed NOC from Australia.

incidents.title: Women's team form and fitness slide
incidents.summary: The women's team slide after the Asian Cup qualification high: down 3-1 to Thailand at half-time with match fitness questioned, Masura Parvin notes the players' standard and fitness are falling while playing in the Bhutan league, and after a 1-0 loss to Malaysia coach Peter Butler takes responsibility while fans say syndicate media have ganged up against him for blocking their interests.

incidents.title: Youth development neglected: no academies, no grassroots, no future
incidents.summary: Fans contrast India's 142 recognised football academies and RFDL youth league with Bangladesh having only one BKSP in name, note BFF's development is zero under Tabith Awal with district leagues, the Bangamata tournament and academy activities all stopped, and point out India play regular international friendlies at U-17, U-20 and U-23 levels in FIFA windows while Bangladesh only nominate players; the U-17s' Asian Cup dream ends 4-0 to China in a system with no age-group structure.

incidents.title: Traditional clubs in decline: Mohammedan unpaid and groundless
incidents.summary: Mohammedan's decline is laid bare: players with no salary, coaches with no honorarium and no proper practice ground, while fans say traditional clubs like Abahani and Mohammedan finished the country's football.

incidents.title: Arham Islam: the Australia U-20 call-up and the one-switch rule
incidents.summary: The defining story of December: Arham Islam, the Bangladesh-born Western United teenager BFF overlooked and then dropped from a U-23 call-up Titu had announced on a Jamuna TV podcast, is called to Australia's U-20 preliminary and then final squad; fans explain FIFA's one-switch rule — Arham has already played for Bangladesh, so a single minute for Australia ends his Bangladesh career forever — his father confirms he will seek his future with Australia, Titu is accused of blocking him from the trial on age grounds, and by mid-December Arham has debuted for Australia's U-18s, prompting fans to ask whether BFF clearance was even needed and to appeal for him and Tasin Hossain to return.

incidents.title: Latin-Bangla Super Cup shambles
incidents.summary: The Latin-Bangla Super Cup draws ridicule: Brazil's seventh-tier Sao Bernardo and Argentina's Atletico Charlone are the foreign opposition, fans ask what the tournament actually is, the skill gap between local and diaspora players is exposed in the opening match, doubt arises over whether organisers can pay the foreign teams' return tickets, and the National Sports Council suspends the allocation over misconduct with journalists and irregularities.

incidents.title: Stadium disputes and renovation promises
incidents.summary: The National Stadium pitch is to be renovated after the tri-nation series and Latin-Bangla Super Cup, fans argue painting existing stadiums, maintaining the grass and adding adboards, roofs and floodlights could transform them but doubt it will ever happen, and cricketers in Sylhet protest the NSC giving Sylhet District Stadium to BFF.

incidents.title: Broadcast blackout: the league cannot be watched
incidents.summary: December's broadcast collapse: the Abahani-PWD match is mocked for overlapping ground markings and wonderful broadcasting, Mohammedan's match against Arambagh only starts broadcasting late, two BFL match days end with no match shown live, content creators at their own expense broadcast better quality than BFF, and fans say the syndicate wants spectators kept away to hide corruption — with the women's game getting the worst broadcast too.
